paras: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Hishaam reports that he once asked Ummul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "Tell me about the character of Rasulullaah ﷺ ." "Have you not read the Qur'aan?" she asked. "Of course, I have," he replied. Hadhrat Aa'isha (SSi then said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ's character was the Qur'aan (every noble character trait mentioned in the Qur'aan was to be found in the life of Rasulullaah ﷺ.
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal '"(Vol. 4 Pg.44).

paras: Another narration mentions that Hadhrat Qataadah (RA) said, "Indeed the Qur'aan brought every noble trait of good character."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Dalaa'il (Pg.57). Tirmidhi and Bayhaqi have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.42) as has Tabraani as quoted in Majma'm Zawaa'id (Vol.9 Pg.l 7). Ibn Abu Dawood in his Masaahif, Abu Ya'la, Rooyaani and ibn Asaakir have also reported a similar narration, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.S Pg.l 85). Ibn Sa'd (Vol. 1 Pg.90) has reported a similar narration as well.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) reports that when he asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) about the character of 'Rasulullaah ﷺ, "she replied, "His character was the Qur'aan. He was pleased with what Allaah is pleased and disliked what Allaah dislikes."

Another narration from Hadhrat Zaid bin Baabnoos states that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) gave a similar reply when they asked her about the character of Rasulullaah ﷺ, This narration however states that Hadhrat Aa'isha asked, "Have you read Surah Mu'minoon?" She then told them to read from the beginning of the Surah (from.) oy then ten verses thereafter. Thereafter she said, "Such was the character of Rasulullaah ﷺ ."

Hadhrat (RA) reports that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) stated, "There was none with better character than Rasulullaah ﷺ. Whenever any of his companions or family called for him, he always responded by saying, 'At your service." It was for this reason that Allaah revealed the verse: (i ij) ji (ji uilijjjf Verily, you Rasulullaah ﷺ are stationed) upon an exalted (flawless) character. (Surah Qalam, verse ' ' Hadhrat Qais bin Wahab reports from a man from the Banu Suraat tribe that he once asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "Tell me about the character of Rasulullaah Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) replied, "Have you not read in the Qur'aan where Allaah says:?" She then continued, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was once with his companions when I and Hafsah both prepared some food for him. When she beat me to sending the food, I sent my slave girl with instructions to overturn the platter. Consequently, when Hafsah was serving the food to Rasulullaah ﷺ, the slave girl overturned it and the food was all scattered about. Rasulullaah ﷺ gathered the food that had fallen on the ground and the Sahabah (RA) ate it. When I sent my platter, Rasulullaah ﷺ handed it over to Hafsah saying, 'Take this platter in place of yours and eat whatever is in it.' I did not notice even a hint of displeasure on the face of Rasulullaah.

Hadhrat Khaarijah bin Zaid narrates that a group of people once came to his father Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) with the request, "Tell us something about the character of Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) said, "I was Rasulullaah ﷺ's neighbour. When revelation would come to him, he would send for me and I would come to him to write it down. Whenever we spoke of worldly matters, he also spoke about it, whenever we spoke of the Aakhirah, he also spoke about it and whenever we spoke of food, he also spoke of the same (he was never aloof from us). I am narrating all this to you on behalf of Rasulullaah ﷺ -.■..'.-•.

Hadhrat Safiyya bint Huyay (RA) (Rasulullaah ﷺ's wife) says, "I have never seen anyone with better character than Rasulullaah ﷺ. I was riding on. the back of his camel with him as we returned from Khaybar. It was at night and as I began to fall asleep, my head hit the back of the carriage. Rasulullaah iiif touched me gently as he said, 'Take it easy, dear lady-Take it easy, O daughter of Huyay (this is not the place to sleep).1 When we cached a place called Sahbaa, he said to me, (t) Abu Nu'aym in his Dalaa'il (Pg.57).
'Do excuse me for what I had to do with your people Jews of Khaybar).' He then explained to me what they had said done) to him (because of which he was forced to act against them)."
sources: Bazzaar and Tabraani, reporting from reliable as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.15).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was one of the most compassionate people. I swear by Allaah that he never refused even a slave or a child who brought water to him on a freezing morning wash with, it and then give it back to them for blessings). the intense cold) He would wash his face and arms with the water. Whenever anyone came to him with a request, he would listen attentively to the person and not move away until the person moved away. Whenever anyone took him by the hand, he would give his hand and not pull it away until the person himself let go."
sources: Ahmad and lbn Maajah.

paras: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) says, "After Rasulullaah ﷺ performed the Fajr salaah, the slaves of Madinah would come to him with their utensils of water. Rasulullaah ﷺ would then dip his hands into every utensil brought that the people may have the blessings of his blessed limbs). At times, people would come to him on an extremely cold morning, but he would still dip his hands into the water."
sources: Ahmad and Bukhaari in his Adab, as quoted in Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.49).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) also reports, "Whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ shook hands with anyone or whenever anyone shook his hands, he would never pull his hand away until the person pulled his own hand away first. He would also not turn away from a person he was facing speaking) until the person himself turned away first. He was also never to be seen stretching out his feet towards a person sitting before him."

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates, "I have never seen Rasulullaah ﷺ move his head away from anyone whispering into his ear until the person himself moved away. I have also never seen Rasulullaah ﷺ pull his hand away from anyone holding his hand until the person himself let go of Rasulullaah ﷺ's hand."

Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah SSi says, "Whenever anyone took Rasulullaah ﷺ 's hand shake it), he never pulled it away until the person himself let go. Rasulullaah ﷺ 's feet were also never to be seen stretched out towards a person sitting in front of him. When someone shook his hand, Rasulullaah ﷺ always turned his full attention towards the person and would not turn away until the person had finished what he had to say." ( ' )

Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Even if it were a child from amongst the common children of Madinah who took Rasulullaah ﷺ by the hand, he would not pull his hand away from hers so that she could take him wherever she wanted to."
sources: Muslim. (Vol.2 Pg.256). Abu Nu'aym has also reported the narration in his Dalaa'il (Pg.57).

paras: Another narration states that even the slaves girls of Madinah could take Rasulullaah ﷺ by the hand and take him wherever she needed him to go."
sources: Tabraani, Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.17) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a lady who was mentally deranged once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ ! I need you to do something for me." Addressing her by her title, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Choose any of the streets (to explain it to me) so that I may address your problem (Rasulullaah ﷺ chose to speak to her privately in a place where people could see them so that no suspicions would be aroused). Rasulullaah gflf then stepped aside with her in one of the streets where she explained her problem to him."
sources: Maalik, Abu Dawood, Nasa'ee and Ahmad, as quoted in Kanzul Pg.47). Abu Nu'aym has also reported the narration in his Dalaa'il (Pg.57).

paras: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslamah (RA) says, "When I once returned from a journey, Rasulullaah ﷺ took me by the hand and did not leave if until I let go of his hand."
sources: Ahmad, as quoted in A! Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.36). Muslim (Vol.2 Pg.256), Abu Nu'aym in his Dalaa'il, Abdur Razzaaq, Abd bin Humayd and Haakim have also reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.47).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ was faced with two options, he always chose the easier of the two (so that it would be easy for the Ummah to emulate) on condition that it did not entail sin. If it entailed sin, he was then the most abstinent of people. He also never took revenge for personal reasons. He had people punished only when anything forbidden by Allaah was violated, in which case he had the punishment meted for the sake of Allaah."

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ never hit any servant or woman. In fact, he never hit anything unless he was fighting in Jihaad in the path of Allaah. Whenever faced with two options, he always chose the easier of the two on condition that it did not entail sin. If it entailed sin, he was then the most abstinent of people. He also never took revenge for anything done against him. He had people punished only when anything forbidden by Allaah was violated, in which case he had the punishment meted for the sake of Allaah Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "I never saw Rasulullaah ﷺ take revenge for any injustice done to himself. He had people punished only when anything forbidden by Allaah was violated, in which case he was amongst the most infuriated of people. Whenever faced with two options, he always chose the easier of the two on condition that it did not entail sin."

Hadhrat Abu Abdullaah Jadali says that when Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) was questioned about the character of Rasulullaah ﷺ, he heard her reply, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was never rude and vulgar and never even pretended to be so. He was never noisy in the marketplaces and never fought evil with evil. In fact, he always forgave and overlooked." (25 Hadhrat Saalih narrates that when describing Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah said, "When he turned towards someone, he turned completely and when he turned away from someone, he also turned completely. May my parents be sacrificed for him! Rasulullaah ﷺ was never rude and vulgar and never even pretended to be so. He was never noisy in the marketplaces." Another narration states that Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) added, "Never have I seen any like him before and never after."
sources: Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il (Pg.25) as well as Abu Ya'la and Haakim, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (VoL Pg.47).

paras: Hadhrat- Anas says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was never vulgar, never cursed people and never rude. The most he would tell someone when scolding him was, "What is the matter with him? May sand fall on his forehead!"
sources: Abu Dawood Tayaalisi and Tirmidhi, as quoted in wan Nihaayah (Vol. 6 Pg.36). lbn Sa'd (Vol.1 Pg.90), Ahmad and Haakim have also reported the narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.47).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was never rude and vulgar and never even pretended to be so. He always said, 'The best of you is the one with the best character.'"

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived in Madinah, Abu Talha led me by my hand to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, 'O Rasulullaah iffi?! Anas is an intelligent lad. Do let him serve you.' I therefore remained Rasulullaah ﷺ's servant at home and on journey. I swear by Allaah that for anything I did, he never said, "Why did you do that in that way?' and when I failed to do something, he never once asked, 'Why did you not do that like this?'" in another narration, Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ had the very best of character. He once sent me to do something one day to which I blurted, 'By Allaah! I shall never do it!' In my heart however,.! had resolved that I would definitely carry out his instructions. After leaving, I passed by some children playing in the marketplace. (As I stood there watching them) Rasulullaah suddenly grabbed hold of my neck from behind. As I looked at him, he was laughing as he said, 'Dear little Anas! Have you been to where I sent you?1 "Yes,' I replied, 'I am presently on my way there, 0 Rasulullaah im."' Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports further. He says, "By Allaah! Although 1 was in Rasulullaah ﷺ's service for nine years, he never said to anything I did, "Why did you do that?' and when I failed to do something, he never once asked, 'Why did you not do that?'"

Another narration states that Hadhrat Anas (RA) said, "I served Rasulullaah Sli for ten years. I swear by Allaah that he never once told me 'Oof!' (synonymous to "Oh no!" or any other expression of displeasure). Not once did he ever ask me, "Why did you do that?' or "Why did you not do that?
sources: Ya'qoob bin Sufyaan.
Abu Nu'aym in his Hifya (Vol.1 Pg.56).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) also narrates, "Although I served Rasulullaah ﷺ for ten years, he never once scolded me for something that I had delayed in carrying out or that 1 had bungled. Even when any member of his household scolded me, he would tell them, 'Leave him alone. When something had been destined to happen, it will happen.
sources: Tabraani, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.2 Pg.253).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Although I served Rasulullaah ﷺ for ten years, not once did he ever swear at me, hit me, scold me or even frown at me. He never once scolded me for something that 1 had delayed in carrying out or that I had bungled and when any member of his household scolded me, he would tell them, 'Leave him alone. When something had been destined to happen, it will happen.'"

Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived In Madinah, I was a boy of eight. My mother took me to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, 'O Rasulullaah Except for me, all the men and women of the Ansaar have given you a gift. I have nothing to offer you as a gift save for this son of mine. Please accept him from me to serve you as you see fit.' I then served Rasulullaah ﷺ for ten years, during which time he never once hit me, never insulted me and never even frowned at me,"
sources: Ya'qoob bin Sufyaan, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.2 Pg.253). Haakim (Vol.2 Pg.266) has reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "There are three men from the Quraysh who are the most handsome, have the best character and have the most resolute sense of modesty, when they speak to you, they can never be lying and when you speak to them, they will never regard you as a liar. They are Abu Bakr Siddeeq, Uthmaan bin Affaan and Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said, "There are three men from the Quraysh who are the most handsome, have the best character and have the strongest sense of modesty. They are Abu Bakr, Uthmaan and Abu Ubaydah.
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.81).

paras: Hadhrat Hasan reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "If I chose to do so, I could take each of my companions to task for aspects of their character except for Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah.
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.81) has commented on the chain of narrators. Haakim and Ibn Asaakir have reported similar narrations, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal Pg.4).

paras: Hadhrat (RA) bin Uthmaan Qurashi (RA) that Rasulullaah ﷺ once visited his daughter as she was washing the head of (her husband) Hadhrat Uthmaan SSi Addressing her, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Beloved daughter! Treat Abu Abdullaah (Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA)) well because from all my companions, his character is closest to my own."
sources: Ahmad, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.272).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that he once happened to go to Hadhrat Ruqayya who was the daughter of Rasulullaah iilf and the wife of Hadhrat uthmaan (RA). .She had a comb in her hand and she said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ just left me after I had combed his hair. 'How do you find Abu Abdullaah (Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) he asked. When I replied that he was an excellent person, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Look after him well because from all my companions, his character is closest to my own.
Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) who was the son of Rasulullaah fill's freed slave Aslam reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to Hadhrat Ja'far (RA), "You resemble me both in looks and in personality."

Hadhrat Ali (RA) narrates, "ja'far (RA), Zaid and I once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ said to Zaid, 'You are our brother and friend,' Zaid with joy. Rasulullaah iii then said to Ja'far, 'You resemble me both in looks and in personality". Ja'far then skipped about even more than Zaid. Thereafter, Rasulullaah ﷺ said to me, 'You are from me and I from you.' I therefore skipped about more than Zaid and ja'far SSHfflfiS.-W Hadhrat usaamah bin Zaid (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to Hadhrat Ja'far (RA), "Your personality is like mine and your physical appearance also resembles my own. You are therefore from me. And you, O Ali. You are also from me and the father of my grandsons." ® Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) the son of Hadhrat Ja'far (RA) said, "I heard from such words that I would not trade even for red camels. I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Ja'far most resembles my looks and my personality. As for you, O Abdullaah! From all of Allaah's creation, you most resemble your father (Ja'far.
sources: Bukhaari, lbn Mundhir, ibn Abi Haatim, lbn Mardway and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.416). (2)lbnsa'd.

paras: Hadhrat Bahriyyah reports, "When my uncle Khidaash saw Rasulullaah eating from a particular plate, he asked Rasulullaah ﷺ to give it to him. The plate then remained with us afterwards. Whenever Hadhrat umar (RA) used to ask for it to be taken out, we would fill it with Zamzam water and give it to him. He would then drink from it and pour it over his head and face. However, it once occurred that a thief did us a grave injustice when he stole the plate along with other possessions of ours. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then came to us one day after the theft and asked us to take the plate out. 'O Ameerul Mu'mineenT' we submitted, 'It was stolen along with some other goods of ours.' Hadhrat Umar Wa exclaimed, 'A pretty clever thief to steal Rasulullaah ﷺ's plate!' By Allaah! Hadhrat Umar (RA) neither swore the thief nor cursed him."
sources: Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.413).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Uyaynah bin Hisn Hudhayfah) bin Badr arrived (in Madinah), he stayed with his nephew Hadhrat Hurr bin Qais (RA) who happened to be amongst those that Hadhrat Umar (RA) kept close to him. It was only the learned ones whom Hadhrat Umar (RA) kept in his company and with whom he consulted, regardless of whether they were young or old. Hadhrat Uyaynah (RA) said to his nephew, "Dear nephew! Since you have some status in the eyes of the Ameer, please secure permission for me to see him." When Hadhrat umar (RA) granted permission, Hadhrat Uyaynah (RA) called out, "Hey son of Khattaab! By Allaah! Neither do you give us much nor do you rule us with justice!" This outburst made Hadhrat Umar (RA) so angry that he was close to assaulting Hadhrat Uyaynah Hadhrat Hurr (RA) then intervened saying, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Allaah had mentioned to His Nabi ﷺ

Adopt forgiveness, instruct (others to do) what is right and ignore the ignorant ones (because it is futile to argue with them), (Surah A'raaf, verse 199) This man is certainly from amongst the ignorant ones."

The narrator says, "By Allaah! When this verse was recited to him, Hadhrat Umar did not do a thing. It was his noble trait to immediately forsake anything for the instruction of the Qur'aan." W Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "I have never seen a time when Hadhrat Umar (RA) became angry and was not dissuaded from taking action (against the perpetrator) by the mention of Allaah, mention of fear for Allaah or by someone reciting a verse of the Qur'aan to him."

Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) once asked Hadhrat Aslam, "How do you find Hadhrat Umar Hadhrat Aslam replied, "He is an excellent man. However, matters are grave when he becomes angry." Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) advised him saying, "If you are with him at a time when he becomes angry, just recite the Qur'aan until his anger vanishes."

Hadhrat Maalik Daar (one of Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s slaves) says, "Hadhrat Umar once shouted at me and was about to strike me with his whip when I said, '1 urge you to remember Allaah!' He immediately threw down his whip saying, have reminded me of a Great Being."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.82).

paras: Hadhrat Aamir bin Rabee'ah (RA) says, "Hadhrat Mus'ab bin Umayr (RA) was a friend of mine from the time he accepted Islaam up to the time that he was martyred at Uhud. May Allaah shower His mercy on him. He accompanied us on both migrations to Abyssinia and was my travelling companion. I must say that I have never seen a person with better character than him nor one who had fewer differences with people than he."

Hadhrat Habba bin Juwayn reports that they were once with Hadhrat Ali (RA) when they started to mention some of the statements of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood. Praising him, someone said (to Hadhrat Ali (RA)), "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! We have never seen a man with better character, nor anyone who teaches as compassionately, nor anyone who is better company nor anyone more pious than Abdullaah bin Mas'ood Hadhrat Ali (RA) asked, "I ask you to say in the name of Allaah whether this is the truth in your hearts." When they expressed that it was, Hadhrat Ali (RA) remarked, "O Allaah! I make You the Witness that my opinion of him (Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA)) is as these people have expressed or even better," Another narration states that in praise for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA), the person even added, "He reads the Qur'aan, regarding what it makes lawful as lawful and what it forbids as forbidden. He has a deep understanding of the Deen and has immense knowledge of the Sunrtah." (,)

Hadhrat Saalim says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) never cursed a single slave save for one whom he then set free (as compensation)," Hadhrat Zuhri says that as he was about to curse a slave, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said, "O Allaah! May Your cur..." He then did not complete the word (curse) and said, "That is a word that I hate to mention." The narration has already passed in the chapter entitled "The fervour that Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) had to Spend in the Path of Allaah"(3), in which Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "Mu'aadh bin Jabal was amongst the most handsome of people, amongst those with the best character and the most open-handed."
sources: Bukhaart.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood SI reports, "After the Battle of Hunayn Rasulullaah ﷺ gave extra (booty) to some people. He gave Aqra bin Haabis and Uyaynah bin Hisn a hundred camels each and gave a lot to certain other people as well. Someone remarked, 'Allaah's pleasure was certainly not intended in this distribution.' I said, 'I am definitely going to report this to Rasulullaah ﷺ When I reported it to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he said., 'May Allaah shower His mercy on Moosa. Greater abuse than this was hurled at him but he exercised patience.'"

Another narration states: "Someone said, 'By Allaah! There is no justice in this distribution and Allaah's pleasure was certainly not intended.' I said, 'I am definitely going to report this to Rasulullaah ﷺ When I reported it to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he said, 'Who will exercise justice when Allaah and Rasool H do not? May Allaah shower His mercy on Moosa. Greater abuse than this was hurled at him but he exercised patience."
sources: Bukhaari and Muslim, as quoted wan Nihaayah (Vol.4 Pg.362).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) narrates that when they were with Rasulullaah ﷺ while he was distribution the spoils of war, Dhu Khuwaysarah who belonged to the Banu Tameem tribe came to him. Dhu Khuwaysarah said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Be just!" Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Shame on you! Who will be just if I am not? May I be a failure and at a loss (if 1 do not exercise justice)! Who can possibly be just if I am not?" Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) then asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Permit me to behead him!" "Leave him," Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "because he has some friends before whose salaah you would look down on your own salaah and before whose fasts you would look down on your own fasts. Although they recite the Qur'aan, it does not pass even their collarbones. They pass through islaam just as an arrow passes through prey and you find no trace of it on the arrow's head when you examine it closely. Even when you examine the thread (that fixes the head to the shaft), you find no trace (of the prey). Similarly, you find no trace of it even after examining the shaft and the feathers of the arrow although the arrow passed through the gut and blood of the prey. The outstanding feature of these people will be a dark-skinned man whose one arm will be hanging loose and will appear like a woman's breast or like a loose piece of flesh. They will make their appearance at a time when there will be disunity amongst the people,"

Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) says further, "1 testify that I had certainly heard these words from Rasulullaah ﷺ and 1 also testify that I was with bin Abi Taalib when he fought against these people. Upon the instruction of Ali, a search was carried out for this man. When he was brought, I saw him to be exactly as Rasulullaah ﷺ had described him."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says that when Abdullaah bin Ubay died, his son approached Rasulullaah ﷺ with the request, "Give me your upper garment so that I may shroud my father in it. I also want you to lead the funeral prayer (Janaazah salaah) for my father and to seek Allaah's forgiveness for him." Rasulullaah ﷺ gave him the garment and told him, "Let me know when I should lead the prayer." When the son called for Rasulullaah ﷺ and he was abouttogo, pulled Rasulullaah ﷺ back saying, "Did Allaah not forbid you from praying for the Munaaflqeen?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "I have two choices because Allaah says: 'Seek forgiveness for them (the Munaafiqeen) or do not seek forgiveness for them.'" (Surah Taubah, verse 80) Rasulullaah ﷺ then proceeded to lead the salaah, after which Allaah revealed the verse: Do not ever perform (the funeral) salaah for any of them who die, (Surah Taubah, verse 84)
sources: Bukhaari and Muslim.

paras: Hadhrat umar (RA) says, "When Abdullaah bin Ubay died, Rasulullaah ﷺ was called for the Jahaazah salaah and he proceeded. When Rasulullaah ﷺ stood before the corpse with the intention of leading the salaah, I turned around and stood in front of him saying, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ Will you perform the salaah for the enemy of Allaah, Abdullaah bin Ubay, the one who made all those (blasphemous) statements?' I then went on to recount the things he had said. Rasulullaah ﷺ continued smiling and it was only when I had gone too far that he said, 'Do move away from me, O Umar because I have been given a choice and have made mine. I have been told: ^ Oj 70 Muhammad ﷺ Seek forgiveness for them Munaafiqeen) or do not seek forgiveness for them. Even if you seek forgiveness for them seventy times, Allaah will never forgive them. This is because they disbelieved in Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ. Allaah does not guide the disobedient ones (because they have no desire to be guided).'
Taubah, verse 80)

If 1 knew that he would be forgiven if 1 sought forgiveness for him more than seventy times, I would certainly exceed seventy.' Rasulullaah ﷺ then proceeded to lead the salaah and stood by the grave until the funeral was over. I was greatly perplexed by my audaciousness before Rasulullaah ﷺ for Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ know best (what is right and what not). By Allaah! it was hardly much longer afterwards that Allaah revealed the following two verses: lit A I.' > i'. ffi ,"< ' fi » ''. X" ", '* (Ao) ^ Do not ever perform (the funeral) salaah for any of them who die and do not stand over their graves (to bury them or to visit their graves), Undoubtedly they disbelieved in Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ and died as disobedient people (as Kuffaar). Their wealth and their children should not impress you. Allaah intends to punish them with these in this worldly life and (Allaah intends) that their souls depart (from this world) while they are Kaafiroon. (Surah Taubah, verses 84,85)
After this and up to the day he passed away, Rasulullaah ﷺ never led the Janaazah salaah of any Munaafiq and never stood by any of their graves."
sources: Ahmad, Tirmidhi and Bukhaari.

paras: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that when Abdullaah bin Ubay died, his son came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ If you do not attend my father's funeral, people will always be insulting us." When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived (at the funeral), he found that the body had already been placed into the grave.

Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Why did you not call me before you lowered him in the grave?" The body was then taken out and Rasulullaah ﷺ blew on it from head to foot and also shrouded it with his own garment (primarily because Abdullaah bin ubay gave his garment to Rasulullaah fill's uncle Abbaas after the Battle of Badr).
sources: Ahmad and Nasa'ee.

paras: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ came to (the funeral) Abdullaah bin Ubay after he had been lowered into his grave. By the command of Rasulullaah ﷺ, the body was then taken out and placing the body on his knees, Rasulullaah ﷺ blew on the body and shrouded it with his own garment.
sources: Bukhaari, as quoted in the Tafseerof Ibn Katheer (Vol.2 Pg.3?8).

paras: Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) says that because a Jew had cast a spell over Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah ﷺ was ill for several days. Hadhrat Jibra'eel then came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "One of the Jews has cast a spell over you. He has tied a few knots and placed them in a certain well. Send someone to fetch it." Rasulullaah ﷺ sent Hadhrat (RA), who removed it from the well and brought it to Rasulullaah iffi?. When Rasulullaah ﷺ untied the knots, it appeared as if he had been freed from bondage, until his death, Rasulullaah ﷺ never even mentioned this to the Jew and no anger could even be noticed on Rasulullaah ﷺ's face.
sources: Ahmad and Nasa'ee.

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates thataspellwascast on Rasulullaah ﷺ because of which he would think that he had been to his wives when in reality he had not. One of the narrators called Sufyaan says that this is the worst effect of witchcraft. Rasulullaah ﷺ one day said to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "O Aa'isha! Allaah has given a reply to the question I posed to Him. Two (angels in the form of) men came to me. The one sat by my head and the other by my feet. The one by my head asked, "What is the matter with this person?' 'He has been affected by witchcraft,' replied the other, 'Who is responsible for the witchcraft?' the first one asked further. 'Labeed bin A'sam,' came the reply. Labeed was a hypocrite belonging to the Banu Zurayq tribe and was an ally to the Jews. The angel enquired further, 'Upon what did he carry it out?' 'Upon a comb and the hairs it had removed,' the other replied. "Where is it now?' was the next question. The reply was, 'In the male spathe of a palm beneath a rock in the Dharwaan well.'" Rasulullaah ﷺ then went to the well and had the thing removed. Rasulullaah also said, "This was the very well I was shown with water appearing like that used to wash a henna-filled container and the palms of which appeared to be the heads of the Shayaateen." Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) asked, "Why did you not publicise the event?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Allaah had cured me from it and I do not wish to start a scandal against someone,"
sources: Bukhaari.

paras: Another narration adds that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "It was for six months that Rasulullaah ﷺ would think that he had been to his wives when in reality he had not. Two angels then came to him..." The rest of the Hadith continues (like the one above).
sources: Muslim and Ahmad, as quoted in the Tafseerof ibn Katheer (Vol.4 Pg.574).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a Jewish woman once gave Rasulullaah ﷺ a poisoned goat meat, which he ate from. When the woman was later bi ought before Rasulullaah ﷺ (when he discovered what she had done), he questioned her about it, "1 wanted to kill you," she admitted. Rasulullaah ﷺ responded by saying, "Allaah would never give the power to kill me." "Are you not going to have her executed?" the Sahabah (RA) asked. "No," replied Rasulullaah ﷺ. Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "I could always notice the effect of the poison on Rasulullaah ﷺ's uvula."
sources: Bukhaari and Muslim.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that a Jewish woman once presented some goat meat to Rasulullaah ﷺ which was poisoned. "Hang on," Rasulullaah cautioned the Sahabah (RA), "this is poisoned." Rasulullaah ﷺ then questioned the woman, "What made you do this?" Her response was, "I wanted to know that if you really are a Rasul, Allaah would inform you about it and if you are not, people could be rid of you." Rasulullaah ﷺ did not take any action against her.
sources: Bayhaqi, Abu Dawood, Ahmad and Bukhaari.

paras: Another narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) adds that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ felt the effect of the poison, he would have his blood cupped. In fact, when he was on a journey and about to enter the state of Ihraam on one occasion, he sensed its effect and had cupping done.
sources: Ahmad.

paras: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that a Jewish woman from Khaybar once poisoned some ruasted goat meat and presented it to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah took a foreleg of the goat and started eating it while a group of Sahabah (RA) also joined him, Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "Take your hands off (the food)!" Rasulullaah ﷺ then sent for the woman and when she arrived, her asked, "Did you poison this meat?" "Who told you about it?" she asked. Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "This (foreleg) here in my hand informed me." When she admitted that she did poison the meat, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked her why she did it. She replied, "I said to myself that it would do you no harm if you really are a Rasul and if you are not, we would be rid of you." Rasulullaah ﷺ forgave her and did not punish her.

However, some of the Sahabah (RA) who had eaten from the meat passed away and because he had also eaten from it, Rasulullaah ﷺ had blood cupped from his shoulder. Hadhrat Abu Hind (RA) who was a freed slave of the Ansaar Banu Bayaadha tribe did the cupping using a horn and a blade. Another narration from Hadhrat Abu Salamah (RA) states that Hadhrat Bishr bin Baraa bin Ma'roor passed away (from the poisoning). The narration further states thaf (because of this death) Rasulullaah ﷺ then had the woman executed.
sources: lbn Is'haaq, as quoted in wan Nihaayah n/ol.4 Pg,208).

paras: Hadhrat Marwaan bin Uthmaan bin Abu Sa'eed bin Mu'allaa narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ was on his deathbed, the sister of Hadhrat Bishr bin Baraa bin Ma'roor came to visit him. Rasulullaah ﷺ said to her, "O Ummu Bishr! I can now feel my arteries shredding because of what I ate with your brother in Khaybar." (Because of this) Muslims believe that together with the mantle of Nabuwaat, Allaah also blessed Rasulullaah ﷺ with the mantle of martyrdom.
sources: Ahmad and Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Khafaaji (Vol.2 Pg.25).

paras: Hadhrat Ja'da bin Khaalid bin Simmah Jushami narrates that Rasulullaah once saw a man with a large belly and pointed towards the man's belly. Hadhrat Ja'da (RA) then heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "It would have been better for you if that had been somewhere else (if you had spent on those without food rather than gorging yourself)," Thereafter, a man was brought and Rasulullaah was informed that the man had intended to assassinate Rasulullaah ﷺ . "There is nothing to be feared," Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Had you tried it, Allaah would have never given you power over me."

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that during the time when the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was being concluded, eighty armed men from Makkah approached from Mount Tan'eem with the express purpose of ambushing Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA). However, they were captured when Rasulullaah ﷺ made a du'aa to Allaah. Rasulullaah ﷺ then forgave them, after which Allaah revealed the verse: It is Allaah Who restrained their hands from (fighting) you and your hands from (Fighting) them right in Makkah Hudaybiyyah) after granting you dominance over them. Allaah is always Watchful over what you do. (Surah Fatah, verse 24) In a lengthy narration, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mughaffal (RA) says, "As we remained there, thirty armed men left (Makkah) and attacked us by surprise.

Rasulullaah ﷺ however, prayed to Allaah and Allaah made them all deaf. (As they stood dumbstruck) We then got up and captured them. Rasulullaah ﷺ then asked them, "Have you men come under the protection of any treaty or has anyone granted you any amnesty?" When they replied in the negative, Rasulullaah ﷺ let them go. It was then that Allaah revealed the verse: It is Allaah Who restrained their hands from (lighting) you and your hands from (fighting) them right in Makkah (at Hudaybiyyah) after granting you dominance over them. Allaah is always Watchful over what you do. (Surah Fatah, verse 24)
sources: Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawood, Tirmidhi and Nasa'ee.
Ahmad and Nasa'ee., as quoted in the Tafseerof Ibn Katheer (Vol.4 Pg.192).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Hadhrat Tufayl bin Amr (RA) of the Daus tribe once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "The Daus tribe are disobedient and refuse to accept (Islaam). Please curse them." Rasulullaah ﷺ then turned to face the Qibla and raised his hands (to pray), to which the Sahabah (RA) remarked, "Those people will certainly be destroyed." Rasulullaah ﷺ then prayed, "O Allaah! Guide the Daus tribe and bring them (to us as Muslims). O Allaah! Guide the Daus tribe and bring them. O Allaah! Guide the Daus tribe and bring them."
sources: Bukhaari and Muslim.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Za'raa (RA) reports that Hadhrat Ali bin Abu Taalib (RA) used to say, "My pure wives, pious progeny and myself have been the most tolerant people in youth and the most learned as adults. It is us that Allaah uses to eradicate dishonesty, to shatter the teeth of rabid dogs, to deliver you from your tyrants, to remove the shackles from your necks, to start off things and to terminate them." C The narration has already passed in which Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas said, "I have not seen any person as quick-witted, as intelligent, as knowledgeable and as tolerant as Abdullaah bin Abbaas.
sources: Abdul Ghani bin Sa'eed in his Idaahul Askaal, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.50).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "I sometimes commence the salaah with the intention of lengthening it when I hear the cries of a child and then shorten the salaah because I know that the crying would pain the mother."
sources: In the chapter entitled " Hadhrat Umar Sffiffig Consults with Men of knowledge" and under the subheading "Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) Consult with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) and the Good Comments that Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) made about him".

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that a man once asked Rasulullaah ﷺ, "where is my father (who died as a Mushrik)?" "In the fire (of Jahannam)," came the reply. When Rasulullaah ﷺ saw the grief on the man's face, he consoled him by saying, "Both my father as well as yours are in the fire."
sources: Bukhaari and Muslim, as quoted in Safwatus Safwa (Pg.66).
Allaah knows best the condition of Rasulullaah ﷺ parents in the Aakhirah because certain narrations suggest that Allaah accepted Rasulullaah ﷺ's intercession on their behalf.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that a Bedouin once came to Rasulullaah to seek assistance in paying some blood money. After giving him a handsome sum, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked "Have I done you justice?" "Not at all," the man replied, "You have not done me any good." This angered some Muslims so much tnat they wanted to get up and hit the man. Rasulullaah ﷺ however motioned to them to restrain themselves. When Rasulullaah ﷺ later stood up and went to his room, he called the Bedouin to his room saying, "You came to us asking for something and we gave it to you. You then made the remark that you did." Rasulullaah ﷺ then gave him some more and asked, "Have I done you justice?" This time the Bedouin said, "You have indeed. May Allah reward you amply on behalf of all my family and relatives." Rasulullaah ﷺ then said to him, "You came to us asking for something and we gave it to you. You then made the remark that you did, thus causing hurt to the hearts of my companions. Now when you leave, tell them what you have just said before me so that the hurt may leave their hearts." The man agreed and when he again arrived (in the gathering), Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Your friend here came to us asking for something and we gave it to him. He then made the remark that he did. We then called for him and again gave him something. He now believes that he is satisfied. Is that not true, dear Bedouin?" the Bedouin replied, "It certainly is. May Allah reward you amply on behalf of all my family and relatives." Thereafter, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Indeed the example of this Bedouin and myself is like a person who had a camel. When the camel bolted from him and the people ran after it, all that they achieved was to make it run further away. The owner of the camel then said, "Leave me to my camel because I am more compassionate towards it and know it better. He then headed for the camel taking along with him some dates that had fallen to the ground. He then called for the camel and it responded and came to him. He then comfortably tied his carriage to it. Had I done as you wanted when he made the remark he did, he would certainly have been doomed for Jahannam."
sources: Bazzaar. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.17) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Asma'ee reports that (when Hadhrat Umar (RA) became the Ameerul Mu'mineen) the people requested Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) to speak to Hadhrat Umar SSI to be gentle with the people because even young damsels in their secluded quarters were overawed by him. When Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf had spoken to Hadhrat Umar (RA), the Ameerul Mu'mineen said, "That is the only way I see appropriate to treat the people. By Allaah! If the people knew the gentleness, the mercy and the compassion I have for them, they would actually take the clothes off my back."
sources: Ahmad. Nasa'ee in his "Yowm wal Layl" and Abu Dawood have also reported the narration.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was more modest than a virgin in her own secluded quarters." Another narration adds that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ disliked something, it would be noticed on his face.
sources: Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il (Pg.26).

paras: Hadhrat Anas Hajggi reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Modesty is goodness through and through." Rasulullaah ﷺ Dislikes Telling People what would Displease them Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once displeased when he saw some Sufrah (a fragrance usually worn by women that stains the clothing yellow) on a person. After the person had left, Rasulullaah ﷺ said (to the other Sahabah (RA), "Why do you people not instruct him to wash the Sufrah off?" Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "It was never the habit of Rasulullaah ﷺ to tell a person on his face something that would displease him."

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Whenever the news reached Rasulullaah ﷺ that someone had said something, he would never say, "What is the matter with that person to say...?' He would rathersay,"Whatisthematterwithsome people who say...?'
Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "I have never seen the private parts of Rasulullaah iii." The Modesty of the Sahabah (RA).

Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Al Aas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ's wife Hadhrat Aa'isha and Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) both reported to him that Hadhrat Abu Bakr once sought permission to see Rasulullaah ﷺ who was lying down on his bed wearing a shawl belonging to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA). Remaining as he was, Rasulullaah ﷺ permitted Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) in and he left after completing the work he had with Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah was still in the same condition when Hadhrat Umar (RA) then asked permission to enter. Rasulullaah ﷺ allowed him in and after completing his work with Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Umar (RA) also left. However, when Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) sought permission to enter, Rasulullaah ﷺ sat up and urgently asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) to ensure that her clothes were covering her properly. After Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) had completed the work he had with Rasulullaah ﷺ, he then also left.

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) then asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Why is it that you became more anxious at the arrival of Uthmaan than you did at the arrival of both Abu Bakr and Umar Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Uthmaan is extremely bashful and I feared that if I let him under the condition that prevailed, he would have been unable to fulfil the need he had come for." Many narrators reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ also said to Hadhrat Aa'isha, "Why should I not be shy in front of that person in front of whom even the angels are shy?"
sources: Ahmad, Muslim and Abu Ya'la. Ahmad and Hasan bin Urfa have reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Hafsah (RA).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once sitting with Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) behind him when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) sought permission to enter and then entered (after permission was granted). Thereafter, Hadhrat Umar (RA) permission to enter and he also entered. Next came Hadhrat Sa'd bin Maalik (RA) who entered after seeking permission to do so. Rasulullaah ﷺ was busy talking to the others with his knees exposed when Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Maan (RA) sought permission to enter. Rasulullaah ﷺ then immediately covered his knees and told Hadhrat Aa'isha to move away. After speaking for some time, the men left. Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) then asked, "O Nabi of Allaah when my father and hio companions entered, you did not place your clothes over your knees neither did you ask me to move away from you (why did you do so when Hadhrat Uthmaan came in?)."

Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "why should I not be shy in front of that person in front of whom even the angels are shy? I swear by the Being Who controls my life that the angels ar„ shy for Uthmaan bin Affaan just as you are shy before Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ . Had he entered when you were close to me, he would neither speak nor raise his head until he left."
sources: Tabraani, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.7 Pg.203,204), Abu Ya'la has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.9 Pg.82). Tabraani and Abu Ya'la have also reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Hafsah (RA), as quoted by Haythami (Vol. 9 Pg.82).

paras: Abu Bakr Speaking about the extreme modesty of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), Hadhrat Hasan says, "Even though he was In a room behind a locked door, he would not remove his clothing to pour water over himself (when taking a bath). His modesty would prevent him from standing straight up (when bathing. He would therefore do so while sitting)."
sources: Ahmad (Vol.1 Pg.74), repcting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.82). Abu Nu'aym has also reported the narration in his Hilya (Vol. l Pg.56).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "Be modest in front of All "ah. I cover my head out of modesty before Al'iah even when I enter the toilet." iA

Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mas'ood (RA) and Hadhrat Umaarah bin Ghuraab Yahsubi both narrate that Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA) qnce came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I do not like my wife to see my private parts." "Why is that so?' asked Rasulullaah ﷺ. Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon replied, "Because 1 feel shy and I dislike it." Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "Allaah has made her your garment and made you hers. At times my wives see my private parts and I see theirs. "You do that, O Rasulullaah filfl" Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA) asked in surprise. When Rasulullaah confirmed that this was indeed so, Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA) said, "Who can there be after you (for me to follow)?" After he had left, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Verily Ibn Madh'oon is extremely bashful and one who always keeps his private area concealed."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.287).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Mijlaz reports that Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) said, "I bath in a dark room and do not stand up straight until I have picked up my clothes. This I do out of shyness for my Rabb." ® Hadhrat Abu Qataadah (RA) states that when Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari took a bath, he would do so in a dark room (sitting down) and bend over when getting his clothing without standing up straight. ® Hadhrat Anas (RA) says that Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) always wore some clothing when sleeping for fear of his private area becoming exposed.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg,260). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.84) has reported a similar narration. (3) ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.84).

paras: Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Nusay reports that Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) once saw some people standing in water without their lower garments. To this, he exclaimed, "I prefer to die and be raised again, then to die and be raised again and again to die and be raised again rather than doing what these people are doing."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.82).

paras: Hadhrat Ashaj Abdul Qais (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to him, "You have two qualities that Allaah loves." When he asked what they were, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Tolerance and modesty." Hadhrat Ashaj (RA) asked further, "Are these natural qualities within me or have they been developed afterwards?" "No," replied Rasulullaah ﷺ , "They have been naturally instilled within you." Hadhrat Ashaj (RA) then said, "All praise is for Allaah Who has instilled within me such qualities that He loves."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.84).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA) was once sitting with Rasulullaah ﷺ when he looked towards the sky. An angel suddenly descended to which Hadhrat Jibra'eel itfelc said, "Since he has been created, this angel has never descended until this moment." When the angel came down, he said, "O Muhammad ﷺ Your Rabb has sent me to you. (Allaah asks whether) 'Is it a Nabi who is a king that I should make you or a Rasool that is a slave (of Allaah)?"' Advising Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA) said, "Adopt humility before your Rabb, O Muhammad ﷺ Rasulullaah ﷺ then replied, "I would rather be a Rasool who is a slave,"
sources: Ahmad, Bazzaar and Abu Ya'la, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.19). (2) in the chapter "Giving Back wealth" and under the subheading "Rasulullaah iiii Refuses to Accept wealth given to him" followed by the subtitle "The Incident of Rasulullaah ﷺ With Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA) and another Angel".

paras: Another narration from Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) adds at the end, "After this, Rasulullaah ﷺ never ate in a reclining position and would say, 'I eat as a slave eats, and sit as a slave sits."
A similar narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) has already passed.

Hadhrat Abu Ghaalib says that he once asked Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) to narrate to them a Hadith that he had heard from Rasulullaah ﷺ. Hadhrat Abu Umaamah replied, "Everything that Rasulullaah ﷺ said was (according to) the Qur'aan. He made Dhikr in abundance, kept his lectures brief, lengthened his salaah and was never too stuck up, or proud to go with a poor or unimportant person to personally see to his needs."
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.20). Bayhaqi and Nasa'ee have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.45).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ made Dhikr in abundance, never engaged in futilities, rode a camel, wore woollen clothing and even accepted the invitations of slaves. If only you saw him (you would realise the extent of his humility) on the day the Battle of Khaypar was fought, he rode a donkey with reins made from the bark of a date palm."
sources: Tayaalisi.

paras: Another narration adds that Rasulullaah ﷺ also visited the ill and attended funerals.
sources: Tirmidhi. lbnSa'd(Vol.lPg.95)hasalsoreported the narration from Hadhrat Anas (RA) in more detail.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to ride a donkey, wear woollen clothes, hold down a goat and milk it and personally serve guests."
sources: Bayhaqi, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.45). Tabraani has also reported the narration from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.20).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ would sit on the floor, eat on the floor, hold down a goat himself while milking it and even accept the invitation of a slave to partake of barley bread." Another narration states that even in the middle of the night Rasulullaah ﷺ would accept the invitation to eat barley bread extended by a person from the upper part of Madman."
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.20).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ would accept an invitation even if it were to eat barley bread and foul-smelling fat. Rasulullaah ﷺ also had a suit of armour that he pawned to a -Jew and until the day he passed away, he did not have enough money to recover the armour from the man.
sources: Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il (Pg.23).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) says that when a man called for Rasulullaah ﷺ three times, Rasulullaah ﷺ replied with the word "Labbaik" ('At your service') each time.
sources: Abu Ya'la. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.20) has commented on the chain of narrators. Abu Nu'aym has also reported the narration in his Hilya, as quoted in Kanzul ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.45).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah Silg narrates that (during the time of Rasulullaah IS there was an immoral woman who was flirtatious with the men. She once passed by rasulullaah il when he was busy eating Thareed. She shouted out, "Look at this man, sitting like a slave and eating like a slave!" Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, "Which slave can be more devoted in his servitude (to Allaah) than I?" She then said further, "He eats without giving me anything to eat." "Do eat," Rasulullaah ﷺ said. "Give me with your hand," she demanded. When Rasulullaah till gave her, she made a further demand saying, "Give me from what is in your mouth." When Rasulullaah ﷺ complied and she ate the food, (its blessings were so profound that) the woman was overcome with modesty and she never flirted with a man for the rest of her life.
sources: Tabraani. Haythami Pg.21) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Jareer (RA) reports that when a man once came before Rasulullaah he started to shiver. Rasulullaah ﷺ put him at ease saying, "Take it easy. I am not a king but merely the son of a woman from the Quraysh who used to eat dried meat."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.20) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Another narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) states that it was on the day the Muslims conquered Makkah that a man started shivering while talking to Rasulullaah ﷺ. The rest of the narration is like the one above. Hadhrat Aamir bin Rabee'ah (RA) says, "I was proceeding with Rasulullaah M to the Masjid when one of his shoe straps broke. I immediately got hold of the shoe to fix it when Rasulullaah iif took it from my hand saying, "You are giving me preferential treatment and I dislike being given preferential treatment."
sources: Bayhaqi, as quoted in A/Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.4 Pg.293).
Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.21).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Jubayr Khuzaa'ee (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once walking with his companions when someone shaded him with a sheet. When he saw the shadow, Rasulullaah ﷺ looked up and saw the sheet that was shading him. "What is this?" Rasulullaah ﷺ exclaimed as he took hold of the sheet and put it down. He then said, "I am merely a human being like you (and therefore do not need preferential treatment)."
sources: Bazzaar, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.21).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) said, "I once said to myself, 'I wonder how long Rasulullaah ﷺ will still remain amongst us. (To ascertain this) I then proceeded to ask, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ Why do you not have a platform constructed for you?' Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'I prefer to remain amongst you (like one of you) with people trampling my heels and pulling at my shawl until the time when Allaah finally gives me comfort (and takes me away) from the people.
sources: Daarmi, as quoted in Jam'ul Fawaa'id (Vol.2 Pg.180). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.2 Pg,193) ruis reported a similar narration.

paras: In another narration from Hadhrat ikramah (RA), Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) says, "I shall definitely find out how long Rasulullaah ﷺ will still be staying amongst us. I then asked, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ I see that the people and the dust they kick up is causing you harm. Why do you not have a platform built for you from which you may address them? Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'I prefer to remain amongst you...' The reply is the same as above. Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) says further, "I then knew that Rasulullaah ﷺ would be with us for only a very short while."
sources: Ahmad. Bukhaari and Ibn Sa'd (Vol.1 Pg.9l) have reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Aswad reports that he once asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "What would Rasulullaah ﷺ do when he entered the house?" Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) replied, "He would engage himself in some domestic chores and would leave to perform salaah when the time for salaah arrived."
sources: Bayhaqi.

paras: Hadhrat Urwa SSI narrates that someone once asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "Would Rasulullaah ﷺ carry out domestic chores at home?" "Certainly," she replied, "He would mend his shoes and stitch his clothes just as any of you does at home." (1) Bazzaar. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.2l) has commented on the chain of narrators.

Hadhrat Amrah reports that she once asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "What would Rasulullaah ﷺ do at home?" Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) replied, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was a human and would remove lice from his clothing, milk his goat and take care of himself."
sources: Bayhaqi and Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il, as quoted in wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.44),

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ never assigned to anyone the duty of making arrangements for his wudhu and also the duty of handing out the charity he gave. He would personally attend to these duties.
sources: Qazweeni, as quoted in jam'ul Fawaa'id (Vol.2 Pg.180).

paras: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ came to visit me, he was neither riding a mule nor a thoroughbred horse."
sources: Bukhaari, as quoted in Saftvatus Safwah (Vol.1 Pg.25).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ performed on an old carriage (atop his camel) which was covered in a sheet that was hardly worth four Dirhams. Despite this, he prayed, 'O Allaahl Make this a Hajj devoid of ostentation and boastfulness.".
sources: Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il (Pg.24).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ffli? entered Makkah (upon the Conquest of Makkah) and the people were crowding to have a look at him, he placed his head against his carriage out of humility. ® Hadhrat Anas (RA) says that when Rasulullaah ﷺ entered Makkah on the day Makkah was conquered, he had his chin on his carriage out of humility.
sources: Abu Ya'la. Haythami (Vol. 6 Pg. 1 69) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Another narration states that when Rasulullaah ﷺ reached Dhu Tuwa, he stood on his carriage. He wore his reddish, striped Yemeni shawl around his head with its end hanging over his face. When Rasulullaah ﷺ saw the great victory that Allaah had blessed him with, he lowered his head so much in humility to Allaah that his beard touched the centre of the carriage.
sources: Bayhaqi.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports, "I once entered the marketplace with Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ sat with some cloth merchants and bought a trouser for four Dirhams. The cloth merchants had with them a person would took measurements. Addressing this person, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Let the benefit be for the buyer when taking measurements (give rather more than less).' Rasulullaah ﷺ then took the trousers and when I attempted to carry them for him, he said 'The owner of an item has a greater right to carrying it unless he is too weak or unable to do so. In that case, his Muslim brother may lend him a hand.' I then said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ Do you wear trousers?' He replied, 'Certainly. I wear them when on journey, when at home, during the night and during the day. I have been commanded to keep my private areas concealed and I find nothing more concealing than trousers.'"' Another narration adds that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Let the benefit be for the buyer when taking measurements." To this, the person taking measurements said, "I have never heard these words from any person before this." Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah said to him, "It is sufficient evidence of your ignorance and foolishness in Deen that you do not recognise your Nabi ﷺ The man immediately threw aside his scale and leapt up to grab the hand of Rasulullaah in an effort to kiss it. However, Rasulullaah ﷺ pulled his hand away from the man saying, "What is this?! It is only the non-Arabs who do this with their kings. I am not a king but a man from amongst you." The man then took the measurements and let the benefit go to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ then took the cloth. The rest of the narration is like the one mentioned above.
sources: Tabraani in his Awsat and Abu Ya'la. Ahmad has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Naseemur Riyaadh (Vol.2 Pg.105).

paras: Hadhrat Aslam reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) arrived in Shaam riding a camel, the people started talking amongst themselves (that he should have rather chosen a good horse for the journey). To this, Hadhrat Umar (RA) remarked, "Their gazes are on the conveyances of people (the Kuffaar) who have no portion (in the Aakhirah. They had rather look to the conveyances used by Rasulullaah and the Muslims)."
sources: Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.5 Pg.121). Tabraani and Abu Ya'la have also reported the narration but Haythami has commented on the chain of narrators. (3) lbn Asaakir and lbn Mubaarak, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 4 Pg.41 7). (4) lbn Sa'd.

paras: Hadhrat Hishaam narrates that he once saw Hadhrat Umar (RA) pass by a woman who was busy making Aseedah (a paste made from flour and clarified butter). "That is not how Aseedah is made," said Hadhrat Umar (RA). He then took a wooden spoon and showed her how to make it saying, "This is how it is done."

Hadhrat Hishaam bin Khaalid says that he heard Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab say (as he taught some women to make Aseedah), "You should never add the flour until the water is hot. When the water gets hot, you should then add the flour gradually as you stir with a spoon because it will then mix well without forming lumps."
sources: Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol.4 Pg.4l7).

paras: Hadhrat zirr says that he saw Hadhrat Umar (RA) proceed barefoot for the Eid salaah.
sources: Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol.4 Pg.418).

paras: Hadhrat Umar Makhzoomi reports that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) once made an announcement for the people to gather in the Masjid. The people got together and when a large number had gathered, Hadhrat Umar (RA) mounted the pulpit. After duly praising Allaah and sending salutations on Rasulullaah he said, "O people! I have seen the time when I used to graze animals for my maternal aunts from the Banu Makhzoom tribe. (As wages) They would then give me a handful of dates and raisins. I would then spend the entire day doing this and what days they were?!"

When Hadhrat Umar (RA) descended from the pulpit, Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! All you have done is ridicule yourself." "Shame on you, O Ibn Hadhrat Umar (RA) exclaimed, "When I was alone by myself, the thought came to mind that since I am the Ameerul Mu'mineen, there must be none better than me. (By doing what I did) I wanted to teach myself who I really was."
sources: Deenowri, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol.4 Pg.4l7). (4) lbn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.293).

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) added, "O people! 1 have seen the time when I had no source of livelihood apart from a few handfuls of raisins that my aunts from the Banu Makhzoom tribe would give me for bringing water for them." This narration ends with the words, "I found some pride in myself and therefore wished to humble myself (by telling the people what I did)."

Hadhrat Hasan reports that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) once left home on an extremely hot day with a shawl thrown over his head. When a young boy passed by riding a donkey, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "Dear boy! Please give me a ride with you on the donkey." The boy immediately jumped off the donkey saying, "You may get on, O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" "No," said Hadhrat Umar SIP "you ride and I will ride behind you. vou want me to have a comfortable place to ride when you are on a hard place (this cannot be)!" Hadhrat Umar then rode behind the boy. when they entered Madinah, the people stared at them because Hadhrat Umar (RA) was still riding behind the boy.

Hadhrat (RA) says, "I once went out with some other boys to pick up dates (that had fallen to the ground). Hadhrat Umar (RA) suddenly appeared with a lash in his hand and when the boys saw him, they dispersed amongst the date palms. I stood where I was with the dates I had picked up collected in my lower garment. 'O Ameerul Mu'mineen,' I said, 'these are the dates that the wind has blown off.' He looked at what was in my garment but did not hit me. I then said further, 'O Ameerul Mu'mineen! The boys are now ahead of me and they take away all that I have.' 'Never,' Hadhrat Umar (RA) assured me, 'Walk ahead.' He then accompanied me to my home."
sources: Deenowri, as quoted in Muntakhab Kamul Ummaal ! (Vol.4 Pg.4I7).

paras: The grandfather of Hadhrat Maalik say that he saw Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) when they arrived from Makkah and camped at a place called Mu'arras (Dhul Hulayfah). when the party rode again to enter Madinah, every one of them took a youngster to ride with him. in this manner, they entered Madinah. Even Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) had someone riding with them, One of the narrator's students asked, "Did they do this because of humility?" The reply was, "Certainly. In addition to this, they also wished to benefit others (so that the person need not walk) and did not want to be like other rulers (who feel it below their dignity to allow a commoner to ride with them)." The narrator then proceeded to criticise the new trend (of rulers) to make youngsters walk behind them as they rode.
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.7 Pg.90).

paras: Hadhrat Maymoon bin Mahraan reports from a man from Hamdaan that he saw Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) riding a mule with his slave Naa'il riding behind him on the same animal. This was during the time that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) was Khalifah.
sources: Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kamul Ummaal ' (Vol.2 Pg.143).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah Roomi says that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) himself fetched the water he needed for performing wudhu during the night. When someone suggested that he get one of the servants to do it for him, he refused saying, "The night is theirs to have a rest."

The grandmother of Hadhrat Zubayr bin Abdullaah had been a servant of Hadhrat Uthmaan. She says, "Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) never awakened any members of the household (at night when he awoke for Tahajjud). The only time he would ask any of them to get him water for wudhu was if he found them awake. He also fasted perpetually."
sources: Ibn Mubaarak in his Zuhd, as quoted in isaabah (Vol.2 Pg.463).

paras: Hadhrat Hasan says, "I saw Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) sleeping in the Masjid covered in a shawl. Although he was then the Ameerul Mu'mineen, there was none around him."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.60).

paras: Hadhrat Unaysa says, "The little girls of the locality would take their goats to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) (for milking). (Not only would he do it for them but) He would also ask, 'Would you like me to milk for you like ibn Afraa (someone from the Ansaar) does?"' The narrations of Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) and Ibn Musayyab have already passed in the chapter entitled "The Lives of the Khulafaa and Leaders". It is stated there that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was a businessman by trade and would proceed to the marketplace every morning to buy and sell. He also had a flock of goats that would come to him in the evenings. He sometimes took them out himself for grazing and sometimes had someone else graze them. He used to milk goats for the people of his locality so when he became the Khalifah, a little girl said, "Now there will be none to milk our animals." When he heard her saying this, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "Why not! 1 swear by my life that I shall definitely still milk for you. I hope that what I have entered into will never change the personality I always had." He then continued milking for the people and would sometimes say to the little girl of the locality, "Dear girl! Would you like me to make the milk foamy or without foam?" At times she would ask for foamy milk while at times she asked for it to have no foam. He then did exactly as she asked.
sources: Ibn Sa'd, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol.4).
Under the subheadings "The Life of Hadhrat Abu Bakr Siddeeq (RA) and "His Life Before Becoming the Khalifah and Afterwards".

paras: The blanket merchant Hadhrat Saalih reports from his grandfather who says, "I saw (Ameerul Mu'mineen) Hadhrat Ali (RA) purchase dates for a Dirham and then carry them in his bag. When 1 or another man offered to carry it for him, he refused the offer saying, 'The father of a family has a greater right to carry their goods.
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.81). Ibn Asaakir has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.56). Abul Qaasim Baghawi has also reported a similar narration, as quoted Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.8 Pg.5).

paras: Hadhrat Zaadhaan reports that even as Ameerul Mu'mineen, Hadhrat Ali (RA) used to walk alone in the marketplace where he would guide lost people, announce lost items and assist the weak. When passing by traders and grocers, he would open the Qur'aan and recite to them: This (fannah) is. the Home of the Aakhirah, which We shall assign to those who do not desire pomp (glory) on earth nor corruption, Qasas, verse 83) He would then say, "This verse was revealed with reference to rulers and people with authority over others who (despite their positions, they) exercise justice and are humble."
sources: lbn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol .5 Pg.56). Abul Qaasim Baghawi has also reported a similar narration, as quoted in A! Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol, 8 Pg.S). (2) lbn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.18). lbn Abdul Birr has reported a similar narration in his Isti'aab (Vol.3 Pg.48).

paras: Hadhrat Jurmooz narrates that he saw Hadhrat Ali (RA) emerge from his house wearing two reddish cloths made in Qatar, a lower garment that reached halfway up his calves and wrapped in a shawl of about the same size. He also carried a lash and walked with it in the marketplace, instructing people to be wary of Allaah and to trade in an amiable manner. He would also say, "Weigh and measure in full and do not blow into the meat (to make it appear large). "

Hadhrat Abu Matar says, "I was once leaving the Masjid when I suddenly heard someone behind me shouting, 'Lift your lower garment because it shows greater wariness of your Rabb and also keeps the garment cleaner. You should also trim your hair if you are a Muslim.' I then noticed that it was Hadhrat Ali holding a lash in his hand. He then went to the camel market where he said (to the traders), 'Never take oaths when selling because although oaths sell goods, they destroy blessings.'

When he went to a date seller, he found a servant weeping. When Hadhrat Ali asked her what the problem was, she informed him that her master refused to accept the dates that the date seller had sold to her for a Dirham. Addressing the seller, Hadhrat Ali (RA) instructed, 'Take back the dates and return her Dirham because she has no choice in the matter.' when it appeared as if the man would refuse, I said, 'Do you not know who this is?' He admitted that he did not. I then told him, 'He is Ameerul Mu'mineen Ali The man then readily poured out the dates into his own and returned the Dirham. Then he said, 'I want you to be pleased with me, O Ameerul Mu'mineen.' Hadhrat Ali (RA) replied, 'I shall be immensely pleased with you if you give people, their dues in full.' As he then passed by the other date sellers, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, 'Feed the poor and your earnings will increase.'

Hadhrat Ali (RA) proceeded further to, the fishmongers, whom he instructed with the words, 'Never sell in our markets fish that are found floating in the water (after dying).' Thereafter, Hadhrat Ali (RA) arrived at the cloth market where all the cloth merchants were found. Addressing one of them, he said, 'Dear old man! Give me a good deal on an upper garment for three Dirhams.' When the man recognised him, Hadhrat Ali (RA) did not buy from him but went to another merchant. However, when he also recognised Hadhrat Ali (RA), the Ameerul Mu'mineen did not buy from him either. Hadhrat Ali (RA) then purchased a garment from a youngster (who did not know him) for three Dirhams. When he wore it, the sleeves reached up to his wrists while the rest of it reached his ankles. When the owner of the store arrived, someone told him that his son had sold a garment to the Ameerul Mu'mineen for three Dirhams. Reprimanding the boy, he said, "Why did you rather not take two Dirhams?' He then took one Dirham and went to Hadhrat Ali (RA) saying, 'Please accept this Dirham,' 'What for?' Hadhrat Ali (RA) enquired. 'My son sold you the garment for three Dirhams when it costs only two Dirhams.' Hadhrat Ali (RA) refused to accept it saying, 'He sold it with my happiness and I bought it with his happiness.
sources: Ibn Raahway, Ahmad in his Zuhd, Abd bin Humayd, Abu Ya'la, Bayhaqi and Ibn Asaaklr, as quoted,

paras: Hadhrat Ataa reports that when Rasulullaah iffil's daughter Hadhrat Faatima kneaded dough, her plaits would hit against the bowl. Referring to Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA), Hadhrat Mutallib bin Abdullaah says, "It was in the evening that the Arab widow came as the bride of the best of all Muslims (Rasulullaah ﷺ) and later that night she was grinding flour."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.3 Pg.312). (3) ibn Sa'd (Vol.8 Pg.64).

paras: Hadhrat Salaamah Ajali says, "One of my cousins from the countryside whose name was Qudaamah came to me with the request, 'I wish to meet Salmaan Faarsi and greet him. We left to see him and found him in Madaa'in in command of an army of twenty thousand men. when we reached him, he was sitting on a platform, weaving baskets out of palm leaves. We greeted him and I said, 'O Abu Abdullaah! This is my cousin who is visiting me from the countryside. He wishes to greet you.' Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) replied to the greeting saying: I then continued to say, 'He also claims that he has a liking for you.' To this, Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) made the du'aa: 'May Allaah love him'."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol. 1 Pg. 1 97),

paras: Hadhrat Haarith bin Umayrah reports, "I once went to Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) and found him in his tannery scraping off some hide with his hands. When I greeted him with Salaam, he said, 'Remain where you are until I come out.' 'By Allaah!' I said, 'I do not think that you know who I am.' 'I certainly do,' he responded, 'My soul knew yours before I came to know you because all souls were a collective army (before coming to this world). Those that acquainted themselves for the pleasure of Allaah become friends and those who acquainted themselves for another besides Allaah will have enmity between themselves.
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Ummaal (Vol. 5 Pg.196). Abu Nu'aym has also reported the narration in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.198) in detail where the words of Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) are quoted from Rasulullaah ﷺ.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Qilaabah narrates that someone once came to Hadhrat Salmaan as he was busy making dough. "What is this?" the man said in surprise. Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) replied, "I had already sent the servant out on an errand and disliked giving him two jobs (so I decided to do this myself). The person then conveyed to Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) greetings from another person. "When did you arrive?" Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) enquired from the man. When the. man explained when he came, Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) said, "Remember well that had you not conveyed the greetings, it would remain an unfulfilled trust.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.20l). ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.64) and Ahmad have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Safwatus Safwah (Vol. 4 Pg.64),

paras: Hadhrat Amr the son of Abu Qurra Kindi says that his father once offered his sister in marriage to Hadhrat Salmaan (RA). However, Hadhrat Salmaan refused the offer and instead married a freed slave woman named Buqayrah (who once belonged to Hadhrat Abu Qurra).

When the news reached Hadhrat Abu Qurra that there had been an argument between Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) and Hadhrat Salmaan (RA), he went to Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) but was told that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) was in his field. There Hadhrat Abu Qurra found Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) with a basket full of greens. He had put his staff through the handle of the basket and carried it over his shoulder. As they walked to Hadhrat Salmaan (RA)'s house, Hadhrat Salmaan entered the house and said, "As Salaamu Alaykum," He then allowed Hadhrat Abu Qurra in. A bedding was spread out with a few bricks at the head side (as pillows). There were also a few odds and ends lying about. Hadhrat Salmaan said to. Hadhrat Abu Qurra, 'You may sit on the bedding that your slave had prepared for herself."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.198).

paras: Hadhrat Maymoon bin Mahraan reports that a man from the Abdul Qais tribe once saw Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) riding a donkey as commander of an army. He wore trousers, the legs of which fluttered about (in the wind). "Here comes the commander!" the soldiers called out (in derision). Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) said, "Good and bad will be known only after today (in the Aakhirah).'' A man from the Abdul Qais tribe says, "I was with Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) when he was commanding an army. As he passed by two youngsters from the army. they laughed as they remarked, 'This is your commander!' 'O Abu Abdullaah!' I protested, 'Do you not see what they are saying?' 'Leave them alone,' he bade me, 'Good and bad are to be seen after today (in the Aakhirah). If you are able to live off the earth, do so rather than being commander over even two persons.
