Beware of the curse of the oppressed and those left with no options because there is no barrier to their curses (Allaah accepts it immediately).'"

Another narration states that when Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) was the governor of Madaa'in, he would go out to the people wearing his simple lower garment and shawl. When they saw him, the people would say, "Gurg Aamad! Gurg Aamad!" "What are they saying?" Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) asked. "They are comparing you to a toy of theirs," the people replied. To this, Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) remarked, "It does not matter (what they say). Good will be seen only after this day (in the Aakhirah),"

Hadhrat Huraym reports, "I once saw Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) riding a donkey that was unsaddled. He was wearing a garment made in Sumbulaan which was short for him and was narrow at the bottom. He was a long-legged and hairy man and the garment reached only up to his knees. When I saw some youngsters (mischievously) prodding his donkey on from the back, I rebuked them saying, 'Will you not get away from your Ameer?!' To this, Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) said, 'Leave them alone because good and evil will only be seen after this day.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.l Pg.199).
Ibn Sa'd, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 7 Pg.23).

paras: Hadhrat Thaabit reports that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) was the governor of Madaa'in when a man arrived from Shaam carrying figs. Because Hadhrat Salmaan was wearing his simple lower garment and shawl, the man (not recognising Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) and thinking him to be a common labourer) called to him saying, "Come and carry this!" Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) obliged and when the people saw him and recognised who he was, they exclaimed, "This is the governor!" When the man pleaded that he did not recognise Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) (and wished to take the load back), Hadhrat Salmaan said to him, "Leave it until I reach your destination." Another narration states that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) added, "I had already formulated an intention (to please Allaah by this service) and I am therefore unable to put this down until I reach your house."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.277j.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Buraydah (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) used to make things with his hands and when he earned some money by selling them, he would purchase some meat or fish. He would then invite some lepers to share the meal with him.
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.373) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen reports that whenever Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab appointed a governor, he would write in the letter of appointment (the following instruction to the people of the area), 'You should listen to him and obey him as long as he exercises justice." However, when Hadhrat Umar (RA) appointed Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) as governor of Madaa'in, he wrote the following in his letter of appointment; "Listen to him, obey him and give him whatever he asks you for."

Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) then left Hadhrat Umar (RA) with a donkey fitted with a carriage to carry his goods. When Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) arrived in Madaa'in and was received by the people of the area and the local farmers, he was sitting on the carriage with a piece of bread and a bone with some meat in his hand. After reading out to them the letter of appointment, the people submitted, "You may ask us whatever you want." Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) said, "All I ask for is some food to eat and fodder for this donkey as long as I am with you." After staying there for some time, Hadhrat Umar (RA) sent for him to return. Upon receiving the news that Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) was approaching (Madinah), Hadhrat Umar (RA) hid himself beside the road at a place where he would not be seen. When he saw Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) return in exactly the same condition he had left in, Hadhrat Umar (RA) came out of his hiding place and embraced Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) saying, "You are my brother and I am yours."
sources: Tabraani and Isfahaani, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.4 Pg.345).

paras: Hadhrat Ibn Seereen narrates, "When Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) arrived in Madaa'in, he arrived riding atop a carriage mounted on his donkey. He was eating a piece of bread with a bone with some meat." A narration of Hadhrat Talha bin Musarrif adds that at the time, Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA)'s legs were dangling on the side of the donkey.

Hadhrat Sulaym bin Abu Hudhayl says, "1 mended clothes by the door of Hadhrat Jareer bin Abdullaah Siffisg, Whenever he came out of his house and mounted his mule, he would take his slave along with him on the animal."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA) was once passing through the marketplace carrying a bundle of wood when someone said to him, "What makes you do this when Allaah has freed you from it (you can always get someone else to do it for you)?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA) replied, "I wish to ward off pride because I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'The person in whose heart is an iota of pride will not enter Jannah."

Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "Three factors form the core of humility. (These are:) That one is first to greet whoever one meets, that one is content with an inferior position in a gathering rather than one of superiority and that one dislikes ostentation and boastfulness."
sources: Askari, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.143).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that the Sahabah (RA) once asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ You manage to joke with us?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "However, I speak only the truth (when I joke)."
sources: Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il (Pg.17) and Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.4l).

paras: A man once asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) whether Rasulullaah used to joke. When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas Wffigfe replied that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to joke, the man enquired about the nature of Rasulullaah fill's jokes, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) replied, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once gave one of his wives a large shawl to wear saying, "wear it, thank Allaah and drag it along like a bride's Rasulullaah ﷺ Jokes with Abu Umayr Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ had the best of character.

Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ had the best of character. I had a brother called Abu Umayr who was just weaned off milk. Whenever Rasulullaah came and saw him, Rasulullaah ﷺ would ask, "O Abu Umayr! How is This was the little red-beaked bird that Abu Umayr played with. At times, the time of salaah would arrive while Rasulullaah ﷺ was at our house. He would then have the mat he sat on spread out, swept and water sprinkled over it. Rasulullaah ﷺ would then stand up in salaah and we would stand behind him as he led the salaah. The mat was made of palm leaves."
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 4 Pg,43).

paras: In another narration, Hadhrat Anas (RA) states, "Rasulullaah ﷺ would associate with us so much that he waiald even ask my little brother, 'O Abu Umayr! How is Nughayr?
sources: Diminutive form of the word "Nughar", which was the little bird the boy played with.

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA). narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once visited Hadhrat Abu Talha (Hadhrat Anas (RA)'s step-father) when he noticed, that Hadhrat Abu Talha's son Abu Umayrwas looking depressed, Rasulullaah ﷺ usually joked with him whenever he met him and asked, "Why is Abu Umayr looking so sad?" When Rasulullaah ﷺ was informed that the little bird with which the child played had died, Rasulullaah ﷺ affectionately asked, "O Abu Umayr! How is Nughayr?"
sources: Ahmad, Abu Dawood and Tirmidhi, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Pg.46). Bukhaari has also reported the narration in his Adab pg.4i), as has Jbn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.224) who has specified the person to be Hadhrat Ummu Aymart (RA),

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a man once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ to ask for transport. Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "we shall give you the child of a camel to ride." "O Rasulullaah ﷺ the man said in surprise, "What will 1 do with the child of a camel (it is too small to ride)?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Is every camel not the child of another?"
sources: Abu Dawood, as quoted Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.46). Tirmidhi has also reported the narration in his Shamaa'il (Pg.16), as have Abu Nu'aym and ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg. 142).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once jokingly called Hadhrat Anas saying, "O two-eared one!"
sources: Ahmad, Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il and Ibn Hibbaan, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.46). Abu Ya'la and Bazzaar have also reported the narration. Bazzaar and Tabraani have also reported the narration from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.369).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a man from the countryside called Zaahir used to give Rasulullaah ﷺ things from the countryside and when he left, Rasulullaah ﷺ would give him things from the city, Rasulullaah ﷺ used to say, "Zaahir is our countryside and we are his city." Although he was not a good looking person, Rasulullaah ﷺ liked him a lot. As he was busy selling his wares in the marketplace one day, Rasulullaah ﷺ grabbed Mm from the back (and covered his eyes) so that he could not see. "Release me!" Hadhrat Zaahir shouted, but when he turned and recognised Rasulullaah ﷺ, he started pressing his back closer to Rasulullaah ﷺ's chest, "who will buy this slave?" Rasulullaah ﷺ announced. "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Zaahir (RA) said, "By Allaah! If you sell me, you will run at a loss." "Not at all," Rasulullaah ﷺ corrected, "You are not a loss in the sight of Allaah. In Allaah's sight, you are expensive."

Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Basheer (RA) -narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr was once about to ask permission to enter Rasulullaah fife's room, he heard (his daughter) Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) raising her voice at Rasulullaah When, he entered, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) grabbed her to give her a slap saying, "Are you raising your voice above that of Allaah's Rasool ﷺ However, Rasulullaah ﷺ stopped him from taking action and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) left in anger. After Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) had left, Rasulullaah ﷺ said to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "Now what do you think of me after I rescued you from that man?" It was a few days later that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) again sought permission to see Rasulullaah ﷺ. This time he found that the couple had reconciled and said to them, "Now enter me into your peace as you had entered me into your war." "We certainly will," Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "We certainly will."
sources: Abu Dawood, as quoted in wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.46).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports, "I once accompanied Rasulullaah ﷺ on one of his journeys when I was still a slim girl who had not put on much weight. Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed the others to go ahead and when they did, he said to me, "Cornel Let's have a race." I then beat him in the race. Rasulullaah ﷺ let the matter rest until the time came when I had put on weight and forgotten about the incident. When I then accompanied him on a journey, he again instructed the others to proceed ahead. When they did so, he said to me, "Come! Let's have a race." This time he beat and he laughed as he said, "This is for that." Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once on a journey with his wives riding in front of him. Addressing the person who was reciting some poems to drive the camels on faster, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Anjasha! Shame on you! Take it easy with the crystals (the women. Do not drive the camels too fast)."
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.4l).

paras: In another narration, Hadhrat Anas (RA) says that Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym was with the wives of Rasulullaah ﷺ (on a journey) when Rasulullaah came to them. (Noticing that the camels were being driven too fast) Rasulullaah ﷺ said (to the person driving them along), "O Anjasha! Move easily with the crystals." Hadhrat Abu Qilaabah says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ made a statement that if any of you made, it would be held against him; (the statement was), "Go easy with the crystals."
sources: Zubayr bin Bakkaar and Ibn Asaakit, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal Pg.43),

paras: Hadhrat Hasan reports that an old woman once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ with the request, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Pray to Allaah to enter me into Jannah." Addressing her by her title, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Old women will not enter jannah." When the lady turn away in tears, Rasulullaah ﷺ sent someone to give her the message that she would not enter jannah as on old woman because Allaah says: Indeed We have created these damsels (of Jannah) very specially and We have made them all virgins... (Surah waaqi'Ahmad, verses 35,36)

Hadhrat AwfbinMaalikAshja'ee (RA) reports, "I went to Rasulullaah ﷺ during the expedition to Tabook while he was in a (very small) leather tent. I greeted Rasulullaah ﷺ with Salaam and after he replied, I asked, 'May I enter?' When Rasulullaah ﷺ permitted me to enter, I asked, 'All of me, 0 Rasulullaah ﷺ Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'All of you.' I then entered."
Hadhrat Waleed bin Uthmaan bin Abu Aaliyah explains that Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik joked "All of me" because the tent was very small. (,)

Hadhrat Ibn Abu Mulaykah (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) only cracked a few jokes with Rasulullaah ﷺ, her mother said, "O Rasulullaah Many of our tribe's jokes come from the Kinaana tribe." "In fact," Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, "this tribe is the subject of many of our jokes."
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.41).

paras: Hadhrat Abul Haytham reports from someone that he heard Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan bin Harb joking with Rasulullaah ﷺ in the house of his daughter Hadhrat Ummu Habeebah (RA) (who was one of Rasulullaah iii?'s wives). Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) said, "By Allaah! As soon as I left you alone (stopped fighting you), all the Arabs also left you, otherwise the horned ones and hornless ones would all still be fighting because of you." Rasulullaah ﷺ smiled as he said, "You and what you say, O Abu Handhala."
sources: Majma'uz Zawaa'ld ^ (Vol.8 Pg.89).

paras: Hadhrat Bakr bin Abdullaah says, "Although the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah used to (playfully) throw melons at each other, they were still the most resolute men when matters were serious."

Hadhrat Qurra narrates that he once said to Hadhrat ibn Seereen, "Did the Sahabah (RA) joke and play?" Hadhrat Ibn Seereen replied, "They were just like other people, in fact, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin umar (RA) used to say the following couplet in jest: "He (is so miserly that) loves to drink wine from the money of his companions and dislikes to part with his own money"

Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once went on a trade journey to Busra. Accompanying him were Hadhrat Nu'aymaan and Hadhrat Suwaybit bin Harmala (RA), both of whom were veterans of the Battle of Badr. Because Hadhrat suwaybit (RA) was in charge of the goods, Hadhrat Nu'aymaan (RA) asked him for something to eat, Hadhrat Suwaybit refused saying that they would have to wait for Hadhrat Abu Bakr. Hadhrat Nu'aymaan (RA) who was a joker and full of tricks, went to the people (of the locality), with his camel in trail. "Who will buy from me an intelligent Arab slave?" he announced. When some people agreed to the sale, Hadhrat Nu'aymaan (RA) warned, "He is however a good talker and may claim to be a free person, if you intend letting him go on this pretext of his, then let me be and do not complicate matters for me (do not make the purchase)." "No!" the people insisted, "We shall buy him from you in exchange for ten young camels." Hadhrat Nu'aymaan (RA) then returned, leading the camels (and the buyers) along with him. He then said to them, "There he is. Grab him!" Hadhrat Suwaybit pleaded, "He is lying! I am a free man." "He has already told us about you," the people said as they threw a rope around his neck and took him away. When Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) returned and was informed about what had happened, he went to the people with his companions, returned the ten camels to them and got Hadhrat Suwaybit (RA) back. Rasulullaah ﷺ was also informed about the incident and it kept him and the Sahabah (RA) laughing for an entire year afterwards.
sources: Ahmad. Abu Dawood Tayaalisi and Rooyaani have reported a similar narration but with the roles of Hadhrat Suwaybit (RA) and Hadhrat Nu'aymaan (RA) reversed. Refer to Isaabah (Vol.2 Pg.98) for further details. Ibn Abdul Birr has also reported the narration in his Isti'aab (Vol. 2 Pg.162) and (Vol.3 Pg.573).

paras: Hadhrat Rabee'ah bin Uthmaan (RA) narrates that a Bedouin once came to see Rasulullaah ﷺ and put his camel to sit in the courtyard of the Masjid. Some of the Sahabah (RA) then suggested to Hadhrat Nu'aymaan bin Amr Ansaari who was referred to as An- Nu'aymaan, "We have a strong desire to eat some meat so why don't you slaughter that camel for us to eat. Rasulullaah ﷺ will then recompense the owner for it."
Hadhrat Nu'aymaan (RA) went ahead to slaughter it and when the Bedouin came out of the Masjid and saw his camel slaughtered, he screamed, "Oh dear!

My camel has been slaughtered, O Muhammad!" ﷺ came out and asked, "Who did that?" When the Sahabah (RA) informed him that it was Hadhrat Nu'aymaan (RA), Rasulullaah ﷺ searched for him. After making queries about his whereabouts, Rasulullaah ﷺ finally found him in the house of Hadhrat Subaagha bint Zubayr bin Abdul Muttalib. He was hiding in a hole and covered himself with palm leaves and bark. Pointing his finger towards the hole, someone shouted as he said, "I have not seen him, O Rasulullaah iii!" When Rasulullaah ﷺ got Hadhrat Nu'aymaan (RA) out of the hole, his face was messed with the palm bark that had fallen onto it. "What made you do that?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him. "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Nu'aymaan (RA) submitted, "The same people who led you to me were the ones who instructed me to do it." Rasulullaah ﷺ then smiled as he started wiping Hadhrat Nu'aymaan's face. Thereafter, Rasulullaah ﷺ recompensed the Bedouin for his camel.

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mus'ab (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Makhramah bin Naufal bin Uhayb Zuhri was an extremely old blind man in Madinah who had already reached the age of a hundred and fifteen. One day he stood in the Masjid ready to urinate when the people started shouting at him. It was then that Hadhrat Nu'aymaan bin Amr bin Rifaa'ah bin Haarith bin Sawaad Najaatj came to him and led him to the corner of the Masjid saying, "Sit here." There he made him sit and urinate. As Hadhrat Makhramah (RA) urinated, the people started to scream at him. When he had finished, Hadhrat Makhramah (RA) asked, "Shame on you people! Who was it that brought me here?" When he was informed that it was Hadhrat Nu'aymaan (RA), Hadhrat Makhramah (RA) cursed him saying, "Take note! I swear by Allaah that if I ever get the upper hand over him, I will hit him most severely with this staff of mine." After some time, Hadhrat Makhramah (RA) had forgotten about the incident when Hadhrat Nu'aymaan (RA) came to him. At the time, Hadhrat Uthmaan was performing salaah in the corner of the Masjid and it was his habit not to ever pay attention to anything else whilst performing salaah. Hadhrat Nu'aymaan asked Hadhrat Makhramah (RA), "Are you still after Nu'aymaan?" "O yes," Hadhrat Makhramah (RA) said, "Where is he? Lead me to him." Hadhrat Nu'aymaan (RA) then led Hadhrat Makhramah (RA) to Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) saying, "Here he is. Grab him!" Hadhrat Makhramah then took his staff into both hands and hit Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) so hard that his head was severely injured. Someone then told Hadhrat Makhramah "It was the Ameerul Mu'mineen that you hit!" When (Hadhrat Makhramah SISSY'S tribe) the. Banu Zuhra heard about the incident, they got together (to punish Hadhrat Nu'aymaan (RA) but Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) said, "May Allaah's mercy be far from him. Leave Nu'aymaan alone because he is a veteran of Badr." Generosity.
sources: Ibn Abdul Birr in his Isti'aab (Vol.3 Pg.575). Zubayr bin Bakkaar has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.3 Pg.570). (25 isti'aab (Vol.3 Pg.57?) and Isaabah (Vol.3 Pg.570).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was the most generous of people. He was even more generous on Ramadhaan when he met Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA) every night and revised the with him. In fact, Rasulullaah ﷺ was even more generous than the blowing wind (that benefits all and sundry),"
sources: Rasulullaah ﷺ then told her, "Adorn yourself with these."

paras: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ never said 'No' to anything asked ofhim." In a lengthy Hadith from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Bakr, Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ never refused anything asked of him."
sources: Hadhrat Ummu Sumbula (RA) narrates that when she once presented a gift to Rasulullaah ﷺ, his wives refused to accept it, saying, "We cannot accept this." They however took it when Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed them to do so. In return, Rasulullaah ﷺ then allotted to her a piece of land between two mountains. It was this piece of land that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Jahash (RA) bought from
Bukhaari, Muslim, as quoted in Safwatus Safwah (Vol.1 Pg.69). lbn Sa'd (Vol .2 Pg.195) has also reported the narration.

paras: In another lengthy narration, Hadhrat Ali (RA) says, "When asked to do something, Rasulullaah ﷺ always said Yes' when he intended doing it and would remain silent when he did not intend doing it (when it was not to the benefit of the person asking). However, he never said 'No' to anything asked of him.
sources: Bukhaari and Muslim, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.42).

paras: Hadhrat Rubayyi bint Mu'awwidh bin Afraa (RA) says, "(My father) Hadhrat Mu'awwidh bin Afraa sent me to Rasulullaah ﷺ with a Saa of fresh dates topped with slices of newly grown cucumbers because Rasulullaah ﷺ loved cucumbers. Rasulullaah iii? had then just received some jewels from Bahrain so he scooped up a handful of the jewels and gave them to me." Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ filled her hand with either jewels or gold.
Hadhrat Hasan bin (RA). Other incidents about the generosity of Rasulullaah ﷺ have passed in the chapters concerning spending of wealth in the path of Allaah.
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.14) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin umar (RA) reports that a woman once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "I want to give this garment to the most generous of all Arabs," Pointing to Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Al Aas (RA) who was standing there, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Give it to this young man." It is for this reason that such garments are referred to as Sa'eediyyah. Other incidents about the generosity of the sahabah have passed in the chapters concerning spending of wealth in Jihaad and in the path of Allaah.
sources: Zubayr bin Bakkaarand, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Vmmaal '(Vol ,5 Pg.189).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "There passed a time when (we had so much concern for each other that) none of us (Sahabah (RA) thought himself more than his fellow Muslim brother. Unfortunately, we are now in a time when Dinaars and Dirhams are more beloved to us than our fellow Muslim brothers." The narration still continues further. Several incidents of preferring others above oneself have passed in the chapter dealing with spending on others despite being in need and other stories about the Ansaar. There, incidents were mentioned how they gave others despite their intense thirst and need for clothing (and other necessities).
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.285). (4) lbn Maajah, Ibn Abi Dunya and Haakim, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.5 Pg.243). Bayhaqi has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kanzul Vmmaal ' (Vol.2 Pg.lS4), as has Abu Nu'aym in his Hllya (Vol. 1 Pg.370).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports that he once visited Rasulullaah ﷺ when Rasulullaah ﷺ was suffering extreme fever and was. covered in a blanket. Placing his hand on the blanket, Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed (RA) said, "What a high fever you have, O Rasulullaah ﷺ Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, "Thus are difficulties intensified for us and likewise are the rewards multiplied." "O Rasulullaah iii!" Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed (RA) asked, "Who are the people who suffer the most difficulties?" "The Ambiyaa," came the reply. "Who next?" Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed asked further. Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "The Ulema." When Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed (RA) asked who was next, Rasulullaah ﷺ informed him, "The pious people. Some of them are so troubled by lice that they are killed and others are so impoverished that they own only the garment they wear. Despite all of this, they are as pleased with difficulties as any of you are pleased with bounties."

Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Hudhayfah (RA) reports from his aunt Hadhrat Faatimah that she was with a few women who visited Rasulullaah ﷺ when he was suffering high fever. Because of the intensity of the fever, Rasulullaah ﷺ had a water bag hung overhead from a branch and lay beneath it so that drops of water fell' on to his head. "O Rasulullaah ﷺ she said, "why don't you pray to Allaah to cure you?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Those who suffer the most difficulties are the Ambiyaa, then those closest to them, then those closest to them and then those closest to them."
sources: Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (VoI,2 Pg.154). Ahmad and Tabraani have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id '(Vol.2 Pg.292).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ was once overcome with pain, he was in great suffering and turned from side to side on his bed. Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) asked, "would you not be angry with any of us if we had to do this?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Difficulties will continue harassing a Mu'min but whenever he is pricked by a thorn or suffers any other pain, a sin is forgiven and a stage (in the Aakhirah) is elevated." The Sahabah mmm Exercise Patience with Illness.
sources: Ibn Sa'd, Haakim and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 2 Pg.154). Ahmad has reported a similar narration from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.292).

paras: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that fever (in the human form Allaah had granted it) once sought permission to see Rasulullaah ﷺ. "Who is it?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. "Ummu Mildam(1)," was the reply, Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed it to go to the people of Quba and (when: it did) only Allaah knows how many people were afflicted, when the people of Quba came to complain about it to Rasulullaah he asked, "You have a choice. If you wish, I shall pray to Allaah to remove it from you or if you prefer, it could (remain amongst you and thereby) be a means of purification for you (from sin)." "Can you really do this?" they asked, when Rasulullaah ﷺ conformed that he could, they bade him to let it stay.
sources: This is the title Arabs give to fever.

paras: Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) narrates that when fever once sought permission to see Rasulullaah ﷺ, '-he asked who it was. It replied, "I am fever. I peel at flesh and suck blood." "Go to the people of Quba," Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed. It then proceeded there and (after a while) the people of Quba came to Rasulullaah im with pale faces, when they complained atout the fever to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he asked them, 'You have a choice. If you wish, I shall pray to Allaah and He will remove it from you or if you prefer, you could leave it to remain amongst you and thereby be a means of removing all the sins you may have left." Their reply was, "Why not (why should we not want our sins forgiven)? Leave it, O Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that fever once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ with the request, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Send me to those people or those of your companions who are most beloved to you." "Go to the Ansaar," Rasulullaah ﷺ said. It then went to them and floored them. The Ansaar then came to Rasulullaah ﷺ pleading, "O Rasulullaah iii! Fever has afflicted us, so do pray to Allaah to cure us." Rasulullaah ﷺ then prayed and they were cured. A woman then ran behind Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Pray for me as well because I am from the Ansaar. Pray for me as you have prayed for them." Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "What do you prefer? Would you rather have me pray for you and that you be cured or would you rather exercise patience (and remain with the illness) in which case it will be incumbent for you to enter Jannah?" She immediately submitted three times, "No! I swear by Allaah O Rasulullaah ﷺ that I would rather exercise patience." She then added, "By Allaah! I shall never jeopardise His Jannah for anything."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg,306) has commented on the chain of narrators. Bayhaqi has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol .6 Pg, 1 60) .

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once did not notice someone who regularly attended his gatherings. When Rasulullaah ﷺ asked what the matter was that the person was not to be seen, the Sahabah (RA) informed Rasulullaah ﷺ that the man had been struck down by an intense fever. "Let us go an visit him," Rasulullaah ﷺ said to them. When Rasulullaah entered the room, the young man started to cry. "do not cry," Rasulullaah H consoled him, "because Jibra'eel has just informed me that fever is my Ummah's share of Jahannam (if they suffer it in this world, they will not be subjected to Jahannam in the Aakhirah, inshaa Allaah)."
sources: Bayhaqi, as quoted in M Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.i60). Bukhaari has also reported the narration in his Adab (Pg.73).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Safar reports that when some people came to visit Hadhrat Abu Bakr during his illness, they said, "O Khalifah of Rasulullaah ﷺ Should we not summon a physician to see you?" "He has already been to see me," Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) informed them. "And what did he say to you?" they asked. (Referring to Allaah) Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) replied, "He said, 'I do as I please'."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.302) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Qurra Sfilg narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Dardaa fell ill, his friends came to visit him. "what is the problem?" they asked. "My sins," he replied. "What do you wish for?" they enquired further. "I wish for jannah," was his reply. "Should we summon a physician for you?" they asked.
Hadhrat Abu Dardaa US replied, "It is He (Allaah) Who has made me lay here (with this illness
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.i4l), Ibrt Shaybah, Ahmad in his Zuhd and Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.34), as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.153).

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Ghanam reports that when the plague struck Shaam, Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) announced, "This plague is a punishment, so flee from it to the valleys and ravines." When news of this statement reached Hadhrat Shurahbeel bin Hasanah (RA), he became incensed and said, "Amr bin Al Aas is wrong! I was a companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ at a time when Amr was more astray than the camel his family owns. This plague is the du'aa of your Nabi the mercy of your and the way in which many pious people lost their lives in the past."

When this news reached Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA), he prayed, "O Allaah! Grant the family of Mu'aadh their share in full." His two daughters then passed away in the plague and his son Abdur Rahmaan was also afflicted. Advising his son, Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) recited the verse: The truth is from your Rabb so never be among those who doubt. (Surah Baqarah, verse 147)
To this, his son replied with the following verse of the Qur'aan: If Allaah wills, you will soon find me to be among the patient ones.

(Surah Saaffaat, verse 102) The plague then struck Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) himself (and it showed up first) on the back of his hand. "This," Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) said, "is more beloved to me than red camels." When he saw a man weeping beside him, he asked, "what makes you weep?" The man replied, "I am crying over the knowledge I used to gain from you (which I shall no longer be gaining after your demise)." "Do not cry," Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) consoled him, "because although Hadhrat Ibraheem was in a place where there was no knowledge to be leamt, Allaah gave him the knowledge. After I die, seek knowledge from four men (viz,) Abdullaah bin Mas'ood, Abdullaah bin Salaam, Salmaan and Abu Dardaa Another narration states that Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA), Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah, Hadhrat Shurahbeel bin Hasanah (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Maalik Ash'ari were all struck by the plague on the same day. Hadhrat Mu'aadh said, "This is the mercy of your Rabb, the du'aa of your Nabi and the manner in which the lives of the pious ones before you were taken. O Allaah! Grant the family of Mu'aadh their full share of this mercy." The night was not yet over when his only son Abdur Rahmaan was struck by the plague. Abdur Rahmaan was the most beloved person to Hadhrat Mu'aadh and it was with his name that Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) received his title (of Abu Abdur- Rahmaan). Returning from the Masjid, Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) found his son restless and asked, "O Abdur Rahmaan! How are you?" In reply, his son said, "Beloved father, "The truth is from your Rabb so never be among those who doubt." Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) said to him, "If Allaah wills, you will soon find me to be among the patient ones." Abdur Rahmaan passed away that night and Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) buried him the following morning. Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) was also afflicted with the plague and when the pangs of death struck him, they struck more severely than they did any other person. Each time he regained consciousness from his coma, he opened his eyes and said, "O Rabb! You may strangle as often as you please because I swear by Your honour that You know how much my heart loves You."

Hadhrat Shahr bin Howshab reports from a man from his tribe called Raaba that when the plague started to spread, Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin jarraah (RA) addressed the people saying, "O people! This plague is the mercy of your Rabb, the du'aa of your Nabi ﷺ and the manner in which the lives of the pious ones before you were taken. Abu Ubaydah prays that Allaah grant him his full share of it." Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah S.G8SS was then struck with the plague and passed away. Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) was then appointed commander over the troops and he later addressed the people saying, "O people! This plague is the mercy of your Rabb, the du'aa of your Nabi ﷺ and the manner in which the lives of the pious ones before you were taken. Mu'aadh prays that Allaah grant his family their full share of it." His son Abdur Rahmaan was then struck by the plague and passed away. Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) then prayed to Allaah that the plague strike him and it did (the first signs appearing) on his palm. The narrator says, "I saw Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) looking at his palm and then turning it around saying, 'I swear by Allaah that I would not like to exchange you for anything in this world.'"

After Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) passed away, Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) was appointed commander. When he stood up to address the people, he said, "O people! When this plague strikes, it spreads like wildfire so seek shelter from it in the mountains." To this, Hadhrat Abu Waathilah Hudhali .USslgi remarked, "You are wrong! By Allaah! I was in the company of Rasulullaah ﷺ when you were worse than this donkey of mine!" Hadhrat Amr (RA)'s response was, "By (1) lbn Khuzaymah and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.325). Ahmad and Bazzaar have also reported the narration, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id '(Vol.2 Pg.312).
Allaah! I shall not reply to what you are saying but I swear by Allaah that we shall not be staying on here."

The narrator continues, "Hadhrat Amr (RA) then left, the people scattered and Allaah removed the plague from them. When the opinion of Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas reached (Ameerul Mu'mineen) Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab he said "I swear by Allaah that he did not condemn it."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.240). Haakim (Voi.l Pg.276) has also reported the narration. Ahmad has also reported the narration from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.311).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Qilaabah narrates that when the plague struck Shaam, Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas said, "This is a scourge that has come so flee from it to the mountains and ravines." When this statement reached Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA), far from confirming it, he said, "Not at all! It is martyrdom, a mercy and the du'aa of your Nabi iiif ." Hadhrat Abu Qilaabah narrates further, "While I knew that it was a form of martyrdom and a mercy, I did not know how it was the du'aa of Rasulullaah ﷺ until I was informed that while performing salaah one night, Rasulullaah ﷺ thrice made du'aa saying, 'Then let it be fever or a plague.' The following morning, one of his family members asked, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ I overheard you making a du'aa last night.' heard it?' Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. 'I certainly did,' came the reply. Rasulullaah iiif then explained, 'I asked my Rabb not to let my Ummah perish through drought and this du'aa was accepted. I then prayed to Allaah never to allow an enemy to overpower them and annihilate them (this was also granted). I also prayed to Him never to let my Ummah fragment into groups, waging wars against each other. This du'aa however was refced. It was then that I thrice said, let it be fever or a plague'."
sources: Ibn Is'haaq, as quoted in wan Nihaayah (Vol.7 Pg.78).

paras: Hadhrat Uxwa bin Zubayr (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah and his family were unaffected by the plague of Amwaas when he prayed to Allaah saying, "O Allaah! Grant the family of Abu Ubaydah their share," When a sore erupted on his little finger, Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) started looking at (thinking that it was a sign of the plague) but he was assured that it meant nothing. He then said, "I wish that Allaah blesses it because when he blesses something little, it becomes a lot."
sources: Ahmad. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.3i l) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Haarith bin Abu Umayrah Haarithi narrates that Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal sent him to ask Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) how he was when the plague struck him. Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) showed Hadhrat Haarith a sore that had erupted on his palm. It looked very serious to Hadhrat Haarith and gave him a fright. Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) then swore in the name of Allaah that he would not want to trade it even for red camels.

Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) says, "When I developed a cataract, Nabi ﷺ came to visit me. He asked, Zaid! What would you do if you lost your eye?' 'I shall exercise patience and look forward to the rewards (from Allaah),' I replied. Rasululiaah then said, 'If after losing your eye you exercise patience and anticipate the rewards, your reward will be Jannah.".
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.74).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that he accompanied Rasululiaah to visit Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) when he was suffering from an eye ailment. Rasululiaah said to him, "O zaid! if you lose your eye and exercise patience and anticipate the rewards, you will meet Allaah without a single sin against your name."
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.78).

paras: Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) narrates that Rasululiaah once visited him when he was ill. Rasululiaah said, "No harm will come to you from this illness but what will you do if you reach old age after my demise and then lose your eyesight?" Hadhrat Zaid (RA) replied, "I shall then exercise patience and anticipate the rewards." "In that case," Rasululiaah remarked, "you shall enter Jannah without reckoning." Hadhrat Zaid (RA) later did go blind after Rasululiaah's demise.
sources: Ahmad. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.308) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Another narration adds that after the demise of Rasululiaah, Hadhrat Zaid (RA) did go blind but Allaah restored his eyesight before he passed away. May Allaah shower his mercies on him.
sources: Abu Yala and Ibn Asaakir. Bayhaqi has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg. 157).

paras: Hadhrat Qaasim bin Muhammad narrates that when some people visited a Sahabi SI who had lost his eyesight, he said, "I wanted my sight only to see Rasululiaah SSI However, since Rasululiaah has passed away, it would not even please me to use them to see a gazelle from the. gazelles of Tabaala (a place in Yemen),"
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.309) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "1 saw (Rasulullaah ﷺ's son) Ibraheem JU) surrendering his soul in front of Rasulullaah ﷺ. With his eyes filled with tears, Rasulullaah said, 'Although the eyes weep and the heart grieves, we shall say only that which pleases Allaah. O Ibraheem! I swear by Allaah that we are deeply saddened by your demise.'"

Hadhrat Makhool narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was leaning on Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf as he entered the room where (his son) Ibraheem was surrendering his soul. When the boy passed away, Rasulullaah iSI?'s eyes filled with tears. Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Is this not what you forbade people from doing? When the Muslims see you weep, they will also weep." When his tears stopped, Rasulullaah said, "This (these tears) is because of mercy (soft-heartedness) and whoever is not merciful will not have mercy shown to him. What we. have been forbidding people from doing is from wailing and from praising attributes of a (deceased) person that he never possessed. Had it not been for Allaah's promise to gather people together (for reckoning), for the fact that death is a well travelled path and for the fact that the last of us will meet with the first of us, we would have felt grief more severe than this. Because of our sorrow over his death our eyes weep and our hearts grieve but we shall never say anything that will anger our Rabb. The balance of his suckling will be done in Jannah."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.1 Pg.90).

paras: Hadhrat Usaamah bin Zaid (RA) narrates that they were with Rasulullaah ﷺ one day when one of his daughters sent for him with the message that her son was dying. Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed someone saying, "Go and inform her that to Allaah belongs all that He takes and all that He gives and He has decreed a fixed term for everything. Instruct her to exercise patience and to look forward to the rewards (from Allaah for her patience)." The messenger returned to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "She is beseeching you to come in the name of Allaah," Rasulullaah ﷺ got up to leave and a few of the Sahabah (RA) went with him. Amongst them were Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA), Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal, Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) and Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit Hadhrat Usaamah (RA) says, "I also accompanied them and when the child was given to Rasulullaah till, he was quivering in the throes of death (making a sound) as if the soul was in an old water bag. As Rasulullaah ﷺ's (1 ) Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.78). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.2 Pg,85) has reported a similar narration. eyes welled with tears, Sa'd Sliife' asked, What is this (tears), O Rasulullaah ii Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'This is the mercy that Allaah has placed in the hearts of His servants and it is only upon His merciful servants that Allaah showers His mercy.
sources: lbn Sa'd (Vol.1 Pg.88) and in more detail in (Vol.1 Pg.89).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that as Rasulullaah ﷺ stood by the body of Hadhrat Hamzah bin Abdul Muttalib (RA) when he was martyred, the sight was more painful than any he had ever witnessed because the body had been savagely mutilated. Rasulullaah ﷺ said words similar in effect to: "May Allaah shower His mercy on you. As far as I know, you were one who maintained family ties and always did good works. By Allaah! If it were not for the added grief it would cause your family, I would prefer to leave you in this condition so that Allaah may resurrect you from the bellies of wild animals (that will eat your corpse)." Rasulullaah ﷺ then added, "Take note! I swear by Allaah that to avenge you, I shall have seventy of the Kuffaar mutilated as they have done to you." It was then that Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA) arrived with the following verse: When you claim retribution (for a wrong done to you), then avenge yourself in proportion to the aggression (wrong) done against you (and not any more). But if you exercise patience (without taking revenge), then this is definitely best for the patient ones. (Surah Nahl, verse 126) Rasulullaah ﷺ then paid the expiation (for not fulfilling the oath) and restrained himself from taking action. ® Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ saw what was done to (his uncle) Hadhrat Hamzah (RA), he remarked, "If it were not for the grief it would cause our women, I would not bury him and would leave him in this condition so that Allaah would resurrect him from the bellies of wild animals and birds of prey." When the sight grieved him too deeply, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "If I get the upper hand over them (the Mushrikeen), I shall mutilate thirty of them." It was then that Allaah revealed the verse: When you claim retribution (for a wrong done to you), then avenge yourself in proportion to the aggression (wrong) done against you (and not any more). But if you exercise patience (without taking revenge/, then this is definitely best for the patient ones. Be patient! Your patience is only from Allaah (only Allaah can give you the ability to exercise patience). Do not grieve over them (the Kuffaar when they refuse to accept Islaam) and do not be saddened by their plotting (against you because Allaah will see to them). (Surah Nahl, verses Rasulullaah ﷺ then gave instructions for the body of Hadhrat Hamzah (RA) to be turned towards the Qiblah and performed the Janaazah salaah with nine Takheers. All the other martyrs were then brought to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Each time a martyr was brought, he was placed beside Hadhrat Hamzah (RA) and Rasulullaah ﷺ would perform the Janaazah salaah for the martyr and Hadhrat Hamzah. In this manner, Rasulullaah ﷺ performed the Janaazah salaah seventy-two times for Hadhrat Hamzah (RA). Rasulullaah ﷺ then stood by the Sahabah (RA) until the martyrs were buried. After the above verse was revealed, Rasulullaah ﷺ forgave the Mushrikeen and forsook the idea of mutilation.
sources: Bukhaari and Muslim, as quoted in wan Nihaayah (Vol.3 Pg.274).

paras: Hadhrat Usaamah bin Zaid (RA) says, "When my father (Hadhrat Zaid bin Haaritha was martyred, I went to see Rasulullaah ﷺ. When he saw me, Rasulullaah ﷺ started weeping. When I again went to him the next day, he said, 'Even today I felt the grief I feel when I saw you yesterday.'" Hadhrat Khaalid bin Shumayr (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Zaid bin Haaritha was martyred and Rasulullaah ﷺ went to the Sahabah Hadhrat Zaid (RA)'s daughter burst out crying in front of Rasulullaah , When Rasulullaah iiii then started weeping profusely, Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah asked, "What is this, O Rasulullaah ﷺ "This," replied Rasulullaah ﷺ, "is the longing a friend has for his friend."
Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ kissed Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon after his demise, his eyes were flowing with tears.

Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Hadhrat Haaritha bin Suraaqa (RA) was killed during the Battle of Badr. Although he was a non-combatant, he was killed by a stray arrow. His mother came there asking, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Tell me what has become of Haaritha. If he is in Jannah, I shall exercise patience. If not, I shall show Allaah what I will do." She was referring to wailing, which had not yet been forbidden at the time. "Shame on you!" Rasulullaah ilii exclaimed, "Are you mad? There are eight levels of Jannah and your son had reached Firdous which is the highest of them all."
sources: Bayhaqi (Vol.9 Pg.167). Ibn Abi Shaybah has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.273). Haakim (Vo!,3 Pg.208) and lbn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.68) have also reported a similar narration.

paras: Another narration states that she said, "I shall exercise patience if he is Jannah. If not, I shall exert myself in oying." "O Ummu Haaritha!" Rasulullaah ﷺ consoled her, "There are many levels of Jannah and your son had reached Firdous which is the highest of them all." Yet another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Ummu Haaritha! There is not only one Jannah. There are many levels of Jannah and he is in Firdous which is the highest of them all." She then said, "I shall then exercise patience."
sources: Tabraani, as quoted in Kanzul Pg.275).
Ibn Najjaar, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.26).

paras: Another narration from Hadhrat Anas (RA) states that Hadhrat Ummu Haaritha said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ if he is in Jannah, I shall not weep and will not be grieved. However, if he is in Jahannam, I shall continue weeping as long as I live." "O Ummu Haarith!" Rasulullaah ﷺ consoled her, "There is not only one Jannah. There are many levels of Jannah and Haarith is in Firdous which is the highest of them all." She then returned laughing as she said, "Well done, Haarith! Well done!"

Hadhrat Muhammad bin Thaabit bin Qais bin Shammaas narrates that when the Muslims fought the (Jewish) Banu Qurayzah tribe, a man from the Ansaar called Khallaad was martyred. When someone went to inform her that he had been martyred, she went (to receive his body) while wearing her veil. Someone remarked, "Khallaad has been killed and you are wearing a veil?!" She replied, "I may have lost Khallaad but I have not lost my modesty." When Rasulullaah ﷺ was informed of this, he said, "Take note that he (Hadhrat Khallaad shall receive the rewards of two martyrs." When someone asked the reason for this, Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Because he was killed by the Ahlul Kitaab."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.83). Abu Nu'aym has also reported the narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (vol.2 Pg.157), as hasAbuYa'la, as quoted in isaabah (Vol.1 Pg.454).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that (his mother) Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) once came to his father Abu Anas saying, "Today I have come with news that you will dislike." His response was: "You are always coming with news from that Bedouin that I dislike." She said, "He is a Bedouin whom Allaah has selected and made a Nabi." "What is the news you have brought?" he asked. "Wine has been forbidden," she replied. To this he said, "Then this is where we separate." He then died as a Mushrik.

When Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) approached Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) (with a marriage proposal), she said, "I cannot marry you when you are a Mushrik." "No," exclaimed Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA), "By Allaah! That is not your motive." "Then what is my motive?" asked Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA). 'Your motive is gold and silver," he replied. "In that case," retorted Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym "I make you and the Nabi of Allaah witness to the fact that if you accept Islaam, I shall be content with you giving me only your acceptance of Islaam (as dowry. I want nothing else)." "Who will stand guarantee for me to this agreement?" Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) asked. Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) then said, "O Anas! Get up and go with your uncle."

Hadhrat Anas (RA) got up and with Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA)'s hand on his shoulder, they proceeded. When they got close to where Rasulullaah ﷺ was and he heard their voices, he remarked, "Here is Abu Talha with the radiance of Islaam sparkling between his eyes." Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) greeted Rasulullaah ﷺ and then professed: I testify that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah and that Muhammad ﷺ is the Rasul of Allaah Rasulullaah ﷺ then married him (to Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA)) on the condition of his accepting islaam. Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) later fathered a son who was the apple of his father's eye. However, when the child started to walk, Allaah decided to take the child away.

(Still unaware that the child had passed away) Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) came to Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) asking, "How is my son, O Ummu Sulaym?" "Better then he had been (because death har relieved him of his illness)," she replied. She then said further,. "Why don't you have your supper because it is already late." After serving him his supper, she asked, "O Abu Talha! When a trust is given to some people for safekeeping and the owners of the trust send a message after some time that they require it back, can those who have it in trust refuse to return it?" "Not at all," replied Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA). Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym then said, "Your son has left this world." "Where is he now?" Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) asked. When she informed him that the child was in the inner room, Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) went there, opened the face and recited: "To Allaah we belong and to Him shall we return" He then went to inform Rasulullaah ﷺ about the statement of Hadhrat ummu Sulaym, to which Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I swear by the Being Who has sent me with the truth that because of her patience at the demise of her child, Allaah has already placed another son in her womb."

After Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) had delivered the child, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Anas! Go and, tell your mother that after cutting the umbilical cord, she should not feed anything to. the baby without first sending for me." Hadhrat Anas says, "She then gave the baby in my arms and I took it to Rasulullaah When I placed the baby before Rasulullaah ﷺ, he asked for three Ajwa dates. When I brought them, he removed the stones, chewed on them and then opened the child's mouth to place it inside. The child immediately started turning it about in his mouth, to which Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, 'The Ansaar certainly love dates.' Thereafter, Rasulullaah ﷺ said to me, 'Go and tell your mother, 'May Allaah bless you in this child and make him obedient and pious.
sources: Bazzaar. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.291) has commented on the chain of narrators. Another narration of Bazzaar states that Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) said to Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA), "How can 1 marry you when you worship the wood which that slave of mine brings?" ibn Sa'd (Vol.8 Pg.316) has reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA)'s son was ill and passed away one day when he was out. When he returned, Hadhrat Abu Talha asked, "How is my son?" Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) replied, "He is calmer than he had been." She then served him supper and after he had completed, the couple engaged in sexual relations.. It was only afterwards that she told him to bury the child. The next morning when Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) informed Rasulullaah ﷺ about what had happened, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "Did you have relations with your wife last night?" After receiving a positive reply, Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed, "O Allaah! Bless them." Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) then gave birth to a son.

Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) then instructed Hadhrat Anas (RA) to carefully take this child to Rasulullaah ﷺ . Ummu Sulaym also sent some dates with the baby and when Rasulullaah ﷺ took the child, he asked, "Has something come with him?" When the Sahabah (RA) informed him that some dates had also come, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked for them. After chewing them, Rasulullaah took it from his mouth, placed it in the child's mouth and rubbed it on the child's palate (called Tahneek). Rasulullaah ﷺ then named the child Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Allaah shall bless them in their night." Hadhrat Sufyaan reports that a man from the Ansaar mentioned, "I saw nine of their (Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Talha children all of whom were proficient scholars of the Qur'aan."
sources: Bukhaari (Vol.2 Pg.822).

paras: Hadhrat Qaasim bin Muhammad narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) the son of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was struck by an arrow in the battle for Taa'if. (After healing) His wound reopened forty days after the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ, causing him to pass away. When he went to (his daughter) Hadhrat Aa'isha Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "Dear daughter! By Allaah! It seems as if a goat was pulled by the ear and removed from our house." She said, "All praise belongs to Allaah who has strengthened your heart and kept you firm on what is right." After leaving, he again came to her saying, "Dear daughter! Are you not afraid that Abdullaah may have been buried while he was still alive?" Hadhrat Aa'isha declared, "Dear father!

To Allaah we belong and to Him shall we return." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then said, "I seek protection from Allaah the All Hearing and All Knowing from the accursed Shaytaan! Dear daughter! Each and every person has influences. One comes from an angel and the other from Shaytaan."

When a delegation from the Thaqeef tribe (the people of Taa'if) came to Hadhrat Abu Bakr, he still had with him the arrow (that killed his son). Taking it out, he asked them, "Does any of you recognise this arrow?" Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubayd of the Banu Ajlaan tribe replied, "It is I who made that arrow, who attached its feathers and head and who shot it." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "It was this arrow that killed my son Abdullaah. All praise belongs to that Allaah Who honoured him (with martyrdom) at your hand and Who did not disgrace you (with death as a Kaafir) at his hand. Allaah is indeed the greatest Protector."
sources: Bukhaari (Vol.1 Pg.174).

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "The good that Allaah grants is indeed vast to both of you."

Hadhrat Amr bin Sa'eed (RA) narrates that whenever a child was born to Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), he would ask for the child while it was still wrapped (after birth). He would then smell the child. When asked why he did this, Hadhrat Uthmaan replied, "I like to do this because should anything happen to the child, there would be love for the child in my heart (I would then be rewarded for the greater patience I would need to exercise)." Someone once said to Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA), "None of your children seem to stay alive?" Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) replied, "All praise belongs to Allaah Who takes them away from this temporary home (this world) and stores them as a treasure (for me) in the eternal abode (of the Aakhirah)."
sources: lbn Sa'd, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.157).
Abu Nu'aym, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg. 1 57).

paras: Hadhrat Umar bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Zaid bin Khattaab narrates that whenever a calamity befell Hadhrat Umar (RA), he would console himself saying, "When I was struck with the calamity of the death of (my brother) Zaid bin Khattaab, I managed to exercise patience (why should I not do so now?)." When Hadhrat Umar one day saw the person who killed his brother Hadhrat Zaid he said to him, "It is a pity that you killed my brother. I think of him every time the wind blows."
sources: Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.227), Bayhaqi (Vol.9 Pg.98).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Hamzah was martyred, (his sister) Hadhrat Safiyyah (RA), unaware of what had happened, came looking for him. When she met (her nephew) Hadhrat Ali (RA) and (her son) Hadhrat Zubayr (RA), Hadhrat Ali (RA) said to Hadhrat Zubayr "Tell your mother (that her brother has been martyred)." "No," replied Hadhrat Zubayr (RA), "You go ahead and tell your aunt." "How is Hamzah?" Hadhrat Safiyyah (RA) asked. The two men made it seem to her that they knew nothing. She then approached (her nephew) Rasulullaah ﷺ who said, "I fear for her sanity (if she knew the truth)." Rasulullaah ﷺ placed his hand on her chest and made du'aa. (Then when he informed her) She wept as she said: To Allaah we belong and to Him shall we return."

Rasulullaah ﷺ then stood by the mutilated body and said, "If it were not for the grief it would cause our women, I would not bury him and would leave him in this condition so that Allaah would resurrect him from the bellies of wild animals and birds of prey." Thereafter Rasulullaah ﷺ gave instructions for all the martyrs to be brought forward and he started performing the Janaazah salaah for them. Nine bodies were brought and laid beside that of Hadhrat Hamzah Rasulullaah ﷺ performed the salaah with seven Takbeers. The bodies were then taken away while that of Hadhrat Hamzah (RA) was left. Thereafter, another nine bodies were brought and Rasulullaah ﷺ performed the Janaazah salaah for them with seven Takbeers. These bodies were then carried away while that of Hadhrat Hamzah (RA) was left behind. Yet again, another nine bodies were brought and Rasulullaah ﷺ performed the Janaazah salaah for them also with seven Takbeers. These bodies were then carried away while that of Hadhrat Hamzah was left behind. This continued until Rasulullaah ﷺ had performed the Janaazah salaah for them all.
sources: Haakim (Vol, 3 Pg.197). lbn Abi Shaybah and Tabraani have reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA), as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaai (Vol.5 Pg.170). Bazzaar has also reported a similar narration, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.6 Pg.l 18).

paras: Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awaam (RA) narrates, "A woman came running during the Battle of Uhud and would have seen the dead bodies when Rasulullaah ﷺ called out, '(Stop) The woman! (Stop) The woman!' Rasulullaah ﷺ disliked that women should see the bodies. When I guessed that she was my mother Safiyya I ran to her and reached her before she could reach the dead. She was a strong woman and struck me in the chest saying, 'Get away from me. The ground does not belong to you!' I said, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ has emphatically prohibited you form going there.' She then halted in her tracks and took out two sheets saying, 'I have brought these two sheets for my brother Hamzah. The news of his death has already reached me and I want you to bury him in these.'

We then took the sheets to enshroud Hamzah in but found next to him someone from the Ansaar who was also killed and mutilated as Hamzah was. Because we felt difficult to enshroud Hamzah in two sheets while the Ansaari had none, we decided that one sheet would be used for Hamzah and the other for the Ansaari. After measuring the two sheets, we found the one to be larger than the other. (To decide who would have which sheet) We then drew lots between the two and enshrouded each one in the sheet that fell to his lot." Discussing the martyrdom of Hadhrat Hamzah (RA), it is reported that when Hadhrat Safiyyah bint Abdul Muttalib (RA) came to see her brother, Hadhrat Zubayr met her saying, "Dear mother! It is the instruction of Rasulullaah that you return." She said, "Why should I? I have already heard that my brother's body has been mutilated. This has taken place for the sake of Allaah and we are pleased with it (with Allaah's decree). I shall definitely exercise patience and look forward to the rewards from Allaah." When Hadhrat Zubayr reported her words to Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Let her go." She then went to the body of Hadhrat Hamzah (RA) and prayed for his forgiveness. Rasulullaah ﷺ then gave instructions for him to be buried.
sources: Bazzaar, Ahmad and Abu Yala. Haythami (Vol.6 Pg.l 18) has commented on the chain of narrators. (3) lbn Is'haaq, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol,4 Pg.349).

paras: Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) says, "(My husband) Abu Salamah once came to me from Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, 'I have heard from Rasulullaah ﷺ something that gives me great pleasure. Rasulullaah iii said that whenever a Muslim is afflicted with any calamity, he will be rewarded and granted something better in return if he recites: 'To Allaah we belong and to Him shall we return' followed by the du'aa: 'O Allaah! Reward me in my calamity and replace me with something better I learnt the du'aa from him and when Abu Salamah passed away, I recited: 'To Allaah we belong and to Him shall we return.'

'O Allaah! Reward me in my calamity and replace me with something better' I then thought to myself, 'Where will I get someone better than Abu Salamah However, after completing my Iddah, I was one day dying a piece of leather when Rasulullaah ﷺ sought permission to see me. After washing the Qaridh leaves (used for dying) from my hands, I permitted him in and placed for him a leather cushion stuffed with the bark of a palm. Rasulullaah ﷺ sat on it and then proposed for my hand in marriage. After Rasulullaah ﷺ had spoken, I said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ I have no reason for not wanting to marry you. However, 1 am a woman who is extremely possessive and I fear that you may see something in me (because of my possessiveness) that would cause Allaah to punish me. in addition to this, I am not young anymore and I have children.' Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'As for your possessiveness, Allaah will soon dispel it. As for your age, I am affected by advanced age just as you are. As for your children, they shall be my children as well.' I then accepted, saying, 'I shall then hand myself over to the Rasool of Allaah Allaah really did replace Abu Salamah for me with someone better, with Rasulullaah ﷺ ."
sources: Ahmad, Nasa'ee, Ibn Maajah and Tirmidhi, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol. 4 Pg.91). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.8 Pg.63,64) has reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says that they were returning from Hajj or Umrah and were welcomed at Dhul Hulayfah where the children of the Ansaar normally met their families. When the people met Hadhrat Usayd bin. Hudhayr (RA) and gave him the news of his wife's death, he covered his face and started to weep. "May Allaah forgive you," Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said to him, "You are a companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ and are one of the first people to enter the fold of Islaam. Why would you be weeping over a woman?" Hadhrat usayd (RA) uncovered his face and said, "You are right. I swear by my life that after the death of Sa'd bin Mu'aadh, I have no right to weep over anyone else especially after what Rasulullaah ﷺ said about him." "What did Rasulullaah illf say about him?" Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) asked. Hadhrat Usayd (RA) then informed her that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "The Arsh (Throne of Allaah) actually shook at the death of Sa'd bin Mu'aadh." Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "At that time, Usayd bin Hudhayr was walking between Rasulullaah ﷺ and I."
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Shaashi and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Voi.7 Pg.42). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.12) and Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.289) have reported a similar narration. Abu Nu'aym, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.l 18).

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Usayd bin Hudhayr (RA) said, "Have I no right to weep when I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, The pillars of the Arsh shook with the death of Sa'd bin Muaa'dh." ^ Yet another narration states that he said, "Why should I not weep when I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say..." The rest of the narration is the same as the one above.
sources: Tabraani, as quoted in Majtm'uz Zawaa'id ' (Vol.9 Pg.309).

paras: Hadhrat Awn reports that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) heard about the death of his brother, Hadhrat Utba (RA), he started to weep. When asked what made him weep, he replied, "He was my real brother and my companion with Rasulullaah ﷺ. However, despite this, I would not have liked to die before him because for him to pass away and for me to anticipate the rewards for (my patience at) losing him is dearer to me than for me to pass away and for him to anticipate the rewards for (his patience at) losing me."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hitya (Vol.4 Pg.253).

paras: Hadhrat Khaythama (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood 'received the news of the death of his brother Hadhrat utba (RA), his eyes welled with tears as he said, "This (weeping) is because of the mercy that Allaah has placed (in the heart) that man has no control of."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.94).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Saleet (RA) narrates, "I saw Abu Ahmad bin Jahash carrying the funeral bier of (his sister) Zaynab bint Jahash. He was blind and in tears. As the people started crowding about the bier, I heard Hadhrat Umar say, 'O Abu Ahmad t! Move away from the bier so the people will not hurt you.' However, Abu Ahmad replied, 'O Umar! It is from her that I received every good. This (carrying her bier) cools the heat of the grief I am feeling.' 'Then hold on tight,' Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, 'Hold on tight.
sources: ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.19), as quoted in Kanzul L/mmaaWoU Pg.67). Tabraani has reported a similar narration but Haythami (Vol.5 Pg.196) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Ahnaf bin Qais (RA) says, "I once heard Hadhrat umar (RA) say, 'The Quraysh are leaders and when any of them enter a door, an entire group of people enter with them.' I however did not fully understand what he meant until he was stabbed. On his deathbed, he instructed Suhayb to lead the salaah for three days and also gave instructions for food to be served to the people until his successor was appointed. When the people returned from the funeral, the food was served and the tablecloths laid out. However, because of their grief, the people refrained from eating. Hadhrat Abbaas bin Abdul Muttalib (RA) then said, 'O people! We ate and drank after the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ and we also ate and drank after the demise of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). Now it is also necessary for us to eat this food." He then stretched out his hand and ate. The people followed suit. I then understood what Hadhrat umar (RA) said about the Quraysh being leaders."
sources: Ibn Abi Khaythamah, Deenowri and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal(yol,8 Pg. 122).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Uyaynah Sftgtg reports thatwhen Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) consoled a person, he said, "There is no calamity when there is patience and no benefit when there is impatience. What precedes death is simple while that which follows it is difficult. If you think of the loss of Rasulullaah ﷺ, your tragedy will seem light and Allaah will inflate your reward."
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.l22).

paras: Hadhrat Sufyaan reports that when consoling Hadhrat Ash'ath bin Qais HIS! upon the death of his son, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "It is the right of your family relationship that you should grieve but if you exercise patience, Allaah shall replace the loss of your son. If you are patient, fate will take its course and you will be rewarded. However, if you are irritated, fate will still take its course and you will be sinful."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once in Makkah when a woman from the Ansaar came to him saying, "O Rasulullaah There is this wretch (evil spirit) that overpowers me (please cure me)." Rasulullaah ﷺ said to her, "If you persevere with this problem, you will appear on the Day of Qiyaamah without any sins and will have no reckoning to give." She replied, "I swear by the Being Who has sent you with the truth, I prefer to persevere until I meet Allaah." She then added, "However, I fear that the wretch would strip me naked." Rasulullaah ffiillf then prayed for her and whenever she feared that the spirit was approaching, she would cling on to the shroud of the Kabah and say to it, "Get away!" It would then leave her.
sources: Ahmad, Bukhaari and Muslim.

paras: Hadhrat Ataa (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) once said to him, "Should I not show you a woman who shall be amongst the inhabitants of Jannah?" "Please do," Hadhrat Ataa (RA) responded. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas then said, "There was this black woman who once approached Rasulullaah ilii with the request, 'Please pray for me because I suffer from epilepsy and (in the fit my clothing opens up and) my body becomes exposed.' Rasulullaah ﷺ said to her, 'If you want,, you can persevere and earn yourself Jannah, otherwise I can pray to Allaah to cure you.' 'Not at all,' she replied, 'I shall rather persevere (and be assured of Jannah), but do pray to Allaah that my body does not become exposed.' Rasulullaah ﷺ then made du'aa for her. Another narration adds that Hadhrat Ataa (RA) then saw the lady holding on to- the shroud of the Kabah. She was called Ummu Zufar and she was a tall black woman.
sources: Bukhaari, as quoted in wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.160),

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mughaffal (RA) narrates that a woman who had been a prostitute during the Period of Ignorance once passed by a man who stretched out his hand towards her. "Stop!" she cautioned, "Allaah has obliterated Shirk and brought Islaam (I am therefore no longer a prostitute)." He then left her and turned away. However, as he continued looking at her, he struck his face on a wall (and was injured). He then went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and reported the incident to him. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "You are a person for whom Allaah intends good. When Allaah had good intentions for a person, He hastens the punishment for his sins in this world (so that he suffers no punishment in the Aakhirah). On the other hand, when Allaah does not intend good for a person, He holds back the punishment (in this world) until the person receives his punishment in full on the Day of Qiyaamah (when the punishment will be much worse)." The statement of Hadhrat llmar (RA) that everything which Affects a Mu'min is a Calamity if he does not Like it Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Khalifah narrates that he was once with Hadhrat Umar when the strap of his sandal broke. Hadhrat Umar (RA) recited: "To Allaah we belong and to Him shall we return" Thereafter (to explain why he said this), Hadhrat Umar IS said, "Everything that is unpleasant to you is regarded as a calamity." {,) Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates that when the front portion of Hadhrat Umar's shoe broke, he exclaimed: "To Allaah we belong and to Him shall we return" "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" the people enquired, "You are reciting (} for a mere front portion of a shoe?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "When anything that he finds unpleasant happens to a Mu'min, it is regarded as a calamity."
sources: Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Vmmaal '(Vol.2 Pg.l5S).

paras: Hadhrat Aslam reports that Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) once wrote to Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab, informing him that the Romans were launching a massive military offensive and also stating the grave dangers they (the Muslim army) faced. In his reply after duly praising Allaah, Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote, "Whenever any difficulty afflicts a Mu'min, Allaah creates ease afterwards and no difficulty can overpower two. Allaah states in His book: O you who have Imaan! Exercise sabr, compete in patience, continue doing good deeds (especially ensuring that the borders of Muslim countries are well guarded) and fear Allaah so that you may be successful (in reaching your goal)., Aal imraan, verse
sources: Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Mundhir and Bayhaqi.

paras: Hadhrat (RA) Mahdi says that Hadhrat Uthmaan Sftsfflgi possessed two virtues that neither Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) nor Hadhrat Umar (RA) had. One was his perseverance until it led to his martyrdom and the other was that he united the Muslims on one standard version of the Qur'aan.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.58).

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once left the Masjid and headed for his room on the upper storey. After entering, he faced towards the Qiblah and fell into Sajdah. He prolonged his Sajdah so much that I thought his soul had been taken. I therefore went close to him and sat down. Raising his head from the ground, he asked, "Who is there?' When I told him that I was Abdur Rahmaan, he asked further, 'What is the matter?' 'O Rasulullaah !' I explained, 'You Sajdah was so long that I feared Allaah may have taken your soul in it.' Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Jibra'eel just came to me saying that Allaah says, 'Whoever invokes My mercy on you (recites, I shall shower My mercies on him and whoever invoked peace on you (sends Salaams), I shall bless him with peace.1 I therefore made Sajdah to Allaah in gratitude.".
sources: Ahmad, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.287).

paras: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) says, "I once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ and found him standing and performing salaah. He continued standing until dawn broke and made such a long Sajdah that 1 thought his life had been taken. Afterwards he asked, 'Do you know what that (long Sajdah) was for?' 'Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ know best,' I submitted. After repeating the question three or four times, Rasulullaah ﷺ explained, 'I performed as much salaah as my Rabb had ordained for me when my Rabb appeared and addressed me. At the end of the conversation, he asked me, 'What shall I do with your Ummah?' 'O my Rabb,' I declared, 'you know best what You shall do with them.' After repeating the question three or four times, Allaah again asked, 'What shall I do with your Ummah?' When I again submitted that He knew best, Allaah said, 'I shall never make you grieve over your ummah.' I then fell into Sajdah because my Rabb is appreciative and loves those who show gratitude.'
sources: Tabraarti. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.288) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan Abu Bakr (RA) narrates that when he once went to visit Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah ﷺ was busy receiving revelation. When the revelation stopped. Rasulullaah ﷺ asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) to pass him his shawl. He then left the house and entered the Masjid where he found some people besides whom there was no one else there. Rasulullaah ﷺ sat on one side until the person addressing them had completed his talk. Thereafter.

Rasulullaah ﷺ recited Surah Tanzeel Sajdah (Surah) and made such a long Sajdah that people living as far as two miles away arrived there as people started telling each other about the Sajdah. Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) sent a message to her family telling them to come because she was seeing Rasulullaah ﷺ do something she had never seen him do before.

After Rasulullaah ﷺ had lifted his head (from Sajdah), Hadhrat Abu Bakr asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ You prolonged your Sajdah so much?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "I prostrated to my Rabb out of gratitude for the Ummah He has granted me. There shall be seventy thousand of them who shall enter Jannah without reckoning." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ You have an Ummah that is large and extremely pure. You should have asked for more for them." This he repeated two or three times when Hadhrat Umar (RA) added, "May my parents be sacrificed for you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ You have asked a great gift for your Ummah."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.289) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once passed by a man suffering from a terminal disease, he dismounted from his animal and made Sajdah. when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) passed by the man, he also dismounted and made Sajdah and Hadhrat Umar (RA) followed suit when he passed by.

Hadhrat Ali (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched an expedition comprising of his family members, he prayed, "O Allaah! If You return them to me safely, I owe it to You to thank You as You ought to be thanked." It was not long afterwards that they came back safely and Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "All praise belongs to Allaah for all the bounties of Allaah." "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Ali (RA) asked, "Did you not say that if Allaah returned them safely, you owed it to Him to thank Him as He ought to be thanked?" "Did I not just do that?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied.
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.289) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when a beggar once came to Rasulullaah he gave instructions for a date to be given to the man. The beggar however (thinking it to be too little) threw it away.
