Another beggar then arrived and again Rasulullaah gpi? gave instructions for a date to be given to him. The man exclaimed (in joy), "Subhaanallaah! A date from Rasulullaah ﷺ Rasulullaah then said to one of the servants, "Go to Ummu Salamah and instruct her to give this man the forty Dirhams she has with her."

Hadhrat Hasan narrates that when a beggar once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and he gave him a date, the beggar exclaimed (in derision), "Subhaanallaah! A Nabi from the Ambiyaa giving a mere date as Sadaqah!" Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "Don't you know that there are multitudes of atoms in that' Thereafter, another man came to beg. When Rasulullaah ﷺ gave him a date as well, he exclaimed (in joy), "A date from a Nabi from the Ambiyaa! I shall never part with this date as long as I live and shall always anticipate its blessings." Rasulullaah then instructed the people to be good to the man and he soon became a wealthy man.

Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Yasaar narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) once passed by a place called Dajnaan, he said, "I once saw myself grazing animals in this place for (my father) Khattaab. By Allaah! As far as I know, he was a stern and harsh man. (By the grace of Allaah) I then became the guide of the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ He then recited the following couplets (which mean): "There is nothing in the things you see besides superficial enjoyment While wealth and children are temporary, all that shall remain is Allaah" He then spurred his camel on saying, "Howbr"
sources: Here Rasulullaah ﷺ was referring to the verse of the Qur'aan that states: Whoever (sincerely) does an atom's weight of good will see it (its consequences when he is rewarded for it). Zilzaal, verse

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "When I come to the conveyance of gratitude and the conveyance of patience, I care not which of the two I ride."
sources: Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.42).

paras: Hadhrat Ikramah (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once passed by a leper who was also blind, deaf and dumb. Addressing the people with him, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "Do you see any of Allaah's bounties in this man?" When the people replied that they saw none, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Why not? Do you not see that he is able to urinate with ease without the urine holding back or coming out with difficulty? This is and extremely great bounty from Allaah."
sources: Ibn Sa'd and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal Pg.4 1 7).

paras: Hadhrat ibraheem reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once heard a man say, "O Allaah! I wish to spend my wealth and my life in Your path.". To this, Hadhrat Umar said, "why doesn't any of you remain silent, exercising patience when in difficulty and expressing gratitude when enjoying prosperity?"
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.l'54). .

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that after a man greeted Hadhrat Umar (RA) and he had replied to the greeting, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked him, "How are you?" "I only have the praises of Allaah to sing before you," the man replied. "That is exactly what I wanted from you," said Hadhrat Umar (RA) Hadhrat Hasan Basri narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote the following letter to Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) "Be content with the sustenance Allaah provides for you in this world because Allaah gives more sustenance to some of His servants and less to others to test all of them. He tests those whom He has given plenty to see whether they are grateful. His gratitude to Allaah fulfils the duty he owes to Allaah for the sustenance and bounties Allaah has blessed him with."
sources: Maalik, Ibn Mubaarak and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 2 Pg.151).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "The grateful ones always received more from Allaah so seek more from Allaah. This is because Allaah says: If you show gratitude (for the favours I grant you), then I will definitely grant you (many) more." (Surah ibraheem, verse 7)
sources: Ibn Haatim, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.151).

paras: Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Moosa narrates that Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) was once called to deal with some people who were involved in some evil activity. However, when Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) went to them, he found that they had already dispersed even though the effects of their evil was still visible. Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) praised Allaah for not encountering them and (as a token of gratitude) he freed a slave.
sources: Deenowri, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol.2 Pg. 151).

paras: Hadhrat Ali is once said, "Every bounty should be followed by gratitude and gratitude is followed by an increase (in the bounty). Gratitude and an increase in bounties are directly proportional to each other. Therefore, Allaah will never stop increasing the bounties on His servant until the servant stops being grateful (in which case they stop)." (,)

Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi narrates that Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib once said, "It never occurs that Allaah opens the door of gratitude and closes the door of increasing bounties. It also never occurs that Allaah opens the door of du'aa and closes the door of acceptance. Similarly, it never occurs that Allaah opens the door of Taubah and closes the door of forgiveness. I shall recite this from Allaah's Book. Allaah says: "Supplicate (make du'aa) to Me and I shall respond." (Surah Al Mumin, verse 60) Allaah also says: "If you show gratitude (for the favours I grant you), then I will definitely grant you (many) more." (Surah ibraheem, verse 7) Allaah says further: "So think of Me and I will think of you." (Surah Baqarah, verse Allaah also says: Whoever commits a (minor) sin or wrongs himself (by committing a major sin) and then seeks Allaah's forgiveness, he will surely find that Allaah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful." (Surah Nisaa, verse 1 10)
sources: Bayhaqi. (2) lbn Maajah and Askari, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.151), (3) lbn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaai (Vol.2 Pg.152) and Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pgs.2 10,220).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "When a night or a day passes without people seeing me suffer any difficulty, I see this as an extremely great bounty from Allaah." Another narration quotes him as saying, "The person who sees Allaah's bounties only in food and drink has a limited understanding and has his punishment ever present,"

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) once said, "Gratitude is binding on the person who drinks even plain water that enters his body without difficulty and then exits without difficulty." When (her son) Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) was martyred, Hadhrat Asmaa bint Abu Bakr happened to lose something that Rasulullaah ﷺ gave her and which she kept in a bag. When she finally found it after some searching, she fell into Sajdah (in gratitude to Allaah).
sources: Ibn Abi Durtya, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.152).
Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.290) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that when the Muslims went for the Battle of Badr, every three of them had to share a camel (to ride in turns because of a shortage of transport), Hadhrat Abu Lubaabah (RA) and Hadhrat shared a camel with Rasulullaah (giif and when it was Rasulullaah ' mi's turn to walk, they both offered to walk instead. However, Rasulullaah ﷺ refused saying, "Neither are you two stronger than I nor am I less in need of rewards than you."
sources: Ah and Nasa'ee, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.3, Bazzaar has also reported the narration, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.6 Pg.69).

paras: Hadhrat Muttalib bin Abu Wadaa'ah (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once saw a person performing salaah while sitting down, he said, "The salaah of a sitting person is half (in reward) of the salaah of a standing person." Thereafter the Sahabah (RA) exerted themselves greatly to perform salaah while standing (despite suffering extreme hunger and weakness at times).
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.150) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived in Madinah, he was suffering with high fever and the other Muslims were also suffering of the same, when Rasulullaah ﷺ entered the Masjid one day and found the people sitting and performing salaah (because of their illness), he said, "The salaah of a sitting person is half (in reward) of the salaah of a standing person." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas narrates that when Rasulullaah and his companions (from Makkah) arrived in Madinah, they were so afflicted by the fever in Madinah that they became extremely ill. Eventually they were able to perform salaah only while sitting down. Allaah however, cured Rasulullaah ﷺ from the condition, when Rasulullaah ﷺ left his room one day and found the Sahabah (RA) sitting and performing salaah, he said, "Take note that the salaah of a sitting person is half (in reward) of the salaah of a standing person." Thereafter the Sahabah (RA) exerted themselves greatly to perform salaah while standing despite their extreme weakness and illness solely in aspiration for the additional rewards.
sources: lbn Is'haaq, as quoted in wan Nihaayah (Vol.3 Pg.224).

paras: Hadhrat Rabaa'ah bin Ka'b (RA) says, "I was Rasulullaah ﷺ's servant and served him all day until he performed the Isha salaah. I would then sit by his door when he entered his room saying to myself, 'Perhaps Rasulullaah ﷺ will need something.' I would then remain sitting there hearing Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Subhaanallaahi wa Bi-hamdihi,' until I would get tired or until my eyes overwhelmed me and I would fall asleep right there. Seeing my fervour to serve him and feeling that he owed something to me, Rasulullaah ﷺ one day asked me, 'O Rabaa'ah bin Ka'b! Ask from me and I shall give you.' 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ !' I submitted, 'Allow me to think about it and then I shall inform you.' I then addressed myself saying, 'The things of this world are temporary and will soon come to an end. In any case, I have my (preordained) sustenance in this world which is sufficient for me and will come to me (it is therefore futile to ask Rasulullaah ﷺ for some worldly thing). I shall therefore ask Rasulullaah ﷺ for something of benefit for my life in the Aakhirah because he enjoys an exalted status with Allaah.' I then approached Rasulullaah ﷺ and he asked, have you decided, O Rabee'ah?' 'I have made a decision, O Rasulullaah ﷺ I said, 'My request to you is to intercede on my behalf that Allaah frees me from Jahannam.' Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, 'Who told you to say this, O Rabee'ah?' I explained to him saying, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ I swear by the Being Who has sent you with the truth that no one told me what to say. You asked me to ask from you and because you enjoy a high status in Allaah's sight, I though the matter over. Realising that the things of this world are temporary and will soon come to an end and that 1 have my (preordained) sustenance in this world which will come to me I decided to ask you for something of benefit for my life in the Aakhirah.' Rasulullaah ﷺ remained silent for a long while after which he said, 'I shall do that but do assist me against your carnal self by making Sajdah in abundance.'

In another narration, Hadhrat Rabee'ah (RA) says, "I used to spend the night in the service of Rasulullaah ﷺ , bringing him his water for wudhu and seeing to his other needs. When he once asked me to make a request, I said, 'I request your company in Jannah.' 'Anything else?' he asked. When I insisted that this was all, he said, 'Then assist me against your carnal self by making Sajdah in abundance.
sources: Ahmad, as quoted in wan Nihaayah (Vol.5 Pg.335). Tabraani, Muslim and Abu Dawood have reported a similar narration in brief.

paras: Hadhrat Abdul jabbaar bin Haarith bin Maallk Hadasi Manaari narrates, "I was part of a delegation to Rasulullaah ﷺ from the land of Saraat. When I came to Rasulullaah ﷺ, I greeted him with the traditional Arab greeting saying, 'May you have a good morning!' Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Allaah has given Muhammad ﷺ and his ummah another greeting. They greet each other with the words of Salaam.' I then said: 'Jbi ii '. Rasulullaah ﷺ replied by saying, '. When he asked what my name was, I informed him that I was Jabbaar bin Haarith. I then accepted Islaam and pledge my allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ. After I had pledge my allegiance someone said to Rasulullaah 'This Manaari is one of the accomplished horsemen of his tribe. Rasulullaah ﷺ then gave me a horse and I remained fighting by his side. When Rasulullaah ﷺ one day missed the neighing of the horse he had given me, he asked, 'Why do I not hear the neighing of the Hadasi's horse?' 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ I explained, 'I was told that its neighing was disturbing you so I had it castrated (to quieten it).' It was then that Rasulullaah ﷺ forbade castrating horses. Someone once suggested to me to request Rasulullaah ﷺ for a note (of guaranteeing for something) as my cousin Tameem Daari had done. 'Did he ask for something of this world or for something of the Aakhirah?' I asked. When I was told that it was for something of this world, I said, 'It was from this world that I have turned away. I shall rather ask Rasulullaah ﷺ to assist me tomorrow when I appear before Allaah.
sources: Ibn Mandah and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.2 15).

paras: Hadhrat Amr bin Taghlib (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ gave something to some people and not to others, it appeared as if they were upset. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "I give to some people only for fear of their impatience and agitation. Then there are those whom I hand over to the goodness and independence Allaah has placed in their hearts. Amongst these people is Amr bin Taghlib." Hadhrat Amr bin Taghlib (RA) said, "I would not trade these words of Rasulullaah ﷺ even for red camels." !2)

Hadhrat Amr bin Hammaad reports that Hadhrat Ali (RA) and Hadhrat Umar were leaving from performing Tawaaf when they saw a Bedouin carrying his mother on his back reciting the following couplets (which mean): "I am her conveyance that never bolts and when other conveyances become crazed, I shall not She did more when she carried me and suckled me"

He then called out, "ii " Addressing Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat All said, "O Abu Hafs! Let us go back to perform Tawaaf so that the mercy descending (on the Bedouin) may encompass us as well." They then started performing Tawaaf as the Bedouin repeated: "I am her conveyance that never bolts and when other conveyances become crazed, I shall not She did more when she carried me and suckled me (At your service, O Allaah, I am at your service)"
At the same time, Hadhrat Ali (RA) reciting the following couplets (which mean): "Allaah is Most Appreciative if you care for your mother He shall then grant you in abundance for your little effort

Hadhrat Maymoon bin Mahraan reports that people from Haroora who were associated with Najdah (one of the leaders of the Khawaarij) once passed by a camel belonging to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) and took it along with them. The shepherd tending to it went to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) saying, "O Abu Abdur Look forward to the rewards for your camel." "What has happened to her?" asked Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA). The shepherd replied, "The people from Haroora who are associated with Najdah passed by and took her along with them." "But how," Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) asked, "did they take the camel away and leave you alone?" "They took me along as well but I managed to escape from them," the shepherd replied.

Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) asked him further, "What made you leave them and come to me (when you would no longer be a slave if you escaped)?" "Because I love you more than them," the man replied. Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) then enquired, "Will you swear by the Being besides Whom there is no god that you love me more than them?" When the shepherd swore on oath, Hadhrat Abdullaah said, "Then I look forward to the reward for (freeing) you together with that of the camel." By so saying, he-set the slave free.

It was a while later when someone came to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) saying, "Do you still want that camel of yours." The person even took the name of the camel and continued, "She is there being sold in the marketplace," "Give me my shawl," Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) said and he stood up as he placed the ( l ) Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.3 1 0) . shawl over his shoulders. He then sat down again and removed the shawl saying, "I had been looking forward to the rewards for (losing) her and will therefore not go out and get her back." '''

Hadhrat Amr bin Dinaar narrates that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) made up his mind not to marry, (his sister) Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) said to him, "Get married because if your children pass away, you will be rewarded (for your patience) and if they live, they will make du'aa for you."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.300).Siraaj in his Taareekh and Abu Nu'aym have also reported the narration, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.2 Pg.348). (2) lbn sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.125). (3) lbn Sa'd (Vol. 3 Pg.258). Abu Nu'aym has also reported the narration in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.143).

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abza (RA) reports that en route to Siffeen when he was on the bank of the Euphrates River, Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) said, "O Allaah! If I knew that you would be pleased with me for throwing myself off a mountain and rolling down as I fall, I would certainly do so. O Allaah! If I knew that you would be pleased with me for kindling a large fire and throwing myself into it, I would certainly do so. O Allaah! If I knew that you would be pleased with me for throwing myself into the water and drowning, I would certainly do so. O Allaah! I am fighting only to please You and I am certain that you will never make me unsuccessful as long as I do things to please You."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.287). Tabraani has also reported the narration from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.354).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas once said, "For me to do a good deed today is more beloved to me than two liked deeds done during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ because when we were with Rasulullaah ﷺ, our only concern was the Aakhirah and not this world. Today, however, the world has fallen for us."
sources: Bukhaari and Muslim, as quoted in Safwatus Safwah (Pg.74).

paras: Hadhrat Alqama narrates that he once asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "was Rasulullaah ﷺ in the habit of specially setting aside certain days (for worship)?" "Not at all," Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) replied, "His deeds were perpetual, but which any of you is capable of doing what Rasulullaah ﷺ did?"

Hadhrat Mughierah bin Shu'ba (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ stood in salaah until his feet cut open." When someone asked him, "Did Allaah not forgive all your past and future errors?" he replied, "Should I then not be a grateful servant?" More narration of this nature will appear in the chapter concerning salaah, Inshaa Allaah.
sources: Bukhaari and Muslim, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol. 6 Pg.58). IbnSa'd (Vol.1 Pg.384) has reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Zubayr bin Abdullaah reports from his grandmother whose name was Zuhaymah that Hadhrat Utnmaan (RA) fasted perpetually and stood in salaah throughout the night save for a portion at the beginning of the night when he slept.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Httya (Vol. l Pg.56), as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Pg. 10).

paras: Hadhrat Mujaahid narrates that the level of worship Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr reached was unmatched. In fact, when a flood prevented people from performing Tawaaf, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) performed several circuits swimming.
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol.5 Pg.226).

paras: Hadhrat Qatan bin Abdullaah narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) would fast for seven days continuously to the extent that his intestines dried up.

Another narration from Hadhrat Hishaam bin Urwa states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr would fast for seven days continuously and it was only when he became extremely old that he reduced it to three days. Incidents about these two great men and others will soon appear in the chapter concerning salaah, Inshaa Allaah.
sources: Ibn jareer, as quoted In Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.226).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was the most handsome of people, the most generous and the bravest, when a frightening sound scared the people of Madinah one night, they ventured towards the sound. However, Rasulullaah beat them to it and was already returning from the place when he met them. He was riding Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) bare-backed horse with a sword dangling from his neck. He assured the people saying, "There is nothing to be alarmed about. There is nothing to be alarmed about." Although the horse was known to be a lazy one, Rasulullaah ﷺ commented, "He was like an ocean speedily and fluidly. This happened by the blessings of Rasulullaah Another narration states that when an alarm was raised in Madinah, Rasulullaah (Hi borrowed Hadhiat Abu Talha Slip's horse whose name was Mandoob. Rasulullaah ﷺ mounted the horse (and after investigating) he reassured the people saving, "We have seen nothing alarming but have found this horse to be like an ocean." Hadhrat Anas (RA) also said, "Whenever the battle grew furious, we always sought refuge with Rasulullaah ﷺ ."
sources: Bukhaari and Muslim.

paras: Hadhrat (RA) says, "During the Battle of Badr, we sought refuge from the Mushrikeert by the side of Rasulullaah ﷺ because he was the most furious of fighters."
sources: Muslim.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Is'haaq reports that a man from the Qais tribe once asked Hadhrat Baraa bin Aazib, "Did you people desert Rasulullaah ipi during the Battle of Hunayn?" Hadhrat Abu Is'haaq then heard Hadhrat Baraa (RA) reply, "However, Rasulullaah ﷺ did not desert. The Hawaazin tribe were ace archers. When we attacked them, they were defeated but when we occupied ourselves with collecting the booty, they intercepted us with a torrent of arrows. I then saw Rasulullaah ﷺ still on his white mule with Abu Sufyaan holding its reins. Rasulullaah ﷺ was saying. (I am a Nabi without a lie)'," Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said: "I am a Nabi without a lie. I am the son of Abdul Muttalib" Yet another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ then dismounted the mule.
sources: Ahmaa and Bayhaqi, as quoted in wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.37).

paras: Hadhrat Baraa (RA) also narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ then descended from his mule and prayed for assistance saying: "I am a Nabi without a lie. I am the son of Abdul Muttalib. O Allaah!

Send down Your assistance" Hadhrat Baraa (RA) says further, "When the battle grew furious, we took refuge with Rasulullaah ﷺ and it was only the bravest ones who could fight by his side." In the chapter concerning the bravery of the Sahabah (RA) in Jihaad, the incidents have already passed about the bravery of Hadhrat Abu Bakr , Umar, Ali, Talha, Zubayr, Sa'd, Hamzah, Abbaas, M-u'aadh, Ibn Umar, Mu'aadh bin Afraa, Abu Dujaanah, Qataadh, Salamah bin Akwa , Abu Hadrad , Khaalid bin Waleed, Baraa bin Maalik, Abu Mihjin, Ammaar bin Yaasir, Amr bin Ma'dikarib and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr.
sources: Bukhaari. Muslim and Nasa'ee have reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas reports that one night Rasulullaah found a date lying by his side and ate it. When he was unable to sleep that night, one of his wives asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ You stayed awake all night?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "I ate a date that I found at my side and because we had the Sadaqah dates with us, I feared that this could be one of those,"
sources: Ahmad, as quoted in wan Niiiaayah (Vol, 6 Pg.59).

paras: Abu Bakr ■ Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen says that besides Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), he knows of no one who forcibly vomited out the food he had just eaten. Once after eating some food he had been served, someone informed him that the food had been provided by Hadhrat ibn Nu'aymaan (RA). Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) exclaimed, "Were you feeding me the incantation fares of Ibn Nu'aymaan?!" He then forced himself to vomit.
Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla reports that Hadhrat Ibn Nu'aymaan was an extremely handsome Sahabi. (During the Period of ignorance)

Some people once came to him asking if he knew anything that would help cure a woman who always miscarries. "Oh yes, I do," he replied, when they asked him what it was, he recited to them an incantation (which means "O disobedient womb!
Be still and stop spoiling blood You are depriving her of bearing many children If only these many children were in the disobedient womb Because then she would bear them and recover"

In exchange for this, the people gave him a goat and some butter (after he had already become a Muslim). He then brought some of the meat to Hadhrat Abu Bakr, who ate. However, (after being informed of the incident) Hadhrat Abu Bakr stood up and forced himself to vomit. He then reprimanded, "Why do you people bring me food without informing me where it has come from?!"
sources: Ahmad in his.

paras: Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) had a slave who earned an income for him. When the slave brought some food one night and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) ate a morsel, the slave asked, "what has happened to you that you have not questioned me tonight (about the source of the food) when you usually do so every night?" Hadhrat Abu Bakr SSi replied, "It was extreme hunger that made me do it. Where did you get it from?" The slave explained, "During the Period of Ignorance, I passed by some people and (to assist them out of some difficulty, I) recited some incantations for them. They had promised to pay me and it was only today that I happened to pass by them as they were celebrating a wedding. They then gave me this food." "You would have killed me!" Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) exclaimed as her thrust his fingers in his mouth to vomit out the food. However, the food would not come out (because he had eaten it when he was very hungry). When someone suggested that it would come out only with water, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) asked for a bowl of water and he continued vomiting out the water until the food also came out. "May Allaah have mercy on you," someone remarked, "All this trouble merely for that morsel?" Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "I would have taken it out even if it cost me my life because I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, The fire of Jahannam is most deserving of a body nourished by that which is unlawful.' I therefore feared that any part of my body should receive nourishment from that morsel."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Voj.l Pg.3l). From his Afraad, Bukhaari has reported a part of the narration, as quoted in Safwatus Safwah (Vol.l Pg.95). Hasan bin Sufyaan and Deenowri in his Mujaalasah have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Muntakhab Karmil ummaal (Vol.4 Pg-360).

paras: Hadhrat Zaid bin Aslam reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once drank some milk and finding the taste queer, he asked the person who brought it, "Where did you get this milk from?" The person explained, "We were passing by a watering place where some zakaah camels were being watered. The herders then milked the camels for us and I put some in this water bag of mine (from which you just drank)." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then thrust his fingers into his throat and vomited the milk out.
sources: Maalikand Bayhaqi, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul ummaal (Vol.4Pg.418). (3)lbnSa'd(Vol.4Pg.418).

paras: Hadhrat Miswar bin Makhrama (RA) says, "We stuck close to Hadhrat Umar Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) was once out in Kufa when he stopped by a house and asked for water. When a little girl came out with a jug and a napkin, Hadhrat Ali (RA) asked, "Dear girl! Whose house is this?" When she informed him the person's name and that he was a coin evaluator, Hadhrat Ali said, "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say that one should never drink from the well of a coin evaluator and never take shade under anything belonging to a tax collector."
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaat ' (Vol.2 Pg.165).

paras: Hadhrat Yahya bin Sa'eed narrates that Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) had two wives. (He was so particular about treating them equally that) When it was the turn of the one (to be with him), he would not even make wudhu in the house of the other, it so happened that both of them passed away on the same day from the plague that struck in Shaam. Because the people were extremely busy that day, both ladies had to be buried in one grave. Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) (still scrupulous about being just between them) then drew lots to decide which of the two would be placed first in the grave.
Another narration states that Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) had two wives and would not even drink water from the house of one of them If It was the turn of the other to be with him.
sources: Abu Mu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.234).

paras: Hadhrat Tawoos says, "I testify that I heard Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) say, 'I testify that I heard Hadhrat Umar !s9SiK recite the Talbiya(3).' We were standing on Arafaat when a man asked, 'Tell me when Hadhrat Umar (RA) left Arafaat.' Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) (because of his cautiousness) replied, 'I do not know." The people were very surprised by this cautiousness of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA)
Tawakkul (Trust in Allaah)
Rasulullaah ﷺ.

Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that he accompanied Rasulullaah ﷺ on an expedition to Najd. On the way back, it was the time for their siesta when they came to a valley filled with thorny trees. As the Sahabah (RA) dispersed to take shade beneath the trees, Rasulullaah ﷺ also found some shade beneath a tree and hung his sword on it. Hadhrat Jaabir narrates further, "We had slept only a short while when Rasulullaah illf called for us. When we responded to his call, we found a Bedouin sitting with him. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'This person drew my sword while I was asleep. When I awoke, it was already drawn and in his hand as he said, will save you from me?' 'Allaah!' I replied. When he again asked, 'Who will save you from me?' I again replied, 'Allaah!' He then sheathed the sword and sat down. Rasulullaah ﷺ did not punish the man despite what he had done.
sources: Bukhaari and Muslim.

paras: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ had been fighting the Muhaarib and Ghatfaan tribes in Nakhlah (in Najd). It was at a time when the enemy found the Muslims in negligence when a man from them named Ghowrath bin Haarith approached Rasulullaah ﷺ with a sword. Standing over Rasulullaah ﷺ's head, he asked, "Who will save you from me?" "Allaahf Rasulullaah ﷺ replied. The sword fell from the man's hand and Rasulullaah Sii took hold of it saying, "Now who will save you from me?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. Ghowrath begged, "Do be a good captor." "Do you testify that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. "No," Ghowrath replied, "But I pledge that I shall never fight against you and neither join forces with anyone who fights against you." Rasulullaah ﷺ then let him go. When he returned to his comrades, he said to them, "I have come to you from the best of people." The narration then continues to explain the Salaatul Khowf.
sources: Bayhaqi, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.4 Pg.85).

paras: Hadhrat Yahya bin Murrah narrates, "When Hadhrat Mi (RA) used to go to the Masjid at night to perform Nafl salaah, we would also go with to guard him. After completing his salaah, he would ask us, 'What are you sitting here for?' When we informed him that we were there to guard him, he asked, 'Is it against the inhabitants of the heavens that you are guarding me or against the inhabitants of the earth?' 'Only from the inhabitants of the earth,' we submitted. He then said, 'Nothing happens on earth until it is decided in the heavens. There are two angels assigned to every person who protect and guard him. However, when a predestined matter arrives, they leave him to it. I therefore have a fortified shield from Allaah which will leave me only when death arrives. No person can taste the sweetness of Imaan until he is convinced that whatever (difficulty) afflicts him would never have passed him by and whatever (good) passes him by would never have come to him in the first place.
sources: Abu Dawood and Ibn Asaakir.

paras: Hadhrat Qataadah (RA) reports that Hadhrat Ali (RA) was extremely restless throughout the last night he spent in this world. This made his family very concerned and after secretly convening, they arrived at a decision and asked him in the name of Allaah (not to leave the house). However, he said to them, "Two angels are assigned to each and every person to protect him from that which is not destined for him (and this happens as long as what is predestined does not come to him). However, when something predestined comes his way, the two angels leave him to it." Hadhrat Aii (RA) then proceeded to the Masjid and he was assassinated.
sources: Abu Dawood and Ibn Asaakir.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Mijlaz narrates that a man from the Muraad tribe once came to see Hadhrat Ali (RA) when he was busy performing salaah in the Masjid. (After Hadhrat Ali (RA) completed the salaah) The man said to him, "Appoint some guards because the people of the Muraad tribe are planning to assassinate you." However, he said to them, "Two angels are assigned to each and every person to protect him from that which is not destined for him. However, when something predestined comes his way, the two angels leave him to it. One's appointed term is a fortified shield (because nothing can violate it)." fl) Hadhrat Yahya bin Katheer and others report that when people offered to guard Hadhrat Ali (RA), he said, "A person's appointed term guards him."
sources: IbnSa'dand, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.88).

paras: Hadhrat Muhammad ﷺ reports that two men presented their dispute to Hadhrat Ali (RA) for judgement. When he sat at the base of a wall, one of the men cautioned "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! That wall is going to fall." Hadhrat Ali reassured him saying, "Continue. Allaah suffices as a protector." When Hadhrat Ali (RA) had passed judgment and stood up, the wall fell down.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilyap/oll Pg.75).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Dhabiyya reports that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) was on his deathbed, Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) visited him. "What is the problem?" Hadhrat uthmaan (RA) asked. "My problem is my sins," Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood replied. Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) asked further, "What do you wish for?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) replied, "For the mercy of my Rabb." Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) then asked, "Should I not have a physician see you?" (Referring to the fact that Allaah is the greatest of curers,) Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "It was the physician (Allaah) Who gave me the illness."

Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) further asked, "Should I then not have an allowance fixed." "I have no need for an allowance," Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) assured him. "But it would belong to your daughters after your demise," Hadhrat Uthmaan explained. "Do you fear that my daughters would suffer poverty after my death?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) asked in surprise. He then continued, "I have instructed my daughters to recite Surah Waaqi'ah every night because I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say that poverty shall never ever afflict the person who recites Surah Waaqi'ah every night." Incidents similar to this concerning Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa have passed in the chapter concerning exercising patience during illness.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Dalaa'il (Pg.2l 1). (4) ibn Asaakir, as quoted in the Tafseerii lbn Katheer (Vol.4 Pg.281).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "I care not how my morning goes, whether it be in a manner that I like or in a manner that I dislike because I know not whether goodness is in what I like or in what I dislike."
sources: Ibn Mubaarak, lbn Abi Dunya in his Faraj and Askari in his Mawaa'idh, as quoted in Kanzul ummaal (Vol.2Pg.US).

paras: Hadhrat Hasan reports that someone once said to Hadhrat Ali (RA), "Abu Dharr says that he prefers poverty to riches and illness to good health," To this, Hadhrat Ali (RA) remarked, "May Allaah have mercy on Abu Dharr. My opinion is that the person who relies on Allaah's good choice for him will never wish to be in a condition other than that which Allaah has chosen for him. This is the highest level of contentment with the decision of Allaah." ® It was also Hadhrat Ali (RA) who said, "Whoever is happy with what Allaah decides will have Allaah's decision pass over him together with being rewarded. On the other hand, whoever is unhappy with what Allaah decides will still have Allaah's decision pass over him but his deeds will be laid to waste."
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul ummaal (Vo!.2 Pg.145).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "On the Day of Qiyaamah, each and every person will wish that in this world he had only that much of food which he could subsist on. The conditions a person experiences each morning and evening in this world will be detrimental to him only if his heart is filled with anger and discontentment. Furthermore, it is better for any on you to bite on a coal and burn himself rather than say about anything that Allaah had decreed, 'If only that had not happened.
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 2 Pg.145).

paras: Hadhrat Kumayl bin Ziyaad says that he was once with Hadhrat Ali (RA) when they reached a graveyard. Turning towards the graves, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "O inhabitants of the grave! O inhabitants of the place of decay! O inhabitants of the place of loneliness! What news have you! The news from us is that your wealth has already been distributed, your children have become orphans and your wives have remarried. That is the news that we have. What news have you?" Hadhrat Ali (RA) then turned and said, "O Kumayl! Had they been permitted to respond, they would have told us that the best provision is Taqwa." He then started weeping as he continued, "O Kumayl! The grave is a box containing one's actions and it is only at the time of death that one finds out about it,"
sources: Deenowri and lbn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 F g.142).

paras: Hadhrat Qais bin Abu Haazim reports that Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "Give more importance to having your aeeds accepted than to Taqwa because while a deed with Taqwa can never be undermined, how can one that is accepted ever be undermined?"
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya and lbn Asaakir.

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "When a deed with Taqwa can never be undermined, how can one that is accepted ever be undermined?"
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya and lbn Abi Dunya, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol. 2 Pg.142).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "The knowledge that Allaah has acceptedevenasingledeedofmineismore beloved to me than the earth full of gold."
sources: Ya'qoob bin Sufyaan and lbn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol .2 Pg. 1 42) .

paras: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "How grand is the sleep of the intelligent ones (who prepare for the Aakhirah) and their days without fastingl How won't they object to the waking nights and fasts of the foolish ones (who have no concern for the Aakhirah), An atom's weight of good that a person with Taqwa and conviction carries out is greater, more rewarding and more likely to be accepted than a mountain's weight of worship carried out by the negligent ones."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol. 1 Pg.2l 1). (6) lbn Abi Haatim, as quoted in the Tafseerof lbn Katheer (Vol.2 Pg.43). lbn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol.2 Pg.142).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) also said, "For me to know with certainty that Allaah has accepted even one salaah of mine is more beloved to me than the entire world and its contents because Allaah says: Allaah accepts only from those with Taqwa. (Surah Maa'idah, verse 27)
sources: This refers to the fear one has for displeasing Allaah because of one's intense love for Allaah.

paras: Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) said, "Whenever a person leaves out something for the pleasure of Allaah, Allaah grants him something much better from sources he does not expect. However, when someone is careless and takes things without knowledge (of the legality of sources), Allaah afflicts him with difficulties from sources he does not expect."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once remarked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I see that your hair is getting white?" Rasulullaah replied, "Surahs Hood, Waaqi'ah, Mursalaat, Amma Yatasaa'aloon and Idhash shamsu Kuwwirat have given me these white hairs." Another narration states that when Hadhrat Umar commented that Rasulullaah ﷺ was getting white hairs very early, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Surah Hood and its companions, namely Waaqi'ah, Amma Yatasaa'aloon and Idhash Shamsu Kuwwirat have given me these white hairs."
sources: These are Surahs 1 1,56, 77, 78 and 81 respectively.
Bayhaqi, as quoted in wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.59).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "How can I possibly enjoy life when the one with the horn (the angel Hadhrat israafeel already has it between his lips with his head bent forward and straining his ears in anticipation of the command (to blow the horn to announce the Day of Qiyaamah)." "O Rasulullaah ﷺ the Sahabah (RA) asked, "What should we say?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "You should recite: 'Allaah is Sufficient for us and He is the best of all Guardians. It is solely in Allaah that we trust'. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ fell unconscious when he heard someone recite the verse: Verily we have (in store for them in Jahannam) handcuffs, the Blazing fire... (Surah Muzammil, verse 12) The Fear of the Sahabah.
sources: Ahmad and Tirmidhi, as quoted in wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.56). (4) lbn Najjaar, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.43).

paras: Hadhrat Sahl bin Sa'd (RA) narrates that when the fear for Allaah gripped a young Ansaari, he wept so much every time he heard mention of Jahannam that this kept him indoors. When this was mentioned to Rasulullaah ﷺ he went to the house. As Rasulullaah ﷺ entered, he embraced the Ansaari, who then expired (in Rasulullaah ﷺ 's armsj. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "Enshroud your companion because fear has ruptured his liver."
sources: Haakim and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Targheeb (Vol.5 Pg.223). (6) lbn Abi Dunya and lbn Qudaamah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol.2 Pg.l44).

paras: Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) has reported a similar narration with the addition that when the youngster saw Rasulullaah ﷺ, he stood up, embraced Rasulullaah ﷺ and then fell down dead. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "Enshroud your companion because fear for Jahannam has ruptured his liver. I swear by the Being who controls my life that Allaah has saved him from it. Whoever aspires for something shall seek it and whoever fears something shall run away from it."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas- (RA) narrates that. after it was revealed to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he one day recited to the Sahabah (RA) the verse: O you who have imaan! Save yourselves and your families from the Fire (of Jahannam), the fuel of which is people and stones. (Surah Tahreem, verse 6) A young Sahabi then fell unconscious. When Rasulullaah ﷺ placed his hand on the Sahabi's heart, it was racing. Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "Dear boy! Recite 'Laa Ilaaha illallaah'." When he recited it, Rasulullaah ﷺ gave him the glad tidings of Jannah. The other Sahabah (RA) then asked, "Does this apply to all of us (or is it exclusively for him)." Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Have you not read the verse: (U) Igiw This (promise) is for him who fears standing before Me (on the Day of Qiyaamah) and who fears My warning (of punishment). (Surah Ibraheem, verse 12)
sources: Haakim, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.5 Pg.194). Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.145).

paras: Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) once fell ill, Rasulullaah ﷺ went to visit him, "How are you feeling, O Umar?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. "I have hope. (in Allaah's mercy) as well as fear (for Allaah's punishment)." Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "Whenever fear and hope are coupled in the heart of a Mu'min, Allaah grants him his hope and saves him from his fear."

Hadhrat Hasan narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once said, "Do you not see that Allaah mentions the verses of ease together with those of hardship and the verses of difficulty together with those of ease so that a Mu'min may be hopeful (in Allaah's mercy) as well as fearful (for Allaah's punishment)? In this manner, he will never have such hopes in Allaah that are unfounded and will also not throw himself into destruction." Other incidents concerning the fear that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar had for Allaah have passed in the chapter entitled "The Fear that the Khulafaa had for Allaah".
sources: Abush Shaykh, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol.2 Pg.144).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Roomi reports that the news reached him that Hadhrat Uthmaan once said, "If I were between jannah and Jahannam, not knowing into which of the two I will be ordered to go, I would prefer to be turned into ashes before knowing towards which of them I would be heading,"
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol. 1 Pg. 133).

paras: Hadhrat Qataadah narrates that Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin jarraah Si once said, "I wish that I was a mere sheep whom my owners would slaughter and then eat my flesh and my gravy."
Hadhrat Qataadah narrates that Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) said, "I wish that I were some sand on the top of a hill that the wind would blow away on a windy day," (2!
Hadhrat Qataadah also narrates that Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) said, "l wish that I were some sand that the wind would blow away."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hi/yaiyolA Pg,164).

paras: Hadhrat Aamir bin Masrooq narrates that someone once mentioned in the presence of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA), "I do not want to be amongst the 'As'haabul Yameen' but wish to be amongst the '." To this, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) remarked, "However, you have here a person (myself) who wishes not to even be resurrected after dying (let alone wanting to be amongst a certain group)."

Another narration from Hadhrat Hasan states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood said, "If I were placed between Jannah and Jahannam and then told, 'Choose between either entering one of these or becoming dust', I would rather be turned to dust." (Because of his humility, he felt unworthy of entering Jannah)

Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) said, "By Allaah! If you people knew what I know, you will neither make advances to your wives nor find rest on your beds. By Allaah! I wish that the day Allaah created me, He should have created me as a tree that is felled and whose fruit is eaten."

Hadhrat Hizaam bin Hakeem reports that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once stated, "If you people knew what you will see after death, you would neither derive pleasure out of eating nor out of drinking. You would then not go into your homes for shade but would rather go out onto the plains beating your chests and weeping over your condition. I wish that I were a tree that would be Those who will have a higher status in Jannah than the 'As'haabul Yameen', as stated in Surah Waaqi'ah. felled and then its fruit eaten."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol. 1 Pg.216).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) also mentioned, "I wish that I were a sheep belonging to some people who have visitors passing by. They will then pass a knife over my jugular veins, eat me and feed others." ® Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) once said, "I wish that I was this pillar."
sources: as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.12).

paras: Hadhrat Tawoos reports, "When Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal SSI came to our land, our scholars said to him, 'If you just give the word, we shall take these rocks and trees and build a Masjid for you.' Hadhrat Mu'aadh replied, 'I fear that I may be made to carry it on my back on the Day of Qiyaamah." Naafi says, "When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) entered the Kabah, I heard him say the following when he was in Sajdah: '(O Allaah!) You know that it is only my fear for You that prevents me from opposing the Quraysh for their position in this world."'

Hadhrat Abu Haazim narrates that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) passed by a man from Iraq who had fallen down (unconscious), he asked, "What is the matter with him?" The people said, "This happens to him every time the Qur'aan is recited to him." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) remarked, "Although we also fear Allaah, we never fall down."
sources: IbnSa'd(Vo!.4Pg.l2).
Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol. 1 Pg,236).

paras: It is reported that whenever Hadhrat Shaddaad bin Aws Ansaari (RA) lay on the bed, he would turn from side to side without being able to fall asleep. He would then say, "O Allaah! The fire of Jahannam has "dispelled my sleep." Thereafter, he would stand up and perform salaah until the morning.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.292).

paras: Hadhrat Amr bin Salamah (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "By Allaah! I Wish that I were a tree. By Allaah! I wish that I were .sand. By Allaah! I wish that Allaah had not created me at all."

Another narration states when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) came to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) before her death, he praised her saying, "Glad tidings for you, O wife of Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ never married a virgin besides you and your innocence was proclaimed from the heavens, it was then that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) entered from the opposite side. Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said to him, "Abdullaah bin Umar Si is heaping praises on me when I do not wish to hear anyone praise me today. I only wish that I had been completely forgotten."
sources: lbn Sa'd (Vol.8 Pg.74).

paras: Rasulullaah Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to me, 'Recite (the Qur'aan) to me.' I replied, 'How can I recite to you when it was to you that the Qur'aan was revealed?' Rasulullaah ill said, 'I would like to hear the Qur'aan recited by someone else.' I then recited Surah Nisaa until I reached the verse: 40 Jlp Qsrj bl How will it be (the condition of the Kuffaar on the Day of Qiyaamah) when We shall bring forth a witness from every nation (the Ambiyaa of - every community who will testify against the Kuffaar) and call you (O Muhammad ﷺ to be a witness over all of them? '(Surah Nisaa, verse 41)
Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, 'That's enough.' When I then looked up, I saw that tears were flowing from his eyes." Some other narration shall appear in the chapter concerning salaah, Inshaa Allaah.
sources: Bukhaari, as quoted in wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.59).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that the men of Suffa wept excessively when Allaah revealed the verse; ("i. c-)l OjSs-H Oj Oj 1 Are you astonished about this speech (the Qur'aan) and do you laugh (at it out of ridicule) instead of crying (out of fear for the warnings it sounds/7 (Surah Najm, verses 59,60)

They wept so much that tears flowed on their cheeks. Hearing them, Rasulullaah also started weeping and seeing him weep, the other Sahabah (RA) also wept, Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "The person who weeps out of fear for Allaah shall never enter Jahannam and the person who sins persistently shall never enter Jannah. However, if you never sin, Allaah shall create a nation that does sin and He will then forgive them (when they repent sincerely because He loves to forgive)."
sources: Bayhaqi, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.5 Pg.190).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once recited the verse; ...(The fire of Jaharmam) the fuel of which is people and stones,,. (Surah Tahreem, verse 6) Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "The Fire of Jahannam was stoked for a thousand years until it became red. It was then stoked for another thousand years until it became white. Thereafter, it was again stoked for a thousand years until it became black. It is now pitch black and dark and its flames cannot be extinguished." In front of Rasulullaah ﷺ was an Abyssinian man who then started to weep very loudly. Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA) then descended and asked (Rasulullaah ill!), "Who is this man weeping in front of you?" Rasulullaah ﷺ informed Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA) that the man was from Abyssinia and also praised the man. Hadhrat jibra'eel (RA) then told Rasulullaah ﷺ that Allaah said, "I swear by My honour, by My power and by My exaltedness over My throne that whenever the eye of My servant weeps in this world out of fear for Me, I shall definitely increase his laughter in Jannah."
sources: Bayhaqi and Isfahaani, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.5 Pg. 194).

paras: Hadhrat Qais bin Abu Haazim (RA) says, "I once went to see Rasulullaah ﷺ and found that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) had already taken his place become the Khalifah). (In his address to the people) Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) praised Allaah tremendously and wept excessively."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Muniakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.260),

paras: Hadhrat Hasan bin Muhammad bin (RA) bin Abi Taalib states that during the Friday sermon, Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to recite the Surah J-S-sJi is Takweer) until he reached the verse: On that day every soul will know what (actions) it had presented.

(Surah Takweer, verse 14) At this point, his voice would stop (because of his excessive weeping). Hadhrat Hasan narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once recited the verse: tf 0 Indeed, the punishment of your Rabb shall take place and there shall be none to avert it. (Surah Toor, verses 7,8) After reciting it, his voice ballooned (because of the emotion. This caused him to fall ill and) because of it, people were visiting him for twenty days.
sources: Abu Ubayd.

paras: Hadhrat Ubayd bin Umayr (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar iP once led them in the Fajr salaah and started reciting Surah Yusuf, However, he started weeping and had to stop when he reached the verse: (At) Oj tf V-iP (Referring to Hadhrat Ya'qoob (RA), Allaah says) His eyes had turned white (blind) with sorrow (because of excessive crying) and he was suppressing it (his sorrow) all the time, Yusuf, verse 84) Hadhrat Umar (RA) then went into Ruku.
sources: Abu Ubayd, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal Pg.401).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Shaddaad bin Haad narrates that even while standing in the last rows of the congregation, he could hear the sobbing of Hadhrat Umar during the Fajr salaah. Hadhrat Umar (RA) was reciting Surah Yusuf and (because of his excessive weeping, he had to stop when he) reached the verse: (Al Jjj-.) J I complain of my sorrow and my grief only to Allaah. (Surah Yusuf, verse 86)
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, Sa'eed bin Mansoor, Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Abi Shaybah and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.387).

paras: Hadhrat Hishaam bin Hasan narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) would sometimes recite a verse of the Qur'aan that would choke him (with emotion). He would then weep so much that he would fall down. (Because of weakness) He would then have to stay indoors and people would visit him thinking him to be ill.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hifya (Vol.1 Pg.5l).

paras: Hadhrat Haani who was the freed slave of Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) says that whenever Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) stopped at a graveyard, he would weep so much that his beard would get wet. Someone once asked him, "You do not weep when you think of Jannah and Jahannam but weep when you think of the grave?" He replied, "I have heard Rasulullaah ilif say, The grave is the first stage from amongst the many stages of the Aakhirah. If one is successful there, the later stages are easier. However, if one is unsuccessful there, the later stages will be extremely difficult."' Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) also added, "I have also heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say that he had never seen a sight more frightening than that of the grave." in his narration, Hadhrat Haani adds that he heard Hadhrat Uthmaan recite the following couplet by a grave (which means): "If you are saved from this (the punishment in the grave), then you are saved from something enormous If not, then I do not think that you will be saved (from future torment) "
sources: Tirmidhi, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.5 Pg.322j. Abu Nu'aym has also reported the narration in brief in his Htiya (Vol.1 Pg.61).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once passed by Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) who was weeping. "What makes you weep?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) enquired. Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) replied, "A Hadith that I heard from Rasulullaah ﷺ (which states that); 'indeed the tiniest amount of ostentation is tantamount to Shirk and the people most beloved to Allaah are those with Taqwa who are anonymous. They are those who will not be missed if they are not there and will not be recognised when they are present. These people are the torchbearers of guidance and the beacons of knowledge. "'(,)

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) was once reciting the Surah (Surah Mutaffifeen). However, he started weeping when he reached the verse: ...the day when all of mankind will stand before the Rabb of the universe (to account for their actions and words (Surah Mutaffifeen, verse 6) He wept so much that he fell down and was unable to recite further. Hadhrat Naafi reports that there was not a single occasion when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar did not weep when reciting the following verses of Surah Baqarah: Whether you make known what is in your hearts or hide it, Allaah will bring you to account for it (will remind you of it on the Day of Qiyaamah). He forgives whoever He wills and punishes whoever He wills. Allaah has control over all things. (Surah Baqarah, verse 284) He would then say, "Verily, this accountability is a grave matter." Hadhrat Naafi also reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) would cry uncontrollably whenever he recited the verse: Has the time not come for the hearts of the Mu'mineen'to submit to Allaah's remembrance? (Surah Hadeed, verse Hadhrat Yusuf bin Maahak says, "I walked with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar to Hadhrat Ubayd bin Umayr (RA) who was busy lecturing to some of his companions. When I again looked at Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) (after he had been listening awhile), I saw that tears were flowing from his eyes."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Pg.l 10).

paras: Hadhrat Ubayd bin Umayr (RA) once recited the verse: How will it be (the condition of the Kuffaar on the Day of Qiyaamah) when We shall bring forth a witness from every nation (the Ambiyaa of every community who will testify against the Kuffaar) and call you (O Muhammad ﷺ to be a witness over all of them? (Surah Nisaa, verse 41)

(Upon hearing this verse) Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) started weeping so profusely that his beard and collar became wet with tears. Hadhrat Abdullaah says, "The man sitting beside Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said to me, '1 actually contemplated getting up and telling Hadhrat Ubayd bin Umayr (RA) to curtail his talk because of the difficulty he was causing the elderly man (Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya. 1 Pg.290). (3) ibn Sa'd (vol.4 pg.62). Abu Nu'aym has reported a similar narration in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.383).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Mulaykah says, "I accompanied Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas from Makkah to Madinah and wherever he set up camp, he stood in salaah for half the night." When Hadhrat Ayyoob asked him what Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas Stmt's recitation of the Qur'aan was like, he replied, "He once cried painfully as he continuously recited the following verse with slow intonation: The pangs (agony) of death will bring the truth (of Imaan to every person). (It will then be said to the dying person,) "This (death) is what you used to avoid (However, now you have no option)." (Surah Qaaf, verse 1 9)
Hadhrat Abu Rajaa (RA) says, "The lines on the face of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas where his tears ran resembled two old shoe straps."
sources: Ibn Mubaarak in his Zuhd, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.2 Pg.l 57).

paras: Hadhrat uthmaan bin Abu Saudah says that he once saw Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit on the wall of the Masjid that (Allaah showed Rasulullaah ﷺ a vantage point that) overlooked a valley of Jahannam. His chest was upon the wall and he was weeping. "O Abu waleedi" Hadhrat Uthmaan asked, "What makes you weep so?" Hadhrat Ubaadah (RA) replied, "Rasulullaah iilf informed us that it was in this place that he saw Jahannam,"

Hadhrat Ya'la bin Ataa reports from his mother who made kohl for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr that he wept excessively, in fact, he would lock his door and weep so much that he developed a condition that caused his eyes to secrete a white fluid all the time. Hadhrat Ya'la says that it was for this reason that his mother prepared the kohl for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) Hadhrat Muslim bin Bishr reports that when Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) was weeping during his illness his death), someone asked him what it was that made him weep. He replied, "Take note that it is not for this world of yours that I am weeping. I am weeping because of the long journey ahead and the deficiency of my provisions. I have now climbed a rise that leads down either to Jannah or to Jahannam and I know not towards which of the two I shall be heading."

Hadhrat Dhamrah bin Habeeb reports from a freed slave of the Sahabi Hadhrat Abu Rayhaanah that when Hadhrat Abu Rayhaanah (RA) once returned from a military expedition, he ate supper, made wudhu and then stood (to perform salaah) at the place where he performed salaah. He started reciting a Surah of the Qur'aan and stood rooted to the spot until the Mu'adhin called out the Adhaan (for the Fajr salaah). "O Abu Rayhaanah!" his wife said, 'You have just marched on an expedition that was extremely exhausting. Thereafter, you returned (and engrossed yourself in salaah without a thought for me). Is there no share for us (in your time)?" Hadhrat Abu Rayhaanah (RA) replied, "By Allaahl Of course there is a share for you in my time, if I had only thought of you." "Then what was it that preoccupied you (from thinking of me)?" she asked. He replied, "Deep meditation about the descriptions Allaah has given about Jannah and its pleasures had engrossed my mind until I heard the Muadhin."

Hadhrat Muhammad bin waasi narrates that a man rode from Basrah to see Hadhrat Ummu Dharr (RA) after the demise of (her husband) Hadhrat Abu Dharr to ask her about the ibaadah of Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA), When he arrived, he said to her, "I have come to you so that you may inform me about the Ibaadah of Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) She said, "He would spend the entire day only meditating in solitude."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg. 164).

paras: Hadhrat Aun bin Abdullaah bin utba reports that he once asked Hadhrat Ummu Dardaa. about the best deed of (her husband) Hadhrat Abu Dardaa She replied, "Meditation and heeding to lessons." Another narration states that when she was asked about the deed that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) did most frequently, she replied, "Heeding to lessons." Yet another narration states that her reply was, "Meditation."
Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once said, "Meditation for a moment is better than standing in salaah an entire night."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.208) and Ahmad, as quoted in Safwatus Safwah (Vol.1 Pg.258).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa S8ffl!8S also said, "Amongst people there are those who are the keys to good and the locks of evil. They shall have great rewards. There are then also those who are the keys to evil and locks of good. They will be terribly punished. Meditation for a moment is better than standing in salaah an entire night."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya, Ahmad and lbn Sa'd (Vol.7 Pg.392). (4) lbn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal Pg. 142).

paras: Hadhrat Habeeb bin Abdullaah narrates that a man intending to march in Jihaad came to Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) for advice. Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "Think of Allaah in prosperity and He will think of you when you are in difficulty. When you admire something of this world, think about what it is to become (old and then turned to dust)."

Hadhrat Saalim bin Abil Ja'd reports that two bulls once passed by Hadhrat Abu Dardaa as they were being worked. When one of them stopped as the other continued, Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "There is certainly a great lesson in this (while the one will be whipped for stopping, the other will be saved from the whipping)."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.209). Ahmad has also reported the first narration, as quoted in Safwatus Safwah (Vol.1 Pg.258). (6) lbn Abi Dunya in Muhaasabatun Nafs, as quoted in Kanzul l/mmaal (Vol. 2 Pg.162).

paras: One of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)'s freed slaves reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr once said, "whoever angers his carnal self for the sake of Allaah will be saved from Allaah's anger."

Hadhrat Thaabit bin Hajjaaj narrates that Hadhrat umar (RA) once said, "Weigh yourselves up before you are weighed and assess yourselves before you are assessed because reckoning with yourself (in this world) is easier than the reckoning you will face tomorrow (in the Aakhirah). You should also adorn yourselves (with good deeds) before the great presentation (the Day of Qiyaamah, about which Allaah says): On that day, you will all be presented and nothing (no action or word) of yours shall remain hidden. (Surah Haaqa, verse) Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports, "I was one day with Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab when he went into an orchard. There was a wall between us and he was standing in the middle of the orchard when I heard him say (to himself), 'O Ameerul Mu'mineen! By Allaah! You should fear Allaah or He will definitely punish you."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hitya (Vol.1 Pg.52).

paras: In a lengthy narration, Hadhrat Simaak says that he once asked Hadhrat Jaabir bin Samurah, "Did you associate often with Nabi ﷺ Hadhrat Jaabir replied, "Yes, He was a person who often remained silent."
sources: Maali, lbn Sa'd, lbn Abi Dunya in his Muhaasabatim Nafs, Abu Nu'aym in his Ma'rifah (Vol. Pg.) and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.4Q0).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Maalik Ashja'ee (RA) reports that his father said, "We were little boys when we used to sit in the company of Rasulullaah ﷺ and have never seen anyone remain silent as much as Rasulullaah ﷺ did. Whenever his companions would talk too much, he merely smiled."
sources: Ahmad and Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.297) has commented on Ahmad's chain of narrators, lbn Sa'd (Vol.1 Pg.372) has reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once out with his companions. As he rode, one of them stepped out ahead of him. Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I pray that Allaah takes our lives before yours. May Allaah never show us the day (of your demise), but should we see it, what deeds should we carry out after you? May my parents be sacrificed for you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ Should it be Jihaad in the path of Allaah?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Jihaad in the path of Allaah is an excellent deed, but people have become accustomed to it. (What you should be doing is) Something that exercises greater restraint (on the carnal self)." "Then fasting and Sadaqah?" Hadhrat Mu'aadh Si asked. "Fasting and Sadaqah are an excellent deeds," Rasulullaah ﷺ commented, "but people have become accustomed to it. (What you should be doing is) Something that exercises greater restraint (on the carnal self)."

Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) then went on to mention every type of good deed, but each time Rasulullaah ﷺ's reply was, "But people have become accustomed to it. (What you should be doing is) Something that exercises greater restraint (on the carnal self)." Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) eventually asked, "If people have become accustomed to these deeds, what is that thing that exercises greater restraint (on the carnal self)?" Pointing to his mouth, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Remaining silent at all times save when speaking what is good." "Will we be taken to task for what our tongues speak?" Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) asked in surprise. Striking his hand on Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA)'s thigh, Rasulullaah ﷺ said something like, 'Your mother ought to have lost you!" He then added, "It is because of what the tongue speaks that people will be thrown headlong into jahannam. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak only what is good or remain silent about evil. Speak what is good and you will reap the rewards. Remain silent about evil and you will be safe.

Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that when someone was martyred, a lady was weeping over him saying, "Oh dear martyr!" Addressing her, Rasulullaah said, "Stop saying that. How do you know that he is a martyr (and is guaranteed immediate access into Jannah)? He may have mentioned something that was futile or was miserly with something that would not have cost him anything." ® In another narration, Hadhrat Anas (RA) states that when one of the Sahabah was martyred during the Battle of Uhud, a rock was found tied to his belly (which he had tied) because of hunger. Wiping the dust off his face, his mother said, "Glad tidings for you, O beloved son of Jannah." Addressing her, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "How do you know that he is a martyr is guaranteed immediate access into Jannah)? He may have mentioned something that was futile or refused something that would not have harmed him (to part with)."

Hadhrat Khaalid bin Numayr says, "Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) often remained silent for prolonged periods of time and always seemed depressed. (When he did speak, he was mostly seeking Allaah's protection from trials."
sources: Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.269),

paras: Hadhrat Abu Idress Khowlani says, "I once entered the Masjid of Damascus when my eyes caught sight of a man with sparkling front teeth. He was a very quiet man and whenever the people with him disagreed on some issue, they referred it to him and readily accepted ids verdict. When I enquired who he was, I was ( i ) Tabraani, Haythami (Vol, 1 0 Pg.299) has commented on the chain of narrators. informed that he was Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) ' Hadhrat Aslam narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) once found Hadhrat Abu Bakr pulling at his tongue, he asked, "What are you doing, O Khalifah of Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) replied, "There is not a part of the body that does not complain of the sharpness of the tongue."
sources: Abu Ya'la. Haythami (Vol. 10 Pg.302) has commented on the chain of narrators. Abu Nu'aym has also reported the narration briefly in his Hilya (Vol. 1 Pg.33).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Waa'il narrates that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once climbed Mount Safa, he caught hold of his tongue saying, "O tongue! Speak what is good and reap the rewards. Shun speaking evil and you will remain safe before having to regret." He then narrated, "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Most of man's sins stem from the tongue."
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol. 10 Pg,300).

paras: Hadhrat Sa'eed Jareeri reports from a man who said, "I once saw Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas holding the point of his tongue as he said, 'Shame on you! Speakwhatisgood and reap the rewards. Shun speaking evil and you will remain safe.' Someone then asked, 'O Ibn Abbaas Why do I see you holding your tongue and saying that?' Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) replied, 'The news has reached me that on the Day of Qiyaamah a person will be more angry with his tongue than with anything else.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.328).

paras: Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Thaabit Bunaani narrates that Hadhrat Shaddaad bin Aws (RA) once said to one of his companions, "Lay the tablecloth so that we may dig in to it!" Another of his companions said in surprise, "I have never heard you speak like that since I have come. to know you." Hadhrat Shaddaad (RA) said, "Since I separated from Rasulullaah ﷺ , every statement I have made was a harnessed one (said with much thought). By Allaah! Another like this shall never again escape."

Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Moosa reports that Hadhrat Shaddaad bin Aws (RA) once said, "Lay the tablecloth so that we may frolic with it." The people with him immediately picked at his words saying, "Look at Abu Ya'la (Hadhrat Shaddaad title)! What a statement has come from him!" Hadhrat Shaddaad (RA) then said, "Dear son of my brother! Since the time I pledged allegiance at Rasulullaah ﷺ's hand, every statement I have made had been a harnessed one, except for this one. Come, forget this and let me tell you something better for you to note. (It is this du'aa) 'O Allaah! We seek steadfastness in our affairs and the resolve to do good. We ask You for the ability to be grateful for Your bounties and for the ability to worship You in a most beautiful manner. We ask You for a pure heart and a truthful tongue. We also beseech You for the good You are aware of and for protection from the evil You know about.' Learn this from me and forget the other words (I said without thinking)."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.265) and (Vol.1 Pg.266). Ahmad has also reported the narration, as quoted in the Tafseeroi lbn Katheer (Vol.2 Pg.35l).

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Shaddaad (RA) added, "Do not learn these words from me, but rather learn what I shall narrate to you that I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "When people started hoarding treasures of gold and silver, fill your treasures with the words: 'O Allaah! We seek steadfastness in our affairs and the resolve to do good."1 Hadhrat Shaddaad (RA) then mentioned words like the narration above before adding, "(O Allaah) I seek forgiveness from You from the sins You know I have committed, for You are the One who knows well all that is hidden."

Hadhrat Isa bin Uqba narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "I swear by the Being besides Whom there is none worthy of worship that nothing on earth is more deserving of a long prison sentence than the tongue."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.134). Tabraani has also reported the narration from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.303).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "Beware of futile speech. All you need to say it that which would get your needs fulfilled."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.303) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "The people guilty of the most sins on the Day of Qiyaamah shall be those who most engaged in idle talk."
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.303).

paras: Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "The tongue is the basis of the body's well-being. When the tongue is upright, the other limbs are all upright. However, as soon as the tongue is out of control, no other limb stays under control." Another narration states that he once said, "Keep a low profile and you will not be talked about (thus saving you from pride). Remain silent and you will remain safe." Another narration states that he said, "silence invites towards Jannah." it was also Hadhrat Ali (RA) who mentioned the following couplets (which mean): "Never disclose your secrets except to yourself Because there Is an advisor to every advisor ( 1 ) Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol. 1 Pg.265) .
And I have also se'en many misguided men Who do not leave upright men unscathed (by their insults) "
sources: lbn Abi Dunya in his Samt, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol,2 Pg. 158). - (2) lbn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.159).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once said, "Learn to remain silent just as you learn to speak because silence is a great source of self-control. You ought to be more interested in listening than speaking and should never speak about things that do not concern you. You should also not laugh when there is nothing to laugh about or go somewhere you do not have to go."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hifya (Vol.1 Pg.220).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) also said, "There is no limb of a Mu'min that Allaah loves more than his tongue because it is by means of this that he will enter jannah. At the same time, there is no limb of a Kaafir that Allaah hates more than his tongue because it is by means of this that he will enter Jahannam."
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said, "The limb that a person most needs to purify is his tongue."
Hadhrat Anas (RA) said, "A person can never have Taqwa until he controls his tongue."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hifya (Vol. 1 Pg.307). (5) lbn Sa'd (Vol.7 Pg.22).

paras: The Speech of Rasulullaah ﷺ.

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ's speech was such (so clear) that if anyone wished to count the words, they could have easily done so." She also mentioned, "Shall I not surprise you? A certain person actually came and spoke to Rasulullaah ﷺ beside my room so loudly that I could hear him. talk as I was busy with my salaah. He then left before I could complete my salaah. Had I been able to find him before that, I would have certainly given him a piece of my mind." She then added, "Rasulullaah ﷺ never spoke continuously and quickly as you people do."
sources: Bukhaari. Ahmad, Muslim and Abu Dawood have also reported the narration from Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA).

paras: In another narration, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ's speech was so clear that everyone could understand it. He would never speak continuously and quickly." it was Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) or Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) who said, "Rasulullaah liii's speech was crisp, with every letter distinctly pronounced."
sources: Ahmad and Abu Dawood.
Bukhaari.

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ spoke anything (of marked importance), he would repeat it thrice and whenever he approached a gathering, he would greet thrice."
sources: Rasulullaah ﷺ greeted once when first seeking permission to enter, thereafter a second time when entering and finally a third time when leaving.

paras: Hadhrat Thumamah bin Anas narrates that whenever Hadhrat Anas (RA) spoke (something of importance), he repeated himself thrice and would say that when Rasulullaah ﷺ greeted with Salaam (to seek permission to enter a home), he did so thrice and when he spoke (something of great importance), he would repeat it thrice. Hadhrat Anas (RA) also reported that when Rasulullaah spoke, he would repeat himself thrice so that people could understand what he was saying."
sources: Ahmad.
Tirmidhi.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "I have been sent with concise yet comprehensive speech and have been assisted with awe. When I was sleeping once, the keys to the treasures of the heavens and the earth were brought to me and placed in my hand." ® Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA) reports, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ sat down to talk, he would often look towards the sky (in anticipation of revelation)."
sources: Ahmad and Bukhaari.

paras: Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) says, "Even when speaking to the worst of people, Rasulullaah ﷺ would turn his full attention to the person so that (they would feel special and) their hearts would be won over.
