By Allaahl I never spoke to Rasulullaah ﷺ about (freeing) the people of my tribe until the Muslims freed them by themselves. In fact, I only found out about it when one of my cousins informed me about it. I then praised Allaah for it."

Hadhrat Ibn Shihaab narrates that it was the year after signing the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah that Rasulullaah ﷺ left to perform Umrah. This occurred seven years after the Hijrah during the month of Dhul Qa'dah, which was the same month in which the Mushrikeen had prevented Rasulullaah ﷺ from entering the Masjidul Haraam (the previous year). When he reached a place called Ya'jij, Rasulullaah ﷺ sent Hadhrat Ja'far bin Abu Taalib SSi to propose on his behalf for the hand of Hadhrat Maymoonah bint Haarith bin Hazan Aamiriyyah in marriage. Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA) handed over her affairs to Hadhrat Abbaas bin Abdul Muttalib (RA) who was married to her sister Ummu Fadhl. Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) then handed her over in marriage. to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ stayed over in Sarif for a while until Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA) arrived there and the marriage was consummated. Allaah had decreed that Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA) should pass away at the same place where her marriage to Rasulullaah ﷺ was consummated.

Another narration states that after marrying Hadhrat Maymoonah bint Haarith Rasulullaah ﷺ stayed in Makkah for three days. On the third day, Huwaytib bin Abdul Uzza came to Rasulullaah ﷺ with a few men of the Quraysh and said, "Your stay has expired, so leave us." Rasulullaah ﷺ said to them, "What harm will it do to you if you leave me to consummate my marriage in your midst, after which I shall host a meal which you all can attend?" "We have no need for you food," they snapped, "do leave us." Rasulullaah ﷺ therefore left for Madinah with Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA) and consummated his marriage at Sarif.

Hadhrat Ali (RA) narrates, "When a marriage proposal for Faatima was sent to Rasulullaah ﷺ, a slave of mine asked, you know that a marriage proposal for Faatima has been sent to Rasulullaah ﷺ When 1 declared that I did not know, she said, She has already received a proposal. what stops you from approaching Rasulullaah ﷺ requesting him) to marry her to you?' 'Do I have anything with which to marry her?' I said. She said, You only have to approach- Rasulullaah ﷺ and he will marry her to you.' By Allaah! She then continued giving me hope until I went to see Rasulullaah ilif . However, when I sat before Rasulullaah ﷺ, I was unable to utter a word out of respect and awe for him. Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "What brings you here? Is there something" you need?' When l remained silent, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Have you perhaps come to propose for Faatima?' Yes,' I managed to reply. 'Have you got anything to give as dowry?' Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. 'By Allaah!' I replied, 'I have nothing.' "What has happened to the suit of armour I gave you?' he asked. I swear by the Being Who controls the life of All that the armour was the type made by the Hatma bin Muhaarib tribe and was barely worth four (hundred) Dirhams. when I informed Rasulullaah ﷺ that I still had it with me, he said, 'Then I have handed her over in marriage to you so send it to her as dowry.' Thi? was therefore the dowry of Faatima the daughter of Rasulullaah ﷺ.
sources: Rooyaani and lbn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg,113). Nasa'ee has reported a similar narration, as quoted in wan Nihaayah (Vol.7 Pg.342).

paras: Hadhrat Buraydah (RA) narrates that a group of the Ansaar once suggested to Hadhrat (RA) that he propose for Hadhrat Faatima (RA) hand in marriage. (When he approached Rasulullaah ffiif) Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "What does the son of Abu Taalib need?" "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Ali replied, "I wish to propose for the hand of Faatima the daughter of Rasulullaah ﷺ All Rasulullaah ﷺ said was, "Marhaban, "Hadhrat Ali then left and met with the group of Ansaar who had been waiting for him. When they asked him what had happened, he replied, "All I know is that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Marhaban wa Ahlan. '"They said, "Even one of two things Rasulullaah ﷺ gave you are sufficient. He gave you both Ahl (a family) as well as Marhab (a comfortable home)."

After handing Hadhrat Faatima (RA) over in marriage, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Ali! It is necessary for a Waleemah to be hosted after consummation." Hadhrat Sa'd offered a sheep he owned (for the meat) and the Ansaar collected a few Saa of wheat (for the bread). When the night of the consummation arrived, Rasulullaah fill gave the couple instructions to do nothing until he arrived. (When he got there) Rasulullaah ﷺ asked for some water, performed wudhu and then sprinkled some of the water on to Hadhrat Ali (RA) saying: "O Allaah! Bless the two of them and bless them in their consummation."
sources: A! Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.7 Pg), lbn Sa'd (Vol.8 Pg.21) has also reported a similar narration.

paras: Another narration similar to the above, states that the du'aa Rasulullaah ﷺ made was: "O Allaah! Bless the two of them and bless them in their two lion like sons." A third narration quotes the du'aa of Rasulullaah ﷺ as: "O Allaah! Bless the two of them, shower Your blessings on them, bless them in their consummation and bless them in their progeny." Yet another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ added: "...and bless their communion."
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.2 10).

paras: Hadhrat Asmaa bint Umays (RA) narrates that after Hadhrat Faatima (RA) was married to Hadhrat Ali Stsifig, all that they saw in her house was a straw mat spread out on the ground, a pillow stuffed with the bark of a palm tree, an earthen jug and an earthen mug. (On the night of the marriage) Rasulullaah ﷺ sent a message saying, "Do nothing" or "Do not get close to your wife until I come." When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived, he asked, "Is my brother here?" When Rasulullaah ﷺ forged bonds of brotherhood between the Sahabah (RA), he forged his brotherhood with Hadhrat Ali (RA). Hadhrat Ummu Ayman (RA), a pious woman who was an Abyssinian and the mother of Hadhrat Usaama bin Zaid asked in surprise, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ ! He is your brother and you have married your daughter to him?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "This (marriage) can take place (despite this type of brotherhood), O Ummu Ayman." Rasulullaah ﷺ then sent for a container of water, uttered some words and then passed his hands over the chest and face of Hadhrat Ali (RA). He then called Hadhrat Faatima (RA) who stood by him shivering in her shawl out of modesty. Rasulullaah ﷺ sprinkled some of the water on her and also uttered some words. He then said to her, "I have not failed you in my duty to get you married to the family member 1 love most." Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) narrates further. She says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ then noticed a figure behind the curtain or behind the door and asked, is that?' 'Asmaa,' I replied. 'Asmaa bint Umays?' Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. 'Yes, O Rasulullaah ﷺ I confirmed. He then asked, 'Have you come to be of service to Rasulullaah ﷺ (and his family)?' 'Yes,' I replied, 'because a young girl must have a family woman with her on her first night to take care of anything she might need.' Rasulullaah ﷺ then made such a wonderful du'aa for me that it is the one deed that I have most hope in (to deliver me to salvation in the Aakhirah). Rasulullaah ﷺ then said to Ali SE 'Look after you wife' and as he left, he continued making du'aa for them until he disappeared in his rooms."

In another narration, Hadhrat Asmaa bint Umays (RA) says, "I was present the night Rasulullaah ﷺ's daughter Faatima became a new bride. That morning, Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived and knocked at the door. When Ummu Ayman got up and opened the door, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, 'O Uramu Ayman! Call my brother for me.' She said, 'He is your brother and you got him married to your daughter?' 'O Ummu Ayman!' Rasulullaah ﷺ continued, 'Do call him for me.' When the other women heard Rasulullaah (Slip's 'voice, they dispersed and he took a seat in the corner. Ali then arrived and after making du'aa for him, Rasulullaah ﷺ sprinkled some water on him as well. Thereafter, Rasulullaah ﷺ sent for Faatima. She arrived all covered in perspiration and takingshortstepsoutofherextreme modesty. 'Relax,' Rasulullaah ﷺ reassured her, 'I have married you to the family member I love the most.'" The rest of the narration is like the one quoted above.
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.210) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Ali (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ got him married to Hadhrat Faatima (RA), Rasulullaah ﷺ sent for some water and then gargled with it. Rasulullaah ﷺ then took Hadhrat Ali (RA) into the room where he sprinkled the water on his chest and between his shoulders and then sought Allaah's protection for him by reciting Surah Ikhlaas (Surah 112) and the Mu'awwadhatayn Falaq and Surah Naas).

Hadhrat Albaa bin Ahmar reports from Hadhrat Ali (RA) that when he proposed for Rasulullaah ﷺ's daughter Hadhrat Faatima (RA), he sold a suit of armour he owned as well as some of his other possessions for a sum of four hundred and eighty Dirhams. Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed him to use two-thirds for perfume and the remaining third for clothing. Rasulullaah ﷺ then gargled in a utensil of water and told the couple to bath with it. Rasulullaah ﷺ also instructed Hadhrat Faatima (RA) not to feed any of her children before he got to the child, but she started feeding Hadhrat Husayn (RA) before Rasulullaah could arrive. As for Hadhrat Hasan (RA), Rasulullaah ﷺ put some unknown thing in his mouth because of which he was more knowledgeable than his brother.

Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates, "We attended the marriage of Ali and Faatima and have not witnessed a better marriage. The matting (on which we sat) was stuffed with the bark of a date palm and we were served raisins and dates to eat. Her bedding on her first night was a sheepskin."
Hadhrat Ali (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Faatima (RA) got married, Rasulullaah ﷺ gave her a blanket, a water bag and a leather pillow stuffed with Idhkhfr grass.

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ sent Hadhrat Faatima (RA) to (her husband) Hadhrat Ali (RA), Rasulullaah ﷺ gave her a blanket, a water bag and a leather pillow stuffed with the bark of a date palm and Idhkhir grass. The couple slept on (half of) the blanket and used the other half to cover themselves.

Hadhrat Rabee'ah (RA) says, "I was Rasulullaah ﷺ's servant. One day he asked, 'O Rabee'ah! Are you not interested in getting married?' I replied, 'I have no intention of marrying. While I have nothing with which to support a wife, I also do not want anything to preoccupy me from (serving) you.' When Rasulullaah turned away from me, I said to myself, 'By Allaah! Rasulullaah ﷺ definitely knows better than me what is best for me in this world and in the Aakhirah. By Allaah! Should he ever again ask me whether I am interested in getting married, I shall reply, 'Certainly, O Rasulullaah ﷺ Instruct me as you please.' When Rasulullaah ﷺ did ask me whether I was interested in getting married, 1 replied, 'Certainly, O Rasulullaah ﷺ Instruct me as you please.' Rasulullaah then instructed me to go to a particular tribe of the Ansaar who did not frequently meet with Rasulullaah ﷺ. He told me to tell them that he had sent me to them with instructions to get me married to a certain girl from amongst them. I therefore went to them and informed them that Rasulullaah ﷺ had sent me with instructions that they get me married. 'Welcome to Rasulullaah and the messenger of Rasulullaah ﷺ they cried out, 'By Allaah! the messenger of Rasulullaah ﷺ shall never return without having his need fulfilled. They then got me married and treated me exceptionally well without even asking for a witness.

I returned depressed to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ I have been to people who are extremely generous. They got me married and treated me exceptionally well without even asking for a witness. However, I have no dowry to give. Rasulullaah ﷺ then called for Buraydah Aslami (the leader of my tribe) and instructed him to collect some gold for me equivalent to the weight of a date stone. When I took possession of what the people collected for me, I brought it to Rasulullaah ﷺ who said. Take this to them and tell them that this is her dowry,' When I did so and told them that this was her dowry, they accepted it with great happiness and said, This is excellent and so much!' When I again returned depressed to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he asked, so gloomy, 0 Rabee'ah?' 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ I began, 'I have never met people -as wonderful as them. They were happy with what I gave them and treated me extremely well. They even told me that the dowry was excellent and so much.' However, I have nothing with which to host a Waleemah. 'O Buraydah!' Rasulullaah ﷺ called out, 'Collect (money) for a goat for him.' After the people (of my tribe) had collected (enough to buy) a large and fat sheep, Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed me to go to Aa'isha and tell her to give me the basket containing the grains. I did as I was ordered and she said, 'Here is the basket containing seven Saa of barley. By Allaah! By Allaah! we have no other food besides this. You may have it.' 1 took the basket to Rasulullaah ﷺ and informed him about what Aa'isha had said. Rasulullaah ﷺ said. Take this to them (your in-laws) and tell them to bake this (the barley) into bread and to cook that (the sheep),' (When I took it to them) They said, "While we can take care of the bread for you, you will have to see to the sheep for us,' Some men of the Aslam tribe and I took the sheep, slaughtered it, skinned it and then cooked it. We then had bread and meat with us and I hosted the Waleemah. I also invited Rasulullaah ﷺ. Thereafter, Rasulullaah ﷺ gave me a piece of land and gave a piece to Abu Bakr as well. The world had finally come to me. It however occurred that Abu Bakr and I fell into a dispute regarding a date palm which I claimed was on my property and he claimed was on his. When an argument ensued, Abu Bakr told me something that I disliked. He however regretted what he did and said to me, '0 Rabee'ah! Please repeat the words to me so that justice is done.' 'I shall never do so,' I replied. He said, 'If you do not repeat the words, I shall complain about you to Rasulullaah ﷺ When I adamantly refused, he forsook the land issue and went to Rasulullaah ﷺ. I went behind him. Some men of the Aslam tribe came and said, 'May Allaah have mercy on Abu Bakr! What will he complain to Rasulullaah ﷺ about when it was he who said those words?' 'Do you people know who that is?' I asked. That is Abu Bakr Siddeeq!' I emphasised, "He was the second of the two (in the cave) and the oldest Muslim. Beware that he should not turn and see you assisting me against him and then become angry, when he then goes to Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah ﷺ should not become angry because of his anger and then Allaah should not become angry because the two of them are angry. If that happens, Rabee'ah shall be doomed.' "What do you want us to do?' they asked. I then told them to return. As Abu Bakr proceeded to Rasulullaah ﷺ and I followed him by myself. After he had narrated the incident as it had occurred, Rasulullaah ﷺ looked up to me and said, 'O Rabee'ah! What is the problem between you and Siddee?Q' I explained the situation to Rasulullaah ﷺ, adding that when he told me something I disliked, he said, 'Please repeat the words to me so that justice is done.' I then refused to do so. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'That was right. You should not repeat the words. However, you could have at least said, 'May Allaah forgive you, O Abu Bakr." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then turned around weeping.
sources: Ahmad, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.368).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Barzah (RA) reports that Hadhrat Julaybeeb (RA) a man who frequently visited women and joked with them. Hadhrat Abu Barzah (RA) himself instructed his wife never to allow Hadhrat Julaybeeb Sliffigi to see her and threatened to do many things if she ever did so. it was a practice amongst the Ansaar never to get any of their widows married until they were sure that Rasulullaah ﷺ was not interested in marrying her. Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to one of the Ansaar, "Will you allow me to marry your daughter?" "Of course," the man obliged, "it will be a great honour and pleasure." "I do not wish to marry her to myself (but to someone else)," Rasulullaah ﷺ pointed out. "Then for whom?" the Ansaari asked. "For Julaybeeb," Rasulullaah ﷺ replied. The Ansaars said, "I shall consult with her mother."

He then asked (his wife), "Rasulullaah ﷺ has proposed for your daughter." "Of course," she agreed, "it will be a great pleasure." "However," the Ansaari explained, "he is not proposing for himself, but on behalf of Julaybeeb." The lady burst out, "To Julaybeeb! Never! To Julaybeeb! Never! I swear by life that we shall never marry him (to our daughter)!" As the Ansaari was about to get up to inform Rasulullaah ﷺ about what the mother said when the. daughter asked, "Who was it that brought to you a proposal for me?" When the mother informed her (that it was Rasulullaah ﷺ who brought the proposal), the girl asked, "Are you then rejecting the command of Rasulullaah ﷺ Hand me over in marriage to him for he shall never destroy me (since the marriage is with Rasulullaah illf's approval)."

Her father then went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and reported the incident to him. saying, "My daughter places her affairs in your hands. You may marry her to whomever you please." Rasulullaah ﷺ then proceeded to get her married to Hadhrat Julaybeeb (RA).

It then occurred that Rasulullaah ﷺ once went out to a battle. After Allaah had given Rasulullaah ﷺ a large booty, he asked, "Is someone missing?" When the Sahabah (RA) said that they found no one missing,. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "But I notice that Julaybeeb is missing. Look for him." When the Sahabah (RA) went out in search of him, they found him beside the bodies of seven men of the enemy whom he had killed before the enemy managed to kill him. They then reported back saying, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ He is there beside the bodies of seven men of the enemy whom he had killed before the enemy managed to kill him." Rasulullaah ﷺ went to the body of Hadhrat Julaybeeb (RA) and said, "He killed seven before they managed to kill him. He is from me and I from him." Rasulullaah ﷺ repeated this two or three times and then took him in his arms. A grave was then dug for him and there was no bier besides the arms of Rasulullaah ﷺ . Rasulullaah ﷺ himself lay the body in the grave. The Hadith does not state whether the body was bathed or not.

When Hadhrat Thaabit noted that there was no widow from the Ansaar who was more charitable than the widow of Hadhrat Julaybeeb (RA), Hadhrat Is'haaq bin Abdullaah bin Abu Talha said to him, "Do you know what du'aa Rasulullaah made for her? He said, "O Allaah! Pour down good on her in abundance and never give her a life of hardship.' It is for this reason that there was never a widow amongst the Ansaar more charitable than her."

Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA) reports that he once married a woman from the Kindah tribe and consummated the marriage in her house. On the night of the marriage, his friends walked with him to her house and when they reached it, he said to them, "You may return now. May Allaah reward you." He did not allow them to enter the house as foolish people generally do. When he looked at the house which had been decorated (with drapes on all sides), he remarked, "Is your house feverish (because of which you had to bandage it) or has the Kabah been moved to the Kindah tribe?" The people replied, "Neither is the house feverish nor has the Kabah been moved to the Kindah tribe." Hadhrat Salmaan then refused to enter the house until all the drapes were removed except for the drape covering the entrance.

When Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) finally entered the house, he saw a large amount of goods there. "Whose goods are these?" he asked. "Yours and your wife's," the people replied. Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) said, "This does not conform with the advice my beloved friend (Rasulullaah ﷺ) gave me. My beloved friend advised me to have only that much of worldly goods that a traveller has as provisions." when he saw a few (female) servants, he asked, "Whose servants are these?" When he was informed that the servants also belonged to him and his wife, he said, "This also does not conform with the advice my beloved friend gave me. He advised me to keep only those (female) servants whom I can marry or who I can get married (to others). If I do keep them and they fornicate (because they have none to satisfy their needs), their sins will be on me without any reduction to the sin they will be guilty of."

Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) then turned to the women around his wife and said, "Will you ladies leave me to be alone with my wife?" They readily agreed and left. Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) then went to the door, shut it and drew the drape over it. Thereafter, he sat with his wife, held her forelock and made du'aa for blessings. He then asked her, "Will you obey any instructions I give you?" Her reply was, "You are sitting in the position of a person who has to be obeyed." He continued to say, "My beloved friend advised me that when I meet with my wife (for the first time), I should meet with her in the obedience of Allaah."He then got up and proceeded to the place of salaah with her following him. After performing salaah for some time, they left the place of salaah and he then fulfilled with her the need a man has with his wife.

Early next morning his friends came to him asking, "How did you find your wife?" When he ignored them, they repeated the question. Again he ignored them but again they repeated themselves. When they repeated the question a third time, he ignored them yet again but then finally said, "Allaah has made drapes, curtains and doors to conceal what lies behind them, it is sufficient to ask about things that are apparent but one should never ask about things that are hidden. I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say that those person who narrate such (private) things are like donkeys having intercourse on the street."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.185).

paras: Another narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) states that when Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) returned after a long absence, Hadhrat Umar (RA) met him and remarked, "You are a most beloved servant of Allaah." Hadhrat Salmaan said, "Then get me married (to one of your daughters)." Hadhrat Umar remained silent. Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) further said, "You consider me a beloved servant of Allaah but are not happy to have me as your son-in-law?"

The next morning, some of Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s family members approached Hadhrat Salmaan (RA). "Do you people need something?" he asked. When they admitted that they did, he said, "What is it? It shall gladly be fulfilled." They said, "We request that you abandon the matter i.e. your proposal to Hadhrat Umar "By Allaah!" Hadhrat Salmaa.n (RA) emphasised, "You should remember well that 1 did not make the proposal because of his being the Khalifah and ruler. The truth is that I thought to myself that because he is a pious man, perhaps Allaah will produce pious offspring from his progeny and mine." Hadhrat Salmaan then got married to a woman from the Kindah tribe. The rest of the narration is like the one above. W The Marriage of Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA)

Hadhrat Thaabit Bunaani reports that Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once went with Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA) to extend a proposal on his behalf for a woman of the Banu Layth tribe. Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) went in to see the family and told them in detail that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) was one of the early Muslims and also recounted his acceptance of Islaam. He then proceeded to mention to them that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) wished to marry a particular girl of their family. Their reply was, "While we do not wish to get Salmaan married (to our daughter), we wouldn't mind getting you married (to her)." They then handed her over in marriage to him and he left.

(When he met Hadhrat Salmaan (RA)) Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "Something has happened that I am too embarrassed to tell you about." "what is it?" Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) asked. When Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) related the incident to him, Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) said, "I should be the one embarrassed since I proposed for a woman whom Allaah had destined for you."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg J 85). Haythami (Vol.4 Pg.291) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Thaabit Bunaani narrates that when Yazeed bin Mu'aawiya sent to Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) a proposal for his daughter Dardaa, he rejected the proposal. One of Yazeed's companions said, "May Allaah mend your affairs. Will you allow me to marry her?" The man persisted, "Then allow me? Allaah will mend your affairs." "Alright," Yazeed said. The man proceeded to propose and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) got him married (to his daughter). The news spread that while Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) rejected Yazeed's proposal, he accepted the proposal of a poor and simple Muslim and then married his daughter to him. Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA)'s comment was, "I did it in the best interests of Dardaa. What do you think would be her condition when (in Yazeed's wealthy household) she has castrated slaves standing over her all the time and when her eyes are dazzled when she sees the (opulent) house? Where will her Deen be then (when she becomes obsessed with worldly wealth)?"
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.251). Imaam Ahmad has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Safwatus Safwah (Vol.1 Pg.260).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Ja'far reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once sent a proposal to Hadhrat Ali (RA) for his daughter ummu Kulthoom's hand in marriage. When Hadhrat Ali (RA) sent a message stating that she was still too young, someone told Hadhrat Umar (RA) that the statement meant that Hadhrat Ali (RA) was refusing. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) explained to Hadhrat Ali (RA) (his reason for wanting to marry her), Hadhrat Ali (RA) (agreed to get her married to him and) said, "(Consider the marriage done, so) I am sending her to you and she is your wife if you are pleased with her." Hadhrat Ali (RA) then sent her to Hadhrat Umar (RA), who (knowing that she was his wife) ventured to lift the garment from her legs. (Not realising that the marriage was already concluded) She however exclaimed, "Leave it! Had you not been the Ameerul Mu'mineen, I would have slapped you across the face!"
sources: Abdur Razzaaq and Sa'eed bin Mansoor, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.291). Ibn Umar Maqdasi has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.4 Pg.492).

paras: Hadhrat Muhammad narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) proposed to Hadhrat Ali (RA) for his daughter Ummu Kulthoom's hand in marriage, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "I am reserving my daughters for the sons of (my brother) ja'far Hadhrat Umar (RA) pleaded, "Please marry her to me because I swear by Allaah that no man on earth will ensure that she is honoured as I will." Hadhrat Ali (RA) agreed and married her to Hadhrat Umar (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) then went to the Muhaajireen and said, "Congratulate me on my new marriage!" They all congratulated him and then asked, "Who did you marry, O Ameerul Mu'mineen?" "The daughter of Ali bin Abi Taalib," he replied. He then started to explain, "Indeed Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Every connection and relation shall be severed on the day of Qiyaamah except my connections and my relations.' I had been a father-in-law of Rasulullaah ﷺ and now I wish this as well (to become his relative by marrying his granddaughter) ." Another narration from Hadhrat Ataa Khuraasaani states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) gave her a dowry of forty thousand Dirhams.
sources: Ibn Sa'd, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.4 Pg.492).

paras: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that Hadhrat Amr bin Hurayth (RA) once proposed for the daughter of Hadhrat Adi bin Haatim (RA). Hadhrat Adi (RA) said, "I shall marry her (to you) only if you fulfil my condition." "What is it?" Hadhrat Amr asked. Hadhrat Adi (RA) explained, "There was indeed a sterling example for you in Rasulullaah ﷺ. I therefore instruct you to pay the dowry Rasulullaah ﷺ gave for Aa'isha, which is a sum of four hundred and eighty Dirhams."

Another narration states that Hadhrat Amr bin Hurayth (RA) sent a proposal for the daughter of Hadhrat Adi bin Haatim (RA) with an appended message to Hadhrat Adi (RA) stating, "Let me know what you decide about me." Hadhrat Adi sent a message stating, "I have decided that you should pay (a dowry of) four hundred and eighty Dirhams, which is the Sunnah of Rasulullaah.
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 8 Pg.299). (2) lbn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.237).

paras: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that when Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) and his brother extended marriage proposals to family from Yemen, Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) said, "I am Bilaal and this is my brother. We were both slaves from Abyssinia. When we were misguided, Allaah guided us and when we were slaves, Allaah set us free. If you marry us (to your daughters), then all praise is due to Allaah (we shall be grateful) and if you refuse, (we will not mind because) Allaah is still the Greatest (and He will open other avenues for us). (The family agreed and got them married), Hadhrat Maymoon reports that one of Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) brothers claimed that he was of Arab descent and considered himself an Arab. When he once proposed for an Arab woman, the family said, "We will marry you only if Bilaal is present." Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) presented himself and after reciting the words of the Khutbah, he said, "I am Bilaal bin Rabaah and this is my brother. He is a man who is poor in his character arid religious practices. You may get him married if you- please and if you chose to refuse him, you are at liberty to do so." The family said, "We shall certainly marry anyone who is a brother of yours." They then got him married.

Hadhrat Urwa bin Ruwaym reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Qurt Thumaali who was a companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ was appointed governor by Hadhrat Umar (RA). He was patrolling the streets of Hims one night when he passed by a bride in front of whom people were lighting several fires. Hadhrat Abdullaah started hitting the people with his whip until they all dispersed. The next morning he sat on his pulpit and after duly praising Allaah, he said, "When Abu Jandalah married Umaamah, he prepared some handfuls of food (as a Waleemah) for (his marriage to) her. May Allaah shower His compassion on Abu Jandalah and may He shower His special mercies on Umaamah. May Allaah however curse your wedding of last night! The people were lighting fires and imitating the Kuffaar whereas Allaah has extinguished their light!"
sources: Surah Nisaa, verse 20.

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that that the dowry Rasulullaah ﷺ gave (her) was twelve Awqiya and a Nash, which totalled an amount of five hundred Dirhams. She then went on to specify that an Awqiya amounted to forty Dirhams and a Nash amounted to twenty Dirhams.

Hadhrat Masrooq narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once mounted the pulpit and said, "I do not know who increased dowries above four hundred Dirhams because the dowry that Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) gave was always four hundred Dirhams or less. Had larger dowries been an act of Taqwa or honour, people would have never beat- Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah to it," After Hadhrat Umar (RA) had alighted from the pulpit, a woman from the Quraysh objected. "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" she said, "Are you forbidding the people from paying dowries in excess of four hundred Dirhams?" When Hadhrat Umar (RA) confirmed it, she said, "Have you then not heard Allaah say in the Qur'aan: '...when you have given one of them (your wives) a fortune (as dowry).
sources: Sa'eed bin Mansoor and Bayhaqi.

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said, "Allaah forgive me! Everyone has more understanding than Umar." He then returned to the pulpit and said, "O people! I had forbidden you from paying dowries in excess of four hundred Dirhams (the prohibition no longer stands). Therefore whoever wishes to give whatever he pleases from his wealth, he may do so."
sources: Abu Umar bin Fadaal in his Amaali, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaa! (Vol.8 Pg.298). (4) ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.298).

paras: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that Hadhrat umar bin Khattaab (RA) once delivered a sermon. After duly praising Allaah, he said, "Take note that you people should not make your dowries exorbitant. If the news ever reaches me that any of you has paid more that what Rasulullaah ﷺ paid or what was paid to him dowry for his daughters), I shall deposit the excess into the public treasury." After Hadhrat Umar (RA) had alighted from the pulpit, a woman from the Quraysh objected. "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" she said, "Is the Book of Allaah more worthy of following or your words?" "The Book of Allaah of course," Hadhrat Umar replied, "what do you mean by this?" She explained, "You just forbade the people from paying dowries in excess of four hundred Dirhams whereas Allaah says in His Book: ...when you have given one of them (your wives) a fortune (as dowry) then- do not take anything from it:..' "
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.298).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) twice or thrice repeated, "Everyone has more understanding than Umar." He then returned to the pulpit and said, "O people! I had forbidden you from paying dowries in excess of four hundred Dirhams (the prohibition no longer stands). A man is at liberty to give whatever he pleases from his wealth."
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol. 4 Pg.284).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "Had (exorbitant) dowries been a source of status and elevation in the Aakhirah, the daughters and wives of Rasulullaah would have been most deserving of it."
Hadhrat Ibn Seereen reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) allowed dowries of two thousand Dirhams while Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) allowed dowries of four thousand.

Hadhrat Naafi reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) married Hadhrat Safiyya for a dowry of four hundred Dirhams. She however returned it saying that it was insufficient. He then added another two hundred Dirhams without Hadhrat Umar (RA) knowing about it.
Hadhrat Ibn Seereen narrates that when Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) married a woman, he sent a hundred slave women to her, each one of them carrying a thousand Dirhams.

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports, "I once brought Rasulullaah ﷺ some Hareerah that I had cooked. Sauda was sitting between between Rasulullaah ﷺ and I, so I told her to have some as well. When she refused, I said, 'If you do not eat, I shall smear it on your face.' She however still refused so I put my hand in the Hareerah and plastered it on her face. Rasulullaah ﷺ laughed as he put his hand in it saying, 'Now you smear her face.' Sauda then smeared it on my face and again Rasulullaah ﷺ laughed. Just then Umar passed by calling out for (someone called) Abdullaah. Thinking that he would soon enter, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Get up and wash your faces!' Thereafter, I always stood in awe of Hadhrat Umar (RA) because of the respect Rasulullaah ﷺ had for him."

Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ lowered his knee for Sauda (to step on) so that she could get even with me. She then took some (Hareerah) from the dish and spread it on my face as Rasulullaah ﷺ laughed."
sources: Abu Ya'la Haythami (Vol. 4 Pg.316) has commented on the chain of narrators. Ibn Asaakir has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Unimaal (Vol. Pg 393), as has lbn Najjaar, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal Pg.302),

paras: Hadhrat Razeenah (RA) who was a freed slave of Rasulullaah ﷺ reports that Hadhrat Sauda Yamaaniyyah (RA) once visited Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) at a time when Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) was with her. Hadhrat Sauda (RA) arrived looking stunning and well-dressed with a Yemeni shawl and matching scarf. She also wore two spots of aloe and saffron on their places (near her eyes) which resembled two pimples. A narrator called Ulayla says that she found women beautifying themselves with aloe and saffron.

Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) said to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "O Ummul Mu'mineen! Rasulullaah ﷺ is due to arrive when this woman is gleaming here between us." "Fear Allaah, O Hafsah!" Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) warned. However, Hadhrat Hafsah said, "I am going to ruin her adornment for her." Hadhrat Sauda who was hard of hearing asked, "What are you two saying?" "O Sauda!" Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) said, "The one-eyed (Dajjaal) has appeared!" "Really!

Hadhrat Sauda (RA). cried out. She was extremely shocked and started to shiver. "Where shall I hide?" she asked. 'You will have to go to the tent," Hadhrat Hafsah told her. The tent was made of palm leaves and was a hiding place for the people, it was however filled with dirt and spider webs. Hadhrat Sauda went to hide there as Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived. Seeing the two women laughing so much that they were unable to talk, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "What is all the laughter about?" Rasulullaah ﷺ had to repeat the question thrice before they pointed towards the tent. Rasulullaah ﷺ went to the tent where he found Hadhrat Sauda (RA) shivering (with fear). "What is the matter, O Sauda?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. "O Rasulullaah iii?!" she said, "The one-eyed one has appeared." "He has not appeared," Rasulullaah ﷺ clarified, "but he is still to appear. He has not appeared but is still to appear." Rasulullaah ﷺ then helped her out and dusted the dirt and spider webs off her.
sources: Maghaafer is the odorous resin of a particular type of palm tree called the Urfut palm.

paras: Another narration adds that Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) said to Hadhrat Aa'isha "Rasulullaah ilil is coming to see us and we are looking so unkempt while she is gleaming between us." Rasulullaah ﷺ Relationship with Hadhrat Aa'isha Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was sitting down when he heard the people and children making a lot of noise. (When he looked out) He saw some Abyssinians dancing with the people around them. Aa'isha!' Rasulullaah ﷺ called out, 'Come and have a look.' Placing my cheek against his shoulder, I started looking from between his shoulders and head, 'o Aa'isha,' Rasulullaah ﷺ kept saying I kept looking for a long time), 'have you not had your fill?' To assess my status with Rasulullaah ﷺ, I kept saying that I had not. I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ taking support on one leg and then the other (as he grew tired of standing so long), when Umar appeared, the people and children all dispersed and Rasulullaah ilii remarked, 'I see the human and Jinn devils all flee from Umar The narration still continues further.
sources: Bukhaari and Muslim.

paras: In another narration, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "By Allaah! I saw Rasulullaah standing at the door of my room as some Abyssinians amused the people with their spears in the of the) Masjid. Rasulullaah ﷺ screened me with his shawl as I watched their feats between his ear and shoulder. Rasulullaah ﷺ then remained standing because of me until I tired and) turned away. You can well imagine how eager a young girl (as I) is for amusement (and for how long I stood watching)."

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to spend time at Zaynab bint jahash's place drinking honey, Hafsah and I therefore collaborated and that whichever of us Rasulullaah ﷺ came to would tell him, 'I get the smell of. Have you eaten Maghaafeer (suggesting that the bees that made the honey ate Maghafeer).' Consequently, when Rasulullaah ﷺ came to one of us, she said the piece. Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'Not at all. But I did have honey by Zaynab bint jahash. I shall however never do so again.' It was then that Allaah revealed the verses: idsa 01 O Nabi ﷺ In seeking the pleasure of your wives, why do you declare unlawful that which Allaah has made lawful for you? Allaah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful. Allaah has ordained that you release yourselves from your oaths (such as this one and pay the relevant Kaffaara). Allaah is your Protecting Friend and He is the All Knowing, the Wise, (The Incident deserves mention) When the Nabi ﷺ whispered something to one of his wives (Rasulullaah ﷺ 's statement, "But I did have honey") and she informed (another of his wives) about it. When Allaah disclosed this to him, he made a part of it (his knowledge of the incident) known (to her) and ignored a part of it (to save her from added embarrassment). When he informed her about it, she exclaimed, "Who told you about it?" He replied, "The All Knowing, The Informed One told me." If the two of you (Hafsa and Aa'isha) repent to Allaah, then your hearts have surely turned (turned back towards the best course after straying for a while). (Surah Tahreem, verses 1-4)

Hadhrat Hishaam says that the words "When the Nabi ﷺ whispered something to one of his wives" refer to the statement Rasulullaah ﷺ made to one of his wives when he said, "1 shall never do so (drink honey) again and this is a vow. However, you should not inform anyone about this." ® Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ loved sweet things and honey.

After performing the Asr salaah, it was his practice to visit all his wives and get close to one of them. When he once went to Hafsah the daughter of Hadhrat Umar (RA), he stayed longer than he usually stayed. Overcome with covetousness, I made enquiries about this and was informed that a woman from her family had given her a container of honey, which she mixed into a drink and gave Rasulullaah ﷺ , 'By Allaah!' I resolved, 'I am definitely going to make some scheme.'

I then said to Sauda bint Zam'ah, 'Rasulullaah (Self will soon be coming to you. When he gets close to you, ask him whether he ate Maghaafeer. When he tells you that he has not eaten any, ask him what it is then that you can smell. He will then tell you that Hafsah gave him a drink of honey, to which you should say, 'The bee must have sucked nectar from the Urfut palm (the palm containing Maghaafeer)! I will also say the same thing and you O Saflyya should also do likewise."

Hadhrat Sauda (RA) later reported (to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA)), "By Allaah! Because of my fear for you, I almost called out what you told while Rasulullaah was still standing at the door. (Controlling myself however) When he drew closer, I said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ -Have you eaten Maghaafeer? 'No,' he replied. 'Then what is that I smell on you?' I asked. He replied, 'Hafsah gave me a drink of honey.' I then said, 'The bee must have sucked nectar from the Urfut palm.'" When Rasulullaah ﷺ went to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), shealsosaid the same thing and Hadhrat Safiyya (RA) also followed suit. When Rasulullaah ﷺ again went to Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) and she offered him some honey to drink, he declined saying, "I do not need any." "By Allaah!" Hadhrat Sauda (RA) said to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "we have stopped Rasulullaah ﷺ from honey." "Be quiet!" Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) told her.

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports, "I had always been eager to ask Umar about the two wives of Rasulullaah ﷺ concerning whom Allaah says(intheQur'aan): 'If the two of you repent to Allaah, then your hearts have surely turned (turned back towards the best course after straying for a while)! (Surah Tahreem, verse 4) This (thought) lingered on until the time when Umar performed Hajj and I performed Hajj with him. We were still travelling when Umar went off the road (to answer the call the nature). I also veered off taking a jug (of water) along with me. After he had completed, Umar SI came to me and I started pouring water into his hands as he made wudhu. 'O Ameerul Mu'mineen!' I said, 'Who were the two wives of Rasulullaah ﷺ concerning whom Allaah says: If the two of .you repent to Allaah, then your hearts have surely turned (turned back towards the best course after straying for a whiiej.'?" (Surah Tahreem, verse 4) Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "I am surprised at you, O Ibn Abbaas! (That despite your vast knowledge, you are still unaware of this incident)." Hadhrat Zuhri comments that although Hadhrat Umar (RA) was surprised at the question, he still proceeded to relate it in detail without concealing anything. "They were Hafsah and Aa'isha," Hadhrat umar IR began. He then started narrating the incident. He said, "We members of the Quraysh always had the upper hand over our wives. When we arrived in Madinah, we encountered people (the Ansaar) whose women had the upper hand over them. Our women then started learning from their women. My house was located in the vicinity of the Banu Urnayyah bin Zaid, which was in the upper reaches of Madinah. When I became angry with my wife one day (and told her something), she surprised me by backchatting. When I objected to her backchatting, shesaid, What are you objecting about my backchatting when I can swear by Allaah that the wives of Rasulullaah ﷺ backchat to him? In fact some of them (when angry) shun him morning to evening.' I then left the house and went to (my daughter) Hafsah. 'Do you backchat Rasulullaah ﷺ When she replied in the affirmative, I asked further, 'Does any of you (when angry) shun Rasulullaah ﷺ morning to evening?' When she again replied in the affirmative, I said, Whichever of you does that is at a loss and destroyed! Does any of you not fear that Allaah would be angry with her because His Rasool ﷺ is angry with her? She will then most certainly be destroyed. You should never backchat Rasulullaah ﷺ and never ask him for anything. Rather ask from me whatever you please and never be deceived by the fact that your companion (Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA)) is prettier than you and more beloved to Rasulullaah ﷺ (do not emulate everything she does).'

I had a friend from amongst the Ansaar who took turns with me in attending Rasulullaah ﷺ's gatherings. He would go one day and I the next so that he brought me the news of revelation one day and I brought it to him the next day. It was during the time when there was a lot of talk about the Ghassaan tribe preparing themselves to attack us when my friend came to me at night. Knocking at my door, he called for me until I came out. 'Something serious has taken place," he said, 'what is it?' I asked, 'Have the Ghassaan tribe come?' 'No,' he replied, 'it is more serious than that and with longer lasting implications. Rasulullaah ﷺ has divorced his wives!' 'Hafsah is at a loss and destroyed!' I cried, 'I had a feeling that this would happen.' After performing the Fajr salaah, I dressed and went down (to Madinah) where I went to see Hafsah. She was in tears. 'Has Rasulullaah ﷺ divorced you?' I queried. 'I do not know,' she replied, 'but he is now there in the upper story room.' 1 went to Rasulullaah ﷺ's Abyssinian slave and asked him to seek permission from Rasulullaah ﷺ for me to enter. The slave went in and then emerged saying, 'I mentioned your name to him but Rasulullaah ﷺ merely remained silent; i then left and went towards the pulpit where I saw a group sitting, some of them in tears. I sat for awhile, but then my anxiety got the better of me and I went back to the slave saying, 'Seek permission for Umar.' Again the slave went in and then emerged saying, 'I mentioned your name to him but Rasulullaah ﷺ merely remained silent.'. I again left to sit near the pulpit but again my anxiety got the better of me and I returned to request the slave to seek permission for me to enter. Yet again the slave went in and emerged saying, 'I mentioned your name to him but he merely remained silent.' As I turned to leave, the slave suddenly called for me saying. You may enter, for Rasulullaah ﷺ has granted you permission.' When I entered, I four.d Rasulullaah ﷺ reclining against a straw mat that had left imprints on his side. 'Have you divorced your wives, O Rasulullaah ﷺ I asked. Raising his head, he replied, 'Allaahu Akbar!' I cried out. I then said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ You have seen that we the members of the Quraysh always had the upper hand over our wives. When we arrived in Madinah, we encountered people Ansaar) whose women had the upper hand over them. Our women then started learning from their women. When I became angry with my wife one day (and told her something), she surprised me by back chatting. When I objected to her back chatting, she said, What are you objecting about my back chatting when I can swear by Allaah that the wives of Rasulullaah ilif backchat to him? In fact some of them (when angry) shun him morning to evening. I said, of them does that is at a loss and destroyed! Does any of them not fear that Allaah would be angry with her because His Rasool ﷺ is angry with her? She will then most certainly be destroyed.' This made Rasulullaah ﷺ smile. - 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ I continued, 'I then went to Hafsah and told her, 'Never be deceived by the fact that your companion (Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA)) is prettier than you and more beloved to Rasulullaah ﷺ Rasulullaah ﷺ smiled again. Then I asked, 'Should I continue with this light-hearted talk?' 'By all means,' Rasulullaah ﷺ said. I then sat down and I swear by Allaah that when I looked about the room, all I saw was three pieces of undyed leather. 'O Rasulullaah I said, 'Pray to Allaah to grant an abundance of wealth to your Ummah. Allaah has given abundance to the Romans and Persians even though they do not worship Him he will readily give us as well).'

Rasulullaah ﷺ then sat up straight and said, 'Are you also in doubt, O son of Khattaab? They are people whose rewards (for their good deeds) have been brought forward to this world (without any share left for the Aakhirah).' I then quickly said, 'Do seek forgiveness for me, O Rasulullaah ﷺ .' Because he was so angry with them at the time, Rasulullaah till had vowed not to go to his wives for an entire month until Allaah directed him otherwise."
sources: Ahmad, Bukhaari, Muslim, Tirmidhi and Nasa'ee.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ separated from his wives, I entered the Masjid where I saw the people fondling pebbles as they said, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ has divorced his wives!' This incident took place before the injunction of Hijaab was ordained, I said to myself, 'I am going to find out properly what is happening Rasulullaah g!8f had divorced them or not).'" The Hadith continues to mention how Hadhrat Umar (RA) went to both Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) as well as Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) to admonish them. Thereafter, the narration quotes Hadhrat Umar (RA) who says, "When I then went to Rasulullaah ﷺ, I found him on the doorstep of the room on the upper storey. I called out saying, 'O Secure permission for me to see Rasulullaah ﷺ ..."' The rest of the narration is like the one above until the part where Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "O Rasulullaah iffif ! Do not let the matter of your wives disturb you. If you have divorced them, then Allaah is with you as well as His angels, Jibreel, Mikaal, myself, Abu Bakr and all the Mu'mineen. I praise Allaah for the fact that whenever I "spoke, I had firm hope that Allaah would confirm what I said. It was therefore with reference to this that Allaah revealed the following verse: if the two of you and Aa'isha, two wives of Rasulullaah ﷺ repent to Allaah, then your hearts have surely turned (turned back towards the best course after straying for a while.). However, if you two assist each other against him (Rasulullaah ﷺ), then his protecting friends are Allaah, Jibreel and the pious Mu'mineen. Besides these, the angels are also his assistants. If he (Rasulullaah ﷺ) has to divorce all of you (wives), then his Rabb shall certainly replace you with wives better than yourselves who will be Muslims, Mu'minaat, obedient, repentant, worshippers, women who fast, previously married women and virgins. (Surah Tahreem, verses 4,5)

'Have you divorced them?' I asked. 'No,' Rasulullaah ﷺ replied. I then stood at the door of the Masjid and called out in my loudest voice, "Rasulullaah ﷺ's wives have not been divorced!' it was with reference to this that Allaah revealed the verse: :s.uaJl 5j_j-j) '1 J-)'

When fftews o/? any matter of peace or fear comes to them, they (immediately) broadcast it (thereby causing harm to the Muslims). If they had (first) referred the matter to the Rasulullaah ﷺ and to those of them who have understanding (to the learned Muslims with insight), it would surely be known to those of them who research (verify) the matter. (Surah Nisaa, verse 83)
Hadhrat Umar (RA) continues, "it was I who researched this matter."
sources: Muslim, as quoted in Tafseerot Ibn Katheer (Vol.4 Pg.389). Abdur Razzaaq, lbn Sa'd, lbn Hibbaan, Bayhaqi, lbn Jareer, lbn Mundhir, lbn Mardway and other have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kaniul ' t/mmaaJ Pg.269).

paras: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was sitting in his house while the Sahabah (RA) were sitting by his door. When Hadhrat Abu Bakr arrived and sought permission to enter, Rasulullaah ﷺ did not grant him permission. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then arrived and Rasulullaah ﷺ did not grant him permission to enter either. Rasulullaah ﷺ later granted permission to both Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) and they both entered the room where Rasulullaah ﷺ was sitting in silence with his wives around him. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to himself, "I am going to say something to make Rasulullaah ﷺ laugh." He then proceeded to say, "O Rasulullaah fli?! If only you had seen (my wife) the daughter of Zaid just now when I slapped her across the neck when she asked me for (an increase in her) allowance!" Rasulullaah ﷺ smiled so broadly that his molars became visible. He said, "Here are my wives around me also asking me for (an increase in) their allowances."

Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then stood up to hit (his daughter) Hadhrat Aa'isha and Hadhrat Umar (RA) also got up to hit (his daughter) Hadhrat Hafsah Both men were rebuking their daughters saying, "How can you ask Rasulullaah ﷺ for something he does not have?!" Rasulullaah ﷺ however stopped the two men and the women said, "By Allaah! After this, we shall never again ask Rasulullaah iil? for something he does not have." It was on this occasion that Allaah revealed the verse offering a choice (to Rasulullaah ﷺ wives). Rasulullaah ﷺ first approached Hadhrat Aa'isha saying, "I am about to present to you an offer that I do not want you to be hasty in deciding until you have consulted with your parents." "What is it?" she asked. Rasulullaah ﷺ then recited for her the verse: O Nabi ﷺ Say to your wives, "if you desire the life of this world and its adornments, then come forward. I shall grant you a generous provision and separate from you (divorce you) in a cordial manner.

However, if you desire Allaah, His Rasool ﷺ and the home of the Aakhirah, then (you may continue enjoying the status of being his wives and living with the allowance he provides because) Allaah has certainly prepared a grand reward for those of you who do good deeds (Allaah will reward you tremendously for your sacrifice)." (Surah Ahzaab, verses 28,29)

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) immediately said, "Should I consult my parents about (having) you?! I definitely choose Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ. Please do not inform any of your other wives what I have decided." Rasulullaah ﷺ told her, "Allaah has sent me to make matters easy for people and not to make them difficult Therefore, if any of them asks me about you decision, I will certainly inform her,"
sources: Abu Dawood, as quoted in Mishkaatul Masaabeeh (Pg.373). (2) lbn Najjaar, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.l 19),

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas Slifflg reports that Hadhrat Aa'isha HIS said, "When the verses giving (us) the choice were revealed, Rasulullaah ﷺ began with me before any of his other wives. He said, 'I am about to present to you a choice about which you are in no hurry to decide until you have consulted with your parents.' Rasulullaah ﷺ said this despite knowing well that my parents would never tell me to separate from Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ then continued, 'Allaah says: Sp-?! a-5j2 O Nabi ﷺ Say to your wives, "If you desire the life of this world and its adornments, then come forward. I shall grant you a generous provision and separate from you (divorce you) in a cordial manner.

However, if you desire Allaah, His Rasool ﷺ and the home of the Aakhirah, then (you may continue enjoying the status of being his wives and living with the allowance he provides because) Allaah has certainly prepared a grand reward for those of you who do good deeds (Allaah will reward you tremendously for your sacrifice)." (Surah Ahzaab, verses 28,29)

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "I immediately .said, "Is there anything to consult my parents about? I certainly want Allaah, His Rasool ﷺ and the home of the Aakhirah.'" Rasulullaah ﷺ then presented the choice to all his wives and the reply each of them gave was similar to that of Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA)
Another narration quotes that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "When Rasulullaah gave us a choice and we chose (to remain with) him, he did not count this (choice as a divorce) against us."

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to her, "I know exactly when you are happy with me and when you are angry." When she asked Rasulullaah ﷺ how he knew that, he replied, "When you are happy with me, you say, 'No, by the Rabb of Muhammad ﷺ and when you are angry with me, you say, 'No, by the Rabb of Ibraheem "That's true," Hadhrat Aa'isha fi said, "but it is only your name that I leave out (while the love for you in my heart remains just as strong)."
sources: Bayhaqi and lbn Najjaar.

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates, "I was once on a journey with Rasulullaah ﷺ when I ran a race with him and beat him. After I had put on some weight, I again ran a race with him, but this time he beat me. He then said, 'This is in lieu of the lastrace.".

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) relates, "(As a young boy) I was once the guest of (my maternal aunt) Maymoona on a night when she was not performing salaah. She brought one shawl and then another, which she lay it down by the head-side of the bedding. She then lay down, pulled the shawl over her and made a bed for me beside her. I shared her pillow with her. Rasulullaah arrived after performing the Isha salaah and when he reached the bed, he took the shawl lying by the head-side of the bed and tied it as a lower garment. Thereafter, he removed the two garments he was wearing, hung them up and got in to the bed with his wife.

Towards the final hours of the night, he got up and took a water bag that was hanging there. He opened it and started making wudhu. I was about to get up to pour the water for him when it occurred to me that I would not like him to know that I had been awake. He then came to the bed, got dressed in his two garments and removed the shawl. Thereafter, he stood at the place where he performed salaah and started performing salaah. I also got up, made wudhu and stood on his left. Rasulullaah ﷺ held me from his back and made me stand on his right. With me following him, he then proceeded to perform thirteen Rakaahs of salaah. Rasulullaah ﷺ then sat down and as I sat beside him, his cheek leaned towards mine (as he fell asleep) and I could hear him breathing like a sleeping person. Bilaal then arrived and called out, 'Salaah, O Rasulullaah ﷺ Rasulullaah ﷺ then stood up in the place where he performed salaah and started performing two Rakaahs salaah as Bilaal started calling out the Iqaamah."

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that when an old woman once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he asked her who she was. When she informed him that her name was Jathaamah Muzaniyyah. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "You are now Hasaanah Muzaniyyah." He then proceeded to ask her how they were, how was their life and how they had been since he last met them. "May my parents be sacrificed for you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ !" she said, "We have been well." After she had left, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ ! You gave such an excellent reception to the old lady?" "Dear Aa'isha," Rasulullaah ﷺ explained, "She used to visit us when Khadeeja was alive. Maintaining old acquaintances is a part of imaan."

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, 'When a particular old woman used to visit Nabi he always became very happy and would honour her greatly. 'May my parents be sacrificed for you!' I said, You treat this woman better than you treat anyone else.1 Rasulullaah iisl explained, 'She used to visit us when Khadeeja was alive. Do you not know that honouring bonds of affection is a part of Imaan?'"

Hadhrat Abu Tufayl (RA) relates, "I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ distributing meat in Ji'irraanah when I was a young boy who could carry only the limb of a camel. When a particular lady came to him, he spread out his shawl for her (to sit on). When I asked someone who she was, I was informed that she was the woman who suckled him as a baby."
sources: Ahmad, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg. 1 7). (3) lbn Asaakir and Muslim. (4) lbn Asaakir. (5) lbn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaai ' (Vol.5 Pg.222).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) reports that when he once went to see Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ 's short Abyssinian slave was busy rubbing his back. "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "Did you hurt yourself?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "The camel dropped me down last night."
sources: Abu Ya'la, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaai (Vol. 7 Pg.106) and Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.9 Pg.182). Bazzaar and lbn Sahaaheen have alsq reported the narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaai. (7) lbn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaai (Vol . 7 Pg. 1 04) .

paras: Hadhrat Qaasim bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood used to put on Rasulullaah ﷺ 's shoes for him. He would then walk ahead with Rasulullaah ﷺ 's staff in his hand. When Rasulullaah ﷺ reached the gathering, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) would remove Rasulullaah ﷺ's shoes, place it under his arms and hand the staff over. As soon as Rasulullaah ﷺ decided to get up, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood would give him his shoes and again walk ahead with the staff until he entered the room before Rasulullaah Sip.
Another narration state that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) used to screen Rasulullaah ﷺ when he bathed, would wake him up when he slept and would walk about with him when there was no one else.

Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived in Madinah, I was a young boy of ten and when he passed away, I was only twenty. It was my mother and aunts who encouraged me to serve Rasulullaah ﷺ.

Hadhrat Thumaamah narrates that when someone asked Hadhrat Anas (RA) whether he was present during the Battle of Badr, he replied, "Shame on you! How could I ever absent myself?" Hadhrat Muhammad bin Abdullaah Ansaari reports that Hadhrat Anas (RA) accompanied Rasulullaah ﷺ to Badr to serve him while he was still a young boy.

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that there were twenty youngsters from the Ansaar who always stuck close to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ would always dispatch them whenever he needed something done. ''' Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) reports that there were always four or five Sahabah (RA) who never parted from Rasulullaah ﷺ (when on journey) or from Rasulullaah ﷺ's door (when at home).

Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri SI relates, "We used to take turns (to be at Rasulullaah ﷺ's service) so that we could fulfil any need he had or he could dispatch us for any errand. Eventually, the people anticipating rewards (for this service) increased and there were plenty of people taking turns. As we were one day discussing Dajjaal, Rasulullaah ﷺ came out to ask, 'What are these whispered discussions all about? Have I not forbidden you from whispered discussion?

Hadhrat Assim bin Sufyaan says that it was either Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) or Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) whom he heard say, "I once sought permission from Rasulullaah ﷺ to spend the night at his door so that he could awaken me for any need he may have. Rasulullaah ﷺ granted permission and 1 spent the night there."

Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) reports, "I once performed salaah with Rasulullaah during the month of Ramadhaan. He then got up to take a bath and I screened him. When some water was left over in the container, he said, 'If you wish, you may use it to bath, otherwise, you may add some more water to it.' 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ !' I replied, 'This left-over water of yours is more beloved to me than anything more I may add.' When I then started to bath, Rasulullaah ﷺ screened me. 'You need not screen me,' I said. He replied, 'Why not? I must screen you just as you screened me.

Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "I have never seen anyone more compassionate towards his family than Rasulullaah ﷺ. His son Ibraheem was given to a woman in the upper reaches of Madinah for suckling. With us in his company, Rasulullaah ﷺ used to go to the house, which would be filled with smoke because the nursing mother's husband was a blacksmith. Rasulullaah ﷺ would always pick up the child and kiss him before leaving." Hadhrat Amr (RA) reports that when Ibraheem passed away, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Ibraheem was my son and (Val-2) 701 has passed away while still suckling. Verily he shall have two nursing mothers in Jannah who will complete his period of suckling."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Haarith (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to place Abdullaah, Ubaydullaah and Katheer, all the children of Hadhrat Abbaas in a line and would then promise a prize to whichever of them beat the others to him. They would then race towards him and jump on to his back and chest as he hugged and kissed them.

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) reports, "Whenever Rasulullaah giif returned from a journey, the children of his family were brought to receive him. When he once returned from a journey, I was brought first to him so he placed me in front of him (on the animal). Thereafter, one of Faatima 's children either Hasan or Husayn was brought to him and he placed him behind him. When we entered Madinah, we were therefore three people on the animal."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) also narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once passed by me as I was playing with some children. He then picked me up together with one of Abbaas's children and placed us on his animal. We were therefore three on the animal."

In another narration, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) says, 'You should have seen the time when we were children and I would be playing with Ubaydullaah and Quthm, both the sons of Abbaas. Passing by, Rasulullaah ﷺ would say, 'Pick that child up and give him to me.' (I was then passed to him and) He would then put me in front of him. Thereafter, Rasulullaah iii? would say, 'Pick that child up and give him to me.' He would then put the other child behind him. Although Abbaas liked Ubaydullaah more than Quthm, Rasulullaah ﷺ would not be embarrassed in front of his uncle (Abbaas) to take Quthm on the animal and leave Ubaydullaah. Rasulullaah ﷺ would then pass his hand over my head thrice and say each time, 'O Allaah! You be Ja'far's successor for his children.".

Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) says, "When I saw Hasan and Husayn riding on Rasulullaah ﷺ's shoulders, I remarked, "What a fine horse you two are riding?' Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, 'And what fine horsemen are they!?

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once came out of the house carrying Hadhrat Hasan (RA) on his shoulders when someone commented, "Dear child! What a fine conveyance you have!" To this Rasulullaah said, "And he is a mighty fine rider too."

Hadhrat Baraa bin Aazib (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once performing salaah when Hadhrat Hasan (RA) and Hadhrat husayn (RA) or (1) Muslim (vol.2 Pg.254). Ahmad has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.45). one of them (the narrator is unsure) arrived and climbed upon his back. When Rasulullaah ﷺ got up, he held the child or the two children with his hand and (after completing the salaah) said, "What an excellent mount you had mounted." )

Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says that he once went to Rasulullaah ﷺ as he was on all fours with Hadhrat Hasan (RA) and Hadhrat Husayn (RA) on his back. Rasulullaah ﷺ was saying, "You two have an excellent camel and are both excellent loads,"
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.182).

paras: Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) reports that it was midday when they were sitting around Rasulullaah tflf and Hadhrat Ummu Ayman (RA) arrived saying, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Hasan and Husayn are lost!" Rasulullaah ﷺ said to the Sahabah (RA), "Get up and look for my sons!" Every person went in the direction he was facing and Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) went in the direction Rasulullaah ﷺ went. Rasulullaah ﷺ kept searching until he was at the foot of a mountain when he saw the two boys clinging on to each other. In front of them was a snake standing on its tail with flames flashing from its mouth (Allaah had perhaps sent it to ensure that the boys ventured no further). As Rasulullaah darted towards it, it turned to look at him and then slid away into a hole. Rasulullaah ﷺ then went to the boys and as he separated them, he wiped their faces saying, "May my parents be sacrificed for you! How honourable you two are in the sight of Allaah!" when he then carried one of them on his right shoulder and the other on his left shoulder, Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) remarked, "Glad tidings to you two. What an excellent mount you have!" To this, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "What excellent riders are they and their father is even better than them."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.182) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "We were with Rasulullaah ﷺ when we were invited for a meal. When we came across Husayn playing with other children in the street, Rasulullaah ﷺ ran ahead of the others and stretched out his hands (to grab the boy). Husayn started running to and fro as Rasulullaah ﷺ made him laugh in front of everyone there. Rasulullaah ﷺ then stretched out his arms and held the boy with one hand on his chin and the other between his head and ears. Thereafter, Rasulullaah ﷺ hugged and kissed him saying, 'Husayn is from me and I am from him. May Allaah love those who love him. Hasan and Husayn are two (distinguished) grandsons from amongst grandsons. ".
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.182) has commented on the chain of narrators. Tabraani has reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Ya'la bin Murrah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.107).

paras: Hadhrat ibn is'haaq Sabee'ee reports that the wife of Hadhrat uthmaan bin Madh'oon once came to the wives of Rasulullaah ﷺ dressed in unattractive and old clothes. When they asked her what the problem was, she informed them that her husband stood in salaah all night and fasted all day (and therefore had no time for her, because of which she felt no need to look attractive), when Rasulullaah ﷺ was informed of what she said, he met Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA), rebuked him and said, "Do you not have an excellent example in me?" Hadhrat uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA) replied, "Certainly. May my parents be sacrificed for you!" Thereafter, his wife was always looking attractive and wearing enchanting scents. On his deathbed, his wife recited some couplets (which meant): "Dear eyes! Be generous with your tears and never let them stop Over the demise of Uthmaan bin Madh'oon Over a man who spent the entire night pleasing his Creator Over the loss of someone who will be buried. Glad tidings ofjannah to him!

Baqee ^ and its Gharqad trees are graced to be his home And after being troubled (by having Kuffaar buried there), the ground shall be illuminated All that the heart shall inherit will be grief that knows no end Until death comes, my tear ducts shall never dry"
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg,l06). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.394) has reported a similar narration without the couplets.

paras: Another narration names the wife of Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA) as Hadhrat Khowla bint Hakeem (RA) and that it was Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) whom she visited. The narration also states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said to Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA) Uthmaan! Monasticism has not been ordained or us. Am I not a perfect example for you? By Allaah! It is I who fears most and who is most mindful of the limits He has set."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.305) .

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas reports, "My father got me married to a woman from the Quraysh. However, when she first came to me, I paid no attention to her because of my overriding enthusiasm for acts of Ibaadah such as salaah and fasting. (My father) Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) once came to his daughter-in-law (my wife) and asked, 'How do you find your husband?' She ( 1 ) The graveyard of Madinah. replied, 'He is the best of husbands but has not yet ventured to expose any part of my body and has not even come near our bed.' My father then came to me and rebuked me most severely. Biting into me with his tongue, he said, 'I got you married to an honourable lady of the Quraysh and you have left her dangling in suspension?!' After enumerating more of the things I was doing, he then went to complain about me to Rasulullaah ﷺ.

Rasulullaah ﷺ sent for me and when I arrived, he verified, 'Do you fast every day?' Yes,' I replied. He then asked further, 'And do you stand in salaah all night?' When I again replied in the affirmative, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'But while 1 fast regularly, there are also days when I do not fast. While I perform salaah (at night) I also sleep and I also touch my wives. Whoever turns away from my way of life cannot be my follower.' Rasulullaah ﷺ then proceeded to say, 'Complete a recitation of the Qur'aan once a month.' 'But I can do more than that,' I said. 'Then complete it once every ten days,' Rasulullaah ﷺ permitted. When I ' insisted that I could do more than that as well, Rasulullaah ﷺ told me that I could then complete a recitation in three days.

Thereafter, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Fast only three days a month.' when I informed Rasulullaah ﷺ that I was capable of much more, he continued increasing the number of days until he finally said, 'Then fast one day and skip the next. This is the best type of fast and was the manner in which my brother Dawood used to fast.'"

In his narration, Hadhrat Husayn states that Rasulullaah ﷺ added, "Every keen worshipper has a period of great enthusiasm but every such period comes with a waning phase. When this phase comes, the person either resorts to the Sunnah or towards Bid'ah. Whoever during this phase resorts towards the Sunnah has been rightly guided and whoever turns towards Bid'ah has been destroyed."

Hadhrat Mujaahid says that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas grew old and weak, he would fast several days consecutively and then skip several days to regain his strength. When reciting the Qur'aan he would also sometimes recite more and sometimes less. Nevertheless, he would ensure that he completed a recitation within a period of either seven days or three days. Thereafter (when he grew even weaker), he would say, "Had I accepted the concession Rasulullaah ﷺ offered me, I would have liked it more than what (extra Ibaadah) he had to send my way (because of my insistence). However, (I shall now not reduce it because) I would not like to do anything other than what I was doing at the time I separated from Rasulullaah ﷺ (when he passed away)."
sources: Bukhaari (Vol.1 Pg.264). Abu Nu'aym has also reported the narration in his Pg.188), as quoted in Kanzul Um/naaftyoll Pg.137). Tirmidhi, Bazzaar, Ibn Khuzaymah, Daar Qutni, Tabraani and ibn Hibbaan have also reported the narration, as quoted in Fat'hul Baari (Vol.4 Pg.l5l). Ibn Sa'd (Vol. 4 Pg.85) has also reported the narration in different words.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Juhayfah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ had made a bond of brotherhood between Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA). When Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) once came to visit, Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA), he found (his wife) Hadhrat Ummu Dardaa (RA) in a dishevelled condition. When he enquired what the matter was, she replied, "Your brother Abu Dardaa has no need for this world." Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) then arrived and when he got a meal prepared for Hadhrat Salmaan (RA), he said, "You eat because I am fasting." Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) refused saying, "I shall not eat until you eat." Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) was then forced to (terminate the fast and) join in the meal.

That night when Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) started to perform salaah, Hadhrat Salmaan instructed him to sleep. Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) slept awhile and was again about to get up when Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) again told him to go back to sleep. It was only when the night was drawing to an end that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) said to Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA), 'You may now get up." The two men then performed (Tahajjud) salaah. Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) then advised Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) saying, "You have rights owing to your Rabb as well as rights owing to your body and rights owing to your wife. You should therefore give every recipient their due rights." When Hadhrat Abu Dardaa reported the matter to Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Salmaan is right."

Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) the daughter of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) relates, "When Zubayr married me, he possessed neither any property, money, slaves nor anything else apart from his horse. I used to feed his horse for him, tend to it and care for it. I also used to crush the date stones to feed his camel that drew water from the well and fed it myself. In addition to this, I would give it water to drink, sew the water bags (that the camel used to draw water) and knead dough. However, because I was not good at making the bread, my Artsaar neighbours would do it for me. They were extremely sincere and true friends. I used to carry the date stones on my head from the property Rasulullaah ﷺ gave to Zubayr, which lay two-thirds of a Farsakh (approximately two miles) from Madinah. As I was coming one day with the date stones on my head, I met with Rasulullaah llli and some Sahabah (RA). Rasulullaah ﷺ called for me as he instructed his camel to sit so that I may ride on it behind him. I was however too shy to travel with men and also thought of Zubayr's possessiveness. He was one of the most possessive people to be found. When Rasulullaah ﷺ realised that I was too shy, he carried on. When I met Zubayr, I said to him, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ and a few Sahabah met me while I was carrying the date stones on my head. When he made his camel sit down for me to ride on, I felt too shy and also thought of your possessiveness.' He said, 'By Allaahl Your carrying the date stones is more difficult for me to bear than your riding with Rasulullaah ﷺ This continued until (my father) Abu Bakr sent me a servant who relieved me of tending to the horse and it seemed like he had set me free."
sources: IbnSa'd(VoI.8Pg.251).

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) the daughter of Hadhrat Abu Bakr was married to Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awwaam (RA). When she complained to her father about her husband's strict nature, Hadhrat Abu Bakr said, "Dear daughter! Be patient because when a woman has a pious husband and she does not remarry after he dies, Allaah will reunite them in jannah." .
