Hadhrat Kahmas Hilaali reports that they were once sitting with Hadhrat Umar when a lady arrived. She sat down and said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! While the evil nature of my husband has increased, his good nature has dwindled." "Who is your husband?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. When she informed him that her husband was a man called Abu Salamah, Hadhrat Umar said, "He was a companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ and is a righteous man." He then asked the men around him, "Is he not so?" "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" they replied, "We know him to be just as you say." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then instructed someone sitting there to call for the husband. When her husband was sent for, the lady got up and sat behind Hadhrat Umar (RA). It was not long before the two men arrived together and the husband sat in front of Hadhrat Umar (RA). "What has this woman sitting behind me have to say?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. "Who is she, O Ameerul Mu'mineen?" the man asked. "She is your wife," Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied. "And what has she to say?" he asked. Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "She claims that while your evil nature has increased, your good nature has dwindled." The husband said, "A terrible thing she has said, O Ameerul Mu'mineen! She is amongst the most righteous women of her tribe, in addition to this, she also has the most clothing and the most comfortable home. However, her husband is an old man." Addressing the wife, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "And what have you to say?" "He has spoken the truth," she replied. ' Hadhrat Umar (RA) got up with his whip and struck her with it saying, "O enemy of yourself! You have eaten his wealth and finished his youth and then go even further to make false allegations against him!" "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" she pleaded, "Do not be hasty. I swear by Allaah that I shall never sit in this position (as complainant against my husband) ever again."

Hadhrat Umar (RA) then instructed that she be given three garments and said, "Take this in lieu of what I have done to you (when I hit you). However, I am warning you never to complain about this old man again." The narrator says, "(I remember the incident so vividly that) it is as if I can actually see her standing up with those garments." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then turned to her husband and said, "Let not what you have seen me do to her ever provoke you to treat her badly." The husband promised that he would not and they both left. Hadhrat Umar then said, "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'The best period of my Ummah is that in which I am (the first period), followed by the second period and then the third. Thereafter, such people shall come who will take oaths before testifying and who will testify before being asked to do so. They will also be people whose marketplaces will be very noisy."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg. 307-308). Ibn Abi Shaybah has also reported the narration, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.3 Pg.315).

paras: Hadhrat Sha'bi narrates that a woman once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) saying, "I have come to complain to you about a man who is the best of all men apart from a man whose deeds are superior or whose deeds match his. He stands in salaah all night until dawn and fasts all day until evening." She was then overcome with bashfulness and said, "Excuse me, O Ameerul Mu'mineen." "May Allaah reward you tremendously," Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, 'You have certainly praised him well. You are excused." When she left, Hadhrat Ka'b bin Soor remarked, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! She has certainly been eloquent in her complaint to you." "What was her complaint?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. "Her husband," Hadhrat Ka'b replied.

Hadhrat Umar (RA) then sent for the couple and (when they arrived) said to Hadhrat Ka'b, "Now you pass judgement between them." Hadhrat Ka'b said, "How can I pass judgement when you are present?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) insisted saying, "it was you who understood what I did not." Hadhrat Ka'b then said, "Allaah has mentioned: "then marry two, three of four women with whom you are pleased (to have as your wives)." (Surah Nisaa, verse 3) You should therefore fast for three days and then not fast the next day which you will spend with your wife. You may also spend three nights in salaah and then a night with your wife." Hadhrat Umar (RA) remarked, "This (decision) I find more astounding than your first statement." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then appointed him as judge of Basrah.
sources: Ibn Jareer, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.303).

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to the lady, "Be honest with me and do not shy away from the truth." She then said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineenl I am a woman who desires what all women desire."

Hadhrat Qataadah narrates that a woman once said to Hadhrat Umar (RA), "My husband stands in salaah all night and fasts all day." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to her, "Are you instructing me to stop him from performing salaah at night and from fasting during the day?" She then went away, but returned some time later with the same complaint. Hadhrat Umar (RA) again repeated what he had said the first time. However, Hadhrat Ka'b bin Soor pointed out, "O Ameerul Mu'mineenl She has a right." "What is her right?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. Hadhrat Ka'b replied, "Allaah has permitted four wives for him, so count her as one of four. She is therefore entitled to one night in every four nights and one day in every four days." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then summoned the husband and instructed him to spend one of every four nights with her ana' to skip a fast in every four fasts.

Hadhrat Abu Gharzah (RA) once led Hadhrat Ibn Arqam by the hand to his wife and asked her, "Do you hate me." "Yes I do," she replied. "What made you do this?" Hadhrat Ibn Arqam (RA) asked. Hadhrat Abu Gharzah (RA) explained, "People have been saying too many things about me." When Hadhrat Ibn Arqam reported the matter to Hadhrat Umar (RA), the Ameerul Mu'mineen called for Hadhrat Abu Gharzah (RA) and asked, "What made you do that?" Again Hadhrat Abu Gharzah (RA) replied, "People have been saying too many things about me." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then sent for the wife. She arrived with the shrewd aunt of hers who told her, "When he questions you (about your curt statement), say, 'Because he made me say it on oath, I did not like to tell a lie.'" (When she came before him) Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "What made you say what you did?" She replied, "Because he made me say it on oath, I did not like to tell a lie." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Why not? One of you ought to lie and say something nice because every home is not built on love. Many homes are built on polite interaction stemming from social status and Islaam."

Hadhrat Abu Salamah bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf narrates that Hadhrat Aatika the daughter of Hadhrat Zaid bin Amr bin Nufayl (RA) was married to Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) the son of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). He loved her very much and even gave her an orchard on condition that she does not remarry after his death. He was struck by an arrow during the battle at Taa'if and it was forty days after the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ that the wound ruptured and he passed away. In his memory, Hadhrat Aatika (RA) recited the following couplets meant): "I swear that my eye shall always remain hot (with tears) over you and that my skin shall always be covered in dust (because I shall never adorn myself for anyone else)
(This I shall do) Forever, as long as the doves of the dense forest coo and as long as the night issues forth the bright morning"

When Hadhrat Umar (RA) proposed for her afterwards, she informed him that Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) had given her an orchard with the condition that she should not remarry after him. Hadhrat Umar (RA) advised her to acquire a verdict from someone. She then enquired from Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) whose verdict was that she was free to remarry after returning the orchard to the family of Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) then married her and invited a few Sahabah (RA) for the Waleemah meal. Amongst the guests was Hadhrat Ali (RA), who also happened to be the person with whom Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) had made a bond of brotherhood. "Permit me to have a word with her (with your new bride)," Hadhrat Ali (RA) asked Hadhrat Umar With Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s permission, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "O Aaatika!
'I swear that my eye shall always remain hot (with tears) over you and that my skin shall always be covered in dust'"
(Upon hearing this) Hadhrat Aatika (RA) started weeping very loudly. Hadhrat Umar said (to Hadhrat Ali (RA)), "May Allaah forgive you! Do not upset my wife's mood for me."
sources: Wakee, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal ' (Vol.8 Pg.302). ibn Sa'd has reported a similar narration, as quoted in isaabah (Vol.4 Pg.356).

paras: Hadhrat Nadbah the freed slave of Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA) reports that her mistress, (Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA)) once sent her to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas. When she entered the house, she found that there were two beds. When she returned to Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA), she said, "It appears to me that Ibn Abbaas has separated from his wife." Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA) then sent for Ibn Abbaas's wife who was the daughter of Sarj findi. When she asked her about it, the wife replied, "There is nothing between us. I am only menstruating." Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA) then sent a message to Hadhrat Abdullarh bin Abbaas reprimanding him, "Are you averse to the Sunnah of Rasulullaah ﷺ Rasulullaah ﷺ used to touch his wives while they were menstruating and wearing a cloth that reached up to the knees or halfway down " the thighs."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal WeA.5 Pg.138).

paras: Hadhrat ikrama says that he is not sure whether it was Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas who invited his cousin for a meal or whether it was his cousin who invited him. Nevertheless, while a slave woman was working in front of them (as they were eating), one of them called her an adulteress. "Stop that!" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) cautioned, "Even though you will not be lashed for that (slander) in this world, you will certainly be punished in the Aakhirah." The cousin said, "But what if she is as I have said?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas replied, "Verily Mlaah does not like people who are vulgar and who adopt offensive language (it is therefore inappropriate for you to make such a statement)."
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.49).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Imraan of Palestine reports that while the wife of Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas SIP was busy cleaning his hair of lice, she called for her slave woman. When the slave delayed in arriving, Hadhrat Amr (RA)'s wife called her an adulteress. "Have you seen her commit adultery?" Hadhrat Amr (RA) asked. When his wife replied that she had not, Hadhrat (RA) said, "By Allaah! On the Day of Qiyaamah, you will certainly be lashed eighty times (as punishment for slander)." His wife then spoke to the slave and asked her for forgiveness. When the slave forgave her, Hadhrat Amr (RA) remarked, "She has no option but to forgive you because she is in your control. You had rather set her free." "Will that compensate for it?" his wife asked. "Perhaps," Hadhrat Amr (RA) replied.

Hadhrat Abul Mutawakkil narrates that Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) had a Negro slave who had caused grief to the entire household because of something she had done. Raising his whip over her one day, Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) said, "Had it not been for Qisaas (on the Day of Qiyaamah), I would have beat you unconscious. However, I shall sell you to someone who pay your price in full. Go (free)! You are Allaah's."
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted Kanzul Vmmaal (Vol.5 Pg.84).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Qais or ibn Abul Qais says that he was with the delegation of Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin jarraah (RA) that received Hadhrat Umar (RA) when he arrived in Shaam. As Hadhrat Umar (RA) was travelling, he was met by some entertainers from Adhri'aat who were carrying their swords (to entertain Hadhrat Umar (RA) as he entered their town). "Hold on!" Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Stop them and send them back." "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah said, "This is the custom of the non-Arabs. If you stop them, they will think that you wish to annul the pact with them (that you wish to prevent them from freely practising their customs)." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Then leave them. Umar and his family are all under the command of Abu Ubaydah."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.384), as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.334).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar Si reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat, Zubayr (RA) once had a race, Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) beat Hadhrat Umar and cried out, "I beat you! By the Rabb of the Kabah!" when they raced a second time, Hadhrat Umar (RA) beat Hadhrat Zubayr (RA). Hadhrat Umar then called out, "I beat you! By the Rabb of the Kabah!"
sources: Muhaamili, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.334).

paras: Hadhrat Saleem bin Handhalah reports, "We once went to Hadhrat Ubay bin (RA) iliaiis to listen to Ahadeeth from him. (When he had completed) He stood up and we also stood up and walked with him. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then met him and said, "Don't you think that this (walking with people following you) is a danger (source of pride) for the one being followed and a source of dishonour for the ones following?"
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah and Khateeb in his Jaami, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.6l).

paras: Hadhrat Abul Bakhtari narrates that a man once came to Hadhrat Salmaan and said, "How pleasant was the behaviour of people today! I had been travelling and I swear by Allaah that every person I stayed with seemed to be the son of my own father. Each one of them treated me exceptionally well and was extremely kind towards me." Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) said, "My dear brother's son! That is a sign of Imaan being fresh and superb. Don't you see that when an animal is just loaded, it carries the load quickly (because it is fresh) but when the journey is prolonged, it walks in a staggered motion?" (Therefore when Imaan is continually refreshed, it is capable of doing much.)
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.8 Pg.61).

paras: Hadhrat Hayya bint Abu Hayya reports, "it was midday when a man came to my house. 'What is it you want, O servant of Allaah?' I asked. He explained, 'My friend and I have been searching for our camel and while he is still out looking, I have come here to take some shade and to have something to drink.' I got up and gave him some yoghurt to drink. I then looked at him closely and asked, 'Who are you, 0 servant of Allaah?' when he told me that his name was Abu Bakr, I asked, 'The same Abu Bakr who was the companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ and about whom I heard so much? Yes,' he replied. 1 then started mentioning to him the battles that my tribe had fought with the Banu Khath'am and all the fights we (Arabs) had been having with each other during the Period of ignorance. I then spoke of the love that Allaah had created between us (because of Islaam) and asked, 'O servant of Allaah! Until when will this status quo (of mutual love) last? 'As long as the leaders are upright,' he replied. "Who are the leaders?' I enquired. He said, 'Do you not see that every tribe has a leader whom they follow and whom they obey? it shall last as long as these people remain upright."
sources: Musaddad, Ibn Munee and Daarmi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.162).

paras: Hadhrat Haarith bin Mu'aawiya narrates that when he came to Hadhrat Umar Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "In what condition did you leave the people of Shaam?" After he had informed Hadhrat Umar (RA) about the condition of the people there, Hadhrat Umar (RA) praised Allaah and said, "Are you people perhaps socializing with the Mushrikeen?" when Hadhrat Haarith assured Hadhrat Umar (RA) that they were not, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "When you start socialising with them, you will start eating and drinking with them and your situation will remain good only when you do not do that."
sources: Ya'qoob bin Sufyaan, Bayhaqi and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.300).

paras: Hadhrat Ayaadh narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once instructed Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari to present to him all his earnings and expenditure (as governor) on a single piece of leather. Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) had a Christian accounts keeper and when he presented it, Hadhrat Umar (RA) was impressed and said, "He has an excellent memory. Will you read out a letter that has come from Shaam in the Masjid?" "He will be unable to do so," Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari said. "Why not?" Hadhrat Umar US asked, "Is he impure?" "No," Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) replied, "he is a Christian." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then reprimanded Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) and hit him on the thigh saying, "Dismiss him!" He then recited the verse: O you who have Imaan! Do not take the Jews and Christians as friends (confidantes). They are only the friends of each other (and cannot be your friends). Whoever of you befriends them, then he is surely from among them. Verily Allaah does not guide a nation of wrong-doers (who befriend the Kuffaar). (Surah Maa'idah, verse 51)
sources: Ibn Abi Haatim, as quoted in Tafseerof Ibn Katheer (Vol.2 Pg.68).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ never found fault with food ever. If he liked it, he ate and if he did not, he would leave it (without comment)."
sources: Bukhaari and Muslim, as quoted in wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.40). (5) ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal Pg.37).

paras: Hadhrat All (RA) reports that the portion Rasulullaah ﷺ liked most of a goat was the foreleg.
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ liked the foreleg of an animal. When the foreleg was once poisoned, everyone suspected that it was the Jews who poisoned it."

Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ came to visit them in their house, they slaughtered a goat in his honour. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "It seems like they knew we like meat." There is a more detailed story attached to this incident. ® Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ loved bottle gourd so when some food was served, I started searching for it (in the plate) and placing them in front of him because I knew that he loved it."
sources: Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il (Pg.12).
Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il.

paras: Hadhrat Anas giisig also narrates that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ ate food, he licked his three fingers (with which he ate).
sources: A variety of gourd called "Doodi" in Urdu.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ (was so humble that he) ate on the floor, tied the feet of goats when they were to be milked and even accepted the invitation of slaves to eat (plain) barley bread."
sources: Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il.

paras: Hadhrat Yahyaa bin Abu Katheer reports that a plate of Thareed came to Rasulullaah ﷺ every day from Hadhrat Sa'd bin ubaadah (RA). It went with him to the house of whichever wife he was with.
sources: Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il.

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when some goat's milk was milked for Rasulullaah ﷺ , he drank it and then gargled his mouth saying, "It has some stickiness (which needs to be rinsed out to preserve oral hygiene)."
sources: Ibn Najjaar, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vo!.4 Pg.44).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once stopped over at a certain place, a woman sent her son with a goat to Rasulullaah ﷺ .

Rasulullaah ﷺ milked the goat and told the boy to take it to his mother. After she had drunk to her fill, the boy brought another goat. After milking it, Rasulullaah ﷺ gave the milk to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). When the boy then brought a third goat, Rasulullaah ﷺ milked it and only this time did he drink.
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (vol.4 Pg.37).

paras: Hadhrat Ibraheem (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to keep his right hand free for acts such as eating, drinking and making wudhu. His left hand he would keep free for acts such as Istinfaa, cfeaning his nose and other such Hadhrat Ja'far bin Abdullaah bin Hakam bin Raafi says, "When Hakam once saw me eating from various parts of the plate, he said, 'Dear boyl Do not eat like that as Shaytaan eats. When Rasulullaah ﷺ ate, his fingers would not stray from his hands (they stayed in front of Mm)."
sources: Abu Nu'aym, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg,46). The author of isaabah (Vbl.l Pg.344) has commented on the chain of narrators. .

paras: Hadhrat Umar bin Abu Salamah (RA) reports, "I was once eating with Rasulullaah ﷺ when I started taking meat from all over the plate. Rasulullaah said to me, 'Eat from that which is in front of you.m you and what is nearest to you.
sources: Ibn Najjaar, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.46).

paras: Hadhrat Ummayyah bin Makhshi (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once saw a man eating without first reciting Bismillaah, When there was only a single morsel left, he lifted it to his mouth and eating it, he) recited: Rasulullaah ﷺ then laughed and said, "By Shaytaan continued eating with you until you took Allaah's name. He then vomited out everything that was in his belly." Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "...until when you took Allaah's name, he forcefully vomited out everything in his belly." Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) narrates that they were once with Rasulullaah ﷺ when a platter (of food) was brought and placed before them. When Rasulullaah held back his hand, the Sahabah (RA) did the same because they never ate until Rasulullaah ﷺ did. A Bedouin then came appearing as if he was being shoved along. As he was about to grab at the platter to eat from the food, Rasulullaah ﷺ caught hold of his hand. Just then, a little girl came also appearing as if she was being pushed along, when she also attempted to get her hand into the food, Rasulullaah ﷺ grabbed her hand as well. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "Verily people's food becomes lawful for Shaytaan when they do not take Allaah's name. When Shaytaan saw that we were holding our hands back, he brought the girl so that the food could become lawful for him (when she eats without saying Bismillaah). I however, grabbed her hand. He had also brought the Bedouin to make the food lawful for himself, but I had grabbed his hand as well. I swear by the Being besides Whom there is none worthy of worship! His hand is now in my hands; together with the hands of the two of them."
sources: Ahmad, Abu Dawood, Nasa'ee, Ibn Qaani, Tabraani, Haakim and others, as quoted in Kanzul ummaal (vol.8 Pg.45).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was eating with six others when a Bedouin came and ate all the food in two morsels. Rasulullaah remarked, "Had he recited Bismillaah, the food would have sufficed for them all. When any of you eats, he should take the name of Allaah and if he forgets, he should recite:

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Busr (RA) relates, "Nabi ﷺ once stopped over by my father, who served him a meal of Saweeq W and Hais. After Rasulullaah ﷺ had eaten, my father brought something to drink. After drinking, Rasulullaah passed the cup on to the person on his right. When eating dates, Rasulullaah ﷺ threw the stones like this." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Busr (RA) then pointed with his fmger towards his back (to indicate that Rasulullaah ﷺ threw the stones behind him). Narrating further, he says that when Rasulullaah got on his mule, his father held the reins and said, "Do make du'aa for us, O Rasulullaah ﷺ Rasulullaah ﷺ then made the following du'aa: "O Maah! Bless them in the sustenance You give them, forgive them and have mercy on them."
sources: A type of porridge prepared from barley.

paras: In another narration, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Busr (RA) says, "When my father once asked my mother to prepare some food for Rasulullaah ﷺ, she prepared some Thareed. My father then proceeded to invite Rasulullaah ﷺ for the meal and (when he arrived) Rasulullaah ﷺ placed his hand on the top of the dish saying (to the Sahabah (RA)), 'Dish out taking the name of Maah.' They then dished" out from the sides. After everyone had eaten, Rasulullaah ﷺ made the following du'aa: "O Allaah! Forgive them, have mercy on them and bless them in the sustenance You give them."
sources: A sweet dish prepared with dates, butter and flour.

paras: Hadhrat ibn A'bad reports that Hadhrat (RA) once asked, "O Ibn A'bad! Do you know what is the right of food?" "What is the right of food?" Ibn A'bad asked. Hadhrat Ali (RA) replied, "That you recite: "Luljj Ci U 411! 'I begin with the name of Allaah. O Allaah! bless us in the sustenance You give us'" Thereafter, Hadhrat Ali (RA) asked, "And do you know how to express gratitude after you have finished?" "How do you express gratitude?" Ibn A'bad asked. Hadhrat Ali US replied, "By saying: 'All praise is for Allaah Who has given us food and drink. ".
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Nu'aym.
Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi Dunya in his Du'aa, Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya and Bayhaqi, as quoted in (Vol.8 Pg.46).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "Beware of excessive and drinking because it harms the body, is the cause of many diseases and leads to lethargy in salaah. Rather be moderate in your eating and drinking because it is healthier for the body and further from extravagance. Allaah detests the obese scholar (whose makes eating a priority) and a person shall never be destroyed until he gives precedence to his desires over his Deen."
sources: Abu Nu'aym, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Mah'dhoora (RA) reports that he was once sitting with Hadhrat Umar when Hadhrat Safwaan bin Umayyah (RA) brought a platter (of food). Hadhrat Umar (RA) summoned some poor people and slaves in the vicinity and they all shared the food with him. Thereafter, Hadhrat Umar (RA) remarked, "May Allaah curse the people who are averse to their slaves eating with them." To this, Hadhrat Safwaan said, "We are not averse to them eating with us. We eat by ourselves only because we do not find sufficient good food to feed both us and them."
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.48).

paras: Hadhrat Maalik bin Anas reports that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) stopped over in Juhfah, Ibn Aamir bin Kurayz instructed his baker to take food to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA). When he brought one plate of food, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) told him to put it down. When the baker returned with another plate of food and was going to take the first plate away, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) asked, "What are you doing?" "I am taking the plate away," the baker replied. "No," said Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar "just pour the food into this other food." Thereafter, every time a different dish was served, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) made the man pour it into the other food. When the baker eventually returned to Hadhrat Ibn Aamir, he remarked, "That man must be an uncultured Bedouin!" Hadhrat Ibn Aamir corrected the baker saying, "That man is your leader. He is Ibn Umar.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya Pg.301)

paras: Hadhrat ja'farnarratesthatbecauseHadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) always ate the seeds of the pomegranate, someone asked, "O Ibn Abbaasl Why do you do that?" He explained, '" have heard that every pomegranate on earth grows from a seed from amongst the seeds from Jannah. This seed is perhaps the one."

Hadhrat Saalim says, "I was with my master Zaid bin Sowhaan when Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi passed by us after purchasing a wasaq of grain. 'O Abu Abdullaah!' Zaid called out, You are doing this (buying so much) when you are the companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) replied, The soul is at ease when it has secured its sustenance. It can then free itself for Ibaadah and Waswaas /the devil that whispers evil into the heart) loses hope in (adversely influencing) it.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.207).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi narrates that Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA) said, "I love to eat from the efforts of my own hands."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol. 1 Pg.200).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah SI once said, "I had fifteen dates so I broke my fast with five, ate Sehri with five and kept the other five to break my fast with."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.384).

paras: Hadhrat Muslim who was the freed slave of Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) says, "When Hadhrat Ali (RA) once asked for a drink, I brought him a cup of water and blew into it. He refused to drink it and returned it to me saying, "You drink it.w
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.6 Pg.237). (5) ibn Sa'd, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.37).

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla says that he was once with Hadhrat Umar when he said, "I saw Abu Qaasim (Rasulullaah) ﷺ wearing a narrow-sleeved cloak made in Shaam."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.346).

paras: Hadhrat Jundub bin Makeeth (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ wore his best clothing whenever he received a delegation and would instruct the senior Sahabah to do the same. On the day a delegation arrived from Kindah tribe, I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ wearing clothing made in Yemen and both Abu Bakr and Umar were wearing the same."
Hadhrat Salamah bin Akwa (RA) says that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA)'s loincloth always reached halfway up his calves and he would say, "Such was the garment of my beloved (Nabi) ﷺ.
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah and Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'it, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.55).

paras: Hadhrat Ash'ath bin Sulaym reports from his aunt that her uncle said, "I was walking in Madinah one day when someone behind me said, 'Lift up your loincloth because it keeps it cleaner and makes it last longer.' When I turned around, I saw that it was Rasulullaah ﷺ. 'O Rasulullaah (sagr. I said, 'it is but a simple black and white striped shawl.' Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'Do you not have an example in me?' When I looked at him, I saw that Rasulullaah ﷺ's garment reached halfway up his calves."
The Describe the Attire of Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Abu Burdah narrates that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) once took out and showed them a patched shawl and a loincloth made of coarse cloth. She then said, "It was in these two garments that the soul of Rasulullaah ﷺ was taken away."
sources: Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il (Pg.9).

paras: Hadhrat Urtimu salamah'ESSSSfc'says, "The garment Rasulullaah ﷺ loved most was his Qamees "
sources: Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il (Pg.9).

paras: Hadhrat Asmaa bint Yazeed (RA) reports that the sleeve of Rasulullaah ﷺ 's Qamees reached his wrists.
Hadhrat jaabir (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah illjl was wearing a black turban when he entered Makkah the day he conquered it.
Hadhrat Amr bin Hurayth (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once delivered a sermon wearing a black turban.
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas Si says that once (during his illness)
Rasulullaah ﷺ delivered a sermon while wearing an oily bandage.

Hadhrat Naafi reports from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin umar (RA) that when Rasulullaah ﷺ tied his turban, he would let the tails hang between his shoulders. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) also tied his turban in the same manner and a narrator called Abdullaah says that he saw Hadhrat Qaasim bin Muhammad and Hadhrat Saalim also do the same.
sources: A long, loose tailored upper garment. •(4) Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il (Pg.5).

paras: when Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) was once asked about Rasulullaah ﷺ's bedding, she replied, "it was made of leather and stuffed with the bark of a date palm."
sources: Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il (Pg.9).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) relates, "A lady from the Ansaar once visited me and saw that Rasulullaah ﷺ's bedding comprised of cloak that was double-folded. She then left and later sent a bedding stuffed with wool. When Rasulullaah ﷺ came to me, he asked, What is this, O Aa'isha?' I then informed him about the lady from the Ansaar who had seen his bedding and then sent this. Rasulullaah ﷺ told me to return it Because I liked to have it in my room, I did not return it until Rasulullaah ﷺ repeated the instruction three times. He finally said, 'Return it, O Aa'isha. I swear by Allaah that if I willed, Allaah would have made mountains of gold and silver travel with me (wherever I went).
sources: Hadhrat Hasan bin Arafah, lbn Sa'd (Vol.1 Pg.465) has reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Muhammad narrates that he once asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "what was Rasulullaah ﷺ's bedding like in your home?" She replied, "it was made of leather and stuffed with the bark of a date palm." When he then posed the same question to Hadhrat Hafsah (RA), she replied, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to sleep on a coarse sheet that we double-folded. One night I thought to myself that it would be more comfortable if I four-folded it (so I did that). The following morning, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "What did you spread down for me last night? 'It was the same bedding,' I explained, 'all that I did was to four-fold it so that it would be more comfortable for you.' Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Leave it as it was because its softness prevented me from performing salaah last night.
sources: Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il, as quoted in At Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.53). lbn Sa'd (Vol.1 Pg.465) has also reported the narration but from Hadhrat Aa'isha WSRS6.- (3) lbn Mubaarak, Tabraani, Haakim, Bayhaqi and others, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.55).

paras: Hadhrat Omar (RA) reports that he saw Rasulullaah ﷺ send for some new clothing. When it reached his collar-bone as he was putting it on, he recited: "All praise is for Allaah Who has given me clothing to conceal my private areas and with which I can look beautiful in this life." Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "I swear by the Being who controls my life! When a Muslim wears new clothing, recites these words and then purely for Allaah's pleasure gives the old clothes that he is removing to a poor person, he will remain in the care, the security and the protection of Allaah as long as there remains even a single thread of the garment left (on the poor person). This applies whether he is alive or dead. This applies whether he is alive or dead."

Hadhrat All (RA) reports that he was sitting with Rasulullaah ﷺ near (the graveyard of) Baqee on a rainy day when a woman passed by on her donkey, carrying a heavy load. As she passed through a depression in the ground, she fell off the donkey. Rasulullaah ﷺ turned his face away (so as not to see her body as it became exposed because of the fall). When someone informed Rasulullaah that the lady was wearing trousers (because of which her body did not become exposed), Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Allaah! Forgive all the women of my Ummah who wear trousers." Addressing the Sahabah (RA), Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "O people! Always wear trousers because it is amongst the most concealing of clothing. Ensure that you protect your women with it whenever they go out."
sources: Bazzaar, Uqayli, lbn Mi and others, reporting from various chains of narrators, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.55). lbn Jowzi has wrongly included this narration in his Mowdu'aat.

paras: Hadhrat Dihya bin Khalifah Kalbi (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent him as envoy to Heraclius (the Byzantine Emperor), upon his return, Rasulullaah gave Hadhrat Dihya (RA) a delicate white Egyptian cloth saying, "use a part of it to make a Qamees for you and give your wife the other portion to use as a scarf." As Hadhrat Dihya (RA) was leaving, Rasulullaah ﷺ called him back saying, "Tell her to wear something underneath (the scarf) so that it is not revealing."
sources: and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg,6l).

paras: Hadhrat Usaamah bin Zaid (RA) relates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ gave me some of the thick but delicate white Egyptian cloth that he had given Dihya. I subsequently gave it to my wife to (make something out of it to) wear. Rasulullaah ﷺ later asked me, "what is the matter? why are you not wearing the white Egyptian cloth?' When I informed Rasulullaah ﷺ that I had given it to my wife to wear, he said, 'Tell her to wear something underneath because I fear that it would reveal the shape of her bones."
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Sa'd, Ahmad, Rooyaani, Baaroodi, Tabraafti, Bayhaqi and Sa'eed bin Mansoor, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 8 Pg.62).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that when she once wore some clothing, she kept looking down at it as she walked about in the room, turning about as she did so. (Her father) Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then entered and said to her, "Don't you know that Allaah is presently not looking at you (with affection),"
sources: Ibn Mubaarak and Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya.

paras: In another narration, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "I once wore a new upper garment of mine and was very taken aback by it as I looked at it. Hadhrat Abu Bakr said to me, "What are you looking at? Allaah is not looking at you (with affection).' 'Why not?' I asked. He replied, 'Don't you know that when self-adoration enters a servant because of worldly beauty, Allaah detests the person until the beauty is lost (and the self-adoration with it).' I then took off the garment and gave it away as Sadaqah. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then said, 'That shall perhaps atone for you.

Hadhrat Abdl Azeez bin Abu Jameelah Ansaari reports that the sleeves of Hadhrat Umar's Qamees never extended past his wrists. ® Hadhrat Badeel bin Maysara reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once went for the Jumu'ah salaah wearing a cloak made in Sumbulaan. Apologising to the people (for coming late), he said, "It was this cloak that delayed me." He pulled his sleeves forward and as he let go of them, they returned to the ends of his fingers.
sources: Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.4 1 9) .

paras: Hadhrat Hishaam bin Khaalid reports that he saw Hadhrat Umar (RA) tie his loincloth above his navel.

Hadhrat Aamir bin Ubaydah Baahili narrates that when he once asked Hadhrat Anas lie about Khazz (a material in which there is a small element of silk), Hadhrat Anas (RA) replied, "I wish that Allaah had never created it. Apart from Umar and his son, all the Sahabah (RA) wore it." (Hadhrat Anas (RA) disliked it because it was a fabric worn by affluent non-Muslims)
sources: Hannaad and lbn Abi Dunya, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol .4 Pg.405),

paras: Hadhrat Masrooq narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once came out to them wearing cotton clothing. When the people stared at him, he recited a couplet (which meant): "The beauty of everything you see will never last Allaah will last when all wealth and children will be destroyed"
He then remarked, "By Allaah! compared to the Aakhirah, this world is just a leap of a

Hadhrat Abu Abdullaah who was the freed slave of Hadhrat Shaddaad bin Haad says, "It was on a Friday that I once saw Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) standing on the pulpit wearing a shawl made in Kufa and a coarse loincloth made in Aden that was worth a mere four or five Dirhams. He was a thin, handsome man with a long beard.
sources: Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.96). Tabraani has reported a similar narration from reliable sources, as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.80).

paras: Hadhrat Moosa bin Talha says, "Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) used to lean on a staff (as he came to the Masjid) on Fridays. He was one of the most handsome men wearing his cream-coloured loincloth and shawl as he came to the pulpit and sat on it."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.80) has commented on the chain o' narrators. (6) lbn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.58).

paras: Hadhrat SulaymAbuAamirsays,"lsaw Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) wearing a Yemeni shawl worth a hundred Dirhams."

Hadhrat Muhammad bin Rabee'ah bin Haarith says, "The Sahabah (RA) used to spend generously on such clothing for their wives that was both beautiful as well as concealing. I once saw Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) wearing a shawl edged with silk that was worth two hundred Dirhams. He said, This belongs to (my wife) Naa'ilah. I had given it to her to wear and am wearing it now only to make her happy."
sources: Ahmad in his Zuhd, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.3 Pg.8). (2) ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg. 131).

paras: Hadhrat Zaid bin Wahab narrates that a delegation from Basrah once came to see Hadhrat Ali (RA). Amongst them was a man belonging to the whose name was Ja'd bin Na'Ja. when he started criticising Hadhrat Ali Hugh's clothing, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "What problem have you got with my clothing when it is far away from pride and a most appropriate example for the people to follow."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol. 1 Pg,3Q2).

paras: Hadhrat Amr bin Qais reports that when someone asked Hadhrat Ali (RA) why he patched his Qamees, he replied, "The heart humbles with it and the Mu'min is able to follow the example,"
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.l Pg,302). lbn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.175) has reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Ataa Abu Muhammad says, "I once saw Hadhrat Ali (RA) wearing an unwashed Qamees made of extremely coarse cloth,"
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.l Pg.302).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Hudhayl reports, "I once saw on Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib a Qamees made in Ray which was such that when he stretched out his arms, the sleeves reached the ends of his fingers and when he retracted them, they reached close to halfway up his forearms."

Whenever Hadhrat Ali (RA) wore a Qamees, he would pull the sleeve until it reached his fingers. He would then cut off what was extra (extending further than the fingers) saying, "The sleeves should never extend further than the hands."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.4 Pg.34l).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Azdi who was one of the Imaams of the Azd tribe reports that he once saw Hadhrat Ali (RA) come to the marketplace and say, "Who has a good Qamees for three Dirhams?" When one of the traders said that he had one, Hadhrat Ali (RA) went to him and liked the Qamees very much. "This must be worth more (than three Dirhams)!" Hadhrat Ali (RA) remarked (thinking that the man was reducing the price because Hadhrat Ali (RA) was the Ameerul Mu'mineen). "Not at all," the man replied, "that is really the price." Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed says that he then saw Hadhrat Ali (RA) untie a knot in his clothing containing some Dirhams and giving it to the trader. Hadhrat Ali (RA) then wore the Qamees, which happened extend past the ends of his fingers. By his instruction, the excess that extended past his fingers was, then cut off. A freed slave of Hadhrat Abu Udhayn reports that he once saw Hadhrat Ali (RA) come out of his house and approach cloth merchant saying, "Do you have a Qamees made in Sumbulaan?" The man took out one and when Hadhrat Ali wore it, it reached halfway down his calves. Looking down to his right and left, Hadhrat Ali (RA) remarked, "I have not seen a better fit. How much is this?" "Four Dirhams, O Ameerul Mu'mineen," the man replied. Hadhrat Ali SSi then untied the money from his loincloth, handed it over to the man and then left.
Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ibraheem says, "I saw Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) wearing a shawl or a suit of clothing worth four or five hundred Dirhams."

Hadhrat Qur'ah relates that when he saw Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) wearing coarse and stiff clothing, he approached him saying, "O Abu Abdur Rahmaan! I have brought you soft clothing made in Khurasaan and it would give me great pleasure to see you wearing them because your clothing is extremely coarse and stiff." "Show it to me so that I may see it for myself," Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar said. Feeling it with his hand, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar asked, "Is this silk?" "No, it is cotton," Hadhrat Qur'ah assured him. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) however said, "I fear wearing this because I fear becoming a boastful snob. Verily Allaah detests the boastful snob."
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Hubaysh relates that he saw Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar wearing two cloths made by the Ma'aafir (a tribe in Yemen), which reached halfway down his calves.

Hadhrat Waqdaan reports that he once heard a person asking Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar SSI "What clothing should I wear?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar replied, "Clothing that will neither cause foolish people to ridicule you nor cause intelligent people to criticise you (for being extravagant)." "What type of clothing is that?" the man asked. "What costs between five and ten Dirhams," came the reply.

Hadhrat Abu Is'haaq reports that he saw Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar illi wear his loincloth halfway down his calves. In another narration, he mentions that he saw several Sahabah (RA) such as Hadhrat Usaamah bin Zaid il Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA), Hadhrat Baraa bin Aazib (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar all wearing their loincloths halfway down their calves.
Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Abu Sulaymaan reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas once purchased and wore a garment worth a thousand Dirhams.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.32l).

paras: Hadhrat Katheer bin Ubayd narrates that when he once went to Ummul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) she told him to wait until she completed stitching her old garment. As he waited, he remarked, "O Ummul Mu'mineen! If I went out and informed the people about this, they would regard it as miserliness from your side that you are too miserly to buy new clothes)." Hadhrat Aa'isha said, "Do as you see fit. The person who does not wear old clothes does not deserve new clothes (and may not have them in the Aakhirah)."
sources: Bukhaari in his Adah (Pg.68). (3) ibn Sa"d (VoL Pg.73). (4) ibn Sa'd (Vol.8 Pg.252).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed reports that when someone entered Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA)'s room as she was stitching her old garment, he remarked, "O Ummul Mu'mineen! Has Allaah not granted an abundance of wealth (to buy new clothing rather than patch old clothing)?" Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) replied, "Leave us alone! The person who does not wear old clothes does not deserve new clothes." when Hadhrat Mundhir bin Zubayr (RA) arrived from Iraq, (his mother) Hadhrat Asmaa bint Abu Bakr (RA) had already become blind. He sent for her delicate and exquisite garments made in Marw and Quw and when she felt it, she exclaimed, "Alas! Send this clothing back to him." Hadhrat Mundhir (RA) felt hurt about it and said, "Dear mother! The garments are not transparent." She replied, "Even though they are not transparent, they are revealing." When he then bought for her common garments made in Marw and Quw, she accepted them saying, "It is these types of garments that you should give me to wear."
sources: Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vols).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a woman once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) saying, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! My upper garment is all tattered." "Have I not given you anything to wear?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. "You have given me," she replied, "but it has torn," Hadhrat Umar (RA) immediately sent for an exquisite upper garment and some thread to be given to her. He then said to her, "Wear that (old clothing) when you are making bread and cooking and then wear this (new garment) once you have finished. Those not wearing old clothing do not deserve new clothes."

Hadhrat Kharasha bin Hurr reports that he was once looking at Hadhrat Umar as a youngsten passed by, wearing his loincloth below his ankles and dragging it along as he walked. Hadhrat Umar (RA) called for him. and asked, "Are you menstruating?" "What! O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" asked the youngster in surprise "Do men also menstruate. Hadhrat umar (RA) replied, "Then what is the matter with you hanging your garment below your ankles?" Hadhrat Umar then sent" for a knife, gathered the end of the loincloth and cut off whatever hung beneath the ankles." Hadhrat Kharasha says, "it is as if I can still see the threads dangling over his heels."
sources: Abu Dharr Harawi in his Jaami and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal '(VoL.8 Pg.58).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports that they were in Azerbaijan under the command of Hadhrat Utba bin Farqad (RA) when a letter from Hadhrat Umar arrived. The letter read: "Ensure that you wear your loincloths, shawls and shoes and throw away your socks and trousers. Make sure that you adopt the attire of your forefather Ismaa'eel and stay away from lives of luxury and the attire of the non-Arabs. Remain in the sun because it is the bath of the Arab. Dress simply like Ma'd bin Adnaan, live tough lives, wear old clothes, mount your animals without stirrups, do target practice and jump directly onto your horses (from the ground). Remember that Rasulullaah (Sell forbade (men from) wearing silk unless it be only this much. Rasulullaah ﷺ then indicated with his middle finger."

Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Muhammad ﷺ says that they were sitting in a gathering between the pulpit and the grave of Rasulullaah ﷺ . In the gathering was Hadhrat Imraan bin Abu Anas and Hadhrat Ataa Khuraasaani was saying, "I saw that the rooms of Rasulullaah ﷺ wives were made from the trunks of palm trees and their doors were simply veils made from black (animal) hairs. I was also present when the letter of (the king) Waleed bin Abdil Malik was read out, giving instructions for the rooms of Rasulullaah ﷺ's wives to be included within the Masjid. I have never seen more people weeping than I did that day. On that day, I heard Sa'eed bin Musayyib say, 'By I wish that they would leave the rooms as they are so that future generations of Madman's people and people coming from other lands could see with how little Rasulullaah sufficed in his life. This would then cause people to abstain from amassing wealth and from boasting about worldly commodities." Hadhrat Mu'aadh relates further that when Hadhrat Ataa Khuraasaani had completed his narration, Hadhrat imraan bin Abu Anas said, "There were four rooms made from unbaked bricks with courtyards of palm trunks while the other five were made of plastered palm trunks with no courtyards at aft. Their doors were simple veils made from black (animal) hair. When I measured the veils, I found that they were three arm's lengths in height and more than an arm's length in width. As for the weeping that you mentioned, I can recall myself sitting in a gathering with a group of the Sahabah ii children. Amongst them was Abu Salamah bin Abdur Rahmaan, Abu Umaamah bin Sahl bin Hunayf and Khaarijah bin Zaid. They wept so much that their beards were wet. Abu Umaamah was the ( 1 ) sufyaan bin Uyaynah in his Jaami, as quoted in, Kanzul Ummaal (Vc;.a Pg.5.9). one who remarked, 'If only they had preserved the rooms without demolishing them so that seeing them) people would reduce their building endeavours and see what Allaah preferred for His Nabi ﷺ even though He possessed the keys to the treasures of the world."
